scaled, mirrored, clipped anew, inverted) opened with AUDIT finding no error, AutoCAD reading back the corner, sides and
boundary the library gives.

**CHANGED.** An IMAGE or a WIPEOUT read from a file is a `DxfRasterImage` or a `DxfWipeout`, not a `DxfUnknownEntity`:
it is moved where it was refused (`NotSupportedException`), so a drawing holding one is inserted by
`DxfDatabase.Insert` with a placing, and an INSERT of a block with a wipeout under its words explodes with the wipeout
placed, where it was left out. Its `GetGeometry` and `GeometricExtents` give its boundary where they gave nothing and
threw, so `UpdateExt` takes it into the extents, and an image appended or moved grows the extents of the header as any
entity does: the picture 40 by 30 copied to (1010, 1020) beside a line to (1, 1) makes `Extmax` (1050, 1050, 0), and
moved 5 000 along x (6050, 1050, 0). `IntersectWith` crosses its frame or its boundary, and the actions of a dynamic
block and its turn-only entities take an image or a wipeout where they refused it as a type kept as it was. `DxfReader` reads none of them, as before.

## 13.8.0 (2026-11-04)

A minor release: one public member is added, `PackOptions.StartCorner`, and none is removed or renamed in any of the
four libraries. `SheetPacker` can fill each sheet from any corner of its usable area, the packing the mirror image of
the one from the upper left, which stays the default and the same to the bit. The checklist of what AutoCAD reads
records four more points looked at in the AutoCAD 2021 editor (25, 31, 38 and 40); no code changed for them.

**NEW.** `PackOptions.StartCorner`: `SheetPacker` fills each sheet from the corner of its usable area given,
`UpperLeft` (the default, as before), `UpperRight`, `LowerLeft` or `LowerRight`. The first block goes into that corner
and the rows run from its side, laid from its edge; a group laid out afresh puts its main view at that corner of its
block, and a group kept as drawn is mirrored as one block, its boxes as they stood. The packing is the mirror image of
the one from the upper left, so the sheets taken and how full they are do not change: from the lower right, three
boxes 100 by 50 on a usable area 267 by 190 put two in the bottom row, the first at the right, and the third above
the first. `SheetCorner.Center` is refused. From the upper left every result is the same to the bit as before (a
thousand boxes in 200 groups on A1, hashed), and as fast, about 5 ms. Tested by 60 scenes packed from each corner
against the mirror of the upper left's, and the packing promises checked from every corner (40 scenes each).

## 13.7.0 (2026-11-04)

A minor release: one public member is added, `DxfDatabase.PatternSearchPath`, and none is removed or renamed in any of
the four libraries. Of its eight entries, 3 NEW, 4 FIXED and 1 CHANGED, one is a fix to the queries of solids and the
rest are DXF, each checked against what AutoCAD 2021 reads, writes or draws. Where a point, a ray, a segment or a line
stands against a solid far out is worked out near the origin, as its booleans and its measures are: of 18 000 such
probes beside bodies ten million to a thousand million out, 67 answers are wrong where 209 were, and within a million of
the origin nothing changed, to the bit. The big font of a text style is read from `FontSearchPath` and its letters
measured beside the style's SHX font as AutoCAD draws them: all 6 910 letters beside AutoCAD's ten CJK big fonts are
boxed as AutoCAD boxes them, and 15 382 of 15 450 TEXTs in styles with a big font give AutoCAD's place and box. An
MTEXT of several lines is laid out in the fonts found as AutoCAD lays it out, its paragraphs wrapped at its width, its
lines spaced and its TEXTs exploded where the font puts them: of AutoCAD's rounds of paragraphs, widths, spacing and
attachments, 1 604 of 1 650 come out as it gives them, and of its breaks, its first and following lines and its codes
and CJK letters, all 1 492, 9 550 and 789. The checklist of what AutoCAD reads was held against AutoCAD 2021 once more
and 23 of its points settled against it: a drawing of R2000 reads and writes more than ten custom properties as AutoCAD
does, and a block given an attribute definition is marked as one (`HasAttributeDefinitions`), so that AutoCAD fills and
explodes its attributes. `DxfDatabase.PatternSearchPath` names the folders of the caller's own hatch pattern files, and
a HATCH given a predefined pattern is given its lines from there: every pattern of AutoCAD 2021's acad.pat and
acadiso.pat, at three scales and angles, gives AutoCAD's own lines, 918 of 918, and the library carries no pattern of
AutoCAD's. Callers will see results change: where its fonts are measured, an MTEXT of one line spaced exactly is its
height and a third high, as AutoCAD makes it, and one whose words wrap is measured where it kept the file's sizes; a
block made in code holding an attribute definition writes flag 2 in its BLOCK. Reading a one-line `ActualWidth` with
fonts takes 2.5 microseconds more, and far out the first question of a body takes 2 to 14 microseconds to move it into
the frame. Empty, as a drawing is opened or made, `FontSearchPath` and `PatternSearchPath` read nothing and change
nothing, to the byte.

**NEW.** `DxfDatabase.PatternSearchPath` gives a drawing the folders of the caller's own hatch pattern files, separated
by semicolons and searched in their order, as `FontSearchPath` gives it the folders of its fonts (check P4c, point 34). A
HATCH given a pattern by `SetHatchPattern` is then given its lines from there as AutoCAD 2021 gives them: from acadiso.pat
in a drawing of millimetres and acad.pat in one of inches (`Measurement`), or from a file named after the pattern, a
pattern of AutoCAD's file looked for in the drawing's file first and a custom one in its own file first, the type it is
written as that of the file it is found in; each line turned by `PatternAngle` and scaled by `PatternScale` about the
origin of the plane, and written anew when either is set, so that `Explode()` and `GetHatchLinesData()` draw it. ANSI31 of
acadiso.pat on a square 30 by 20 holds its one line at 45 degrees, offset (-2.245, 2.245), and explodes to 11 LINEs. A
HATCH made in code is given its lines when it is added to the drawing, and one read from a file keeps what the file holds.
A file is read as AutoCAD reads one, comments, blank lines and the blanks about numbers passed over, and a pattern
AutoCAD refuses is refused (a line of fewer than five numbers or more than six dashes, or a number it cannot read); a
pattern not found is left with no lines, as before, said once at Debug, and a malformed file never throws. Every pattern
of AutoCAD 2021's acad.pat and acadiso.pat, at three scales and angles (918 hatches), gives AutoCAD's own lines to 1E-13,
and on squares off the origin AutoCAD draws the library's HATCH, and `Explode()` breaks it, into AutoCAD's own 84 034
LINEs; AUDIT finds nothing to fix. The library carries no pattern of AutoCAD's. Empty, as a drawing is opened or made,
nothing is read and every drawing is written as before, to the byte.

**FIXED.** A block given an attribute definition by `DxfBlockTableRecord.AppendEntity` is marked as one of attribute
definitions (flag 2 of its BLOCK, `HasAttributeDefinitions`), as AutoCAD 2021 marks one, constant or not and model space
too, and the mark is kept when the definition is erased, as AutoCAD keeps it (check P4b, point 61). Without it AutoCAD
2021 took a block made in code for one of no attribute: the value B7 a multileader of the library gave the block's MARK
it did not find, and its EXPLODE gave the block's INSERT no ATTRIB; with it, AutoCAD's EXPLODE and `Explode` give the
INSERT of MARK=B7, as the library's `Explode` does. A block read from a file says what its file says.

**FIXED.** `DxfDatabase.SummaryInfo` of a drawing of R2000 reads every custom property of its DWGPROPS AutoCAD 2021
saved, and writes more than ten as AutoCAD does, where it read ten and refused an eleventh (check P4b, point 26).
AutoCAD writes the first ten in the groups 300 to 309, their count after the base of the hyperlinks, then each after the
tenth in a group 300 of its own: twelve end `90 12`, `300 P8=v8`, `300 P9=v9`. AutoCAD 2021 read its own such save as
twelve, of which the library read ten, and read the library's drawing of twelve as twelve, AUDIT finding nothing. A drawing
of ten or fewer is written as before, to the byte.

**NEW.** An MTEXT of several lines is laid out in the fonts `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` finds, as AutoCAD 2021 lays it
out (check F4): its paragraphs (`\P`) wrapped at its width, its `ActualWidth` and `ActualHeight`, its `GeometricExtents`,
and the TEXTs `Explode` and a drawing of R12 give of it, a TEXT for each run of letters of one look of each line where
the font puts it. A line breaks after the spaces between words and before or after a Chinese, Japanese or Korean letter,
but not before a comma, a full stop or a closing bracket, nor after an opening one; a word moves down where the pen at
it and its own ink would reach the width (romans.shx "H H t" 4 high fits 17.91, not 17.9, though inked 17.524 wide), and
a word longer than the width stays whole on a line of its own. Spaced at least, each line stands the top of the line
before, a third of its height and a third of the MTEXT's height below it, so that "ABC\P{\H3x;g}\PDEF" of txt.shx 4 high
is 28 high; spaced exactly, the MTEXT is its height, the spacing and a third of its height high, whatever its letters.
The codes `\T` (not of a TrueType font), `\A`, `\L`, `\O`, `\K`, `\C` and `\~` are measured with `\W` and `\H`; slanted
letters (`\Q`), other fonts (`\f`), stacks (`\S`) and indents and tabs (`\p`) are not. Against AutoCAD 2021, of 14 750
MTEXTs of five rounds in txt, romans, simplex, isocp and gdt.shx, arial and times.ttf and txt.shx beside gbcbig.shx,
extfont.shx and whgtxt.shx, 14 234 are measured: 14 204 give AutoCAD's `ActualWidth` and `ActualHeight`, 14 205 its
extents, and 14 082 those and every exploded TEXT's words and place. Of the other 152, 103 explode with %% codes, where
AutoCAD's own TEXTs do not follow its lines, 27 are of isocp.shx, up to 0.01 off in height as its MTEXTs of one line were,
and 22 hold letters at the middle of taller ones, wrap where their height changes or line a run at a line's end. With an
empty `FontSearchPath` nothing changes, to the byte, on .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8. No public member is added;
`DxfMText.GeometricExtents` is overridden.

**CHANGED.** Where its fonts are measured, an MTEXT of one line spaced exactly is as high as AutoCAD 2021 makes it, its
height and a third ("ABC" of txt.shx 4 high is 5.333 high, not 4), and one whose words wrap, or that holds `\T`, `\A`,
`\L`, `\O`, `\K`, `\C` or `\~`, is measured where it kept the file's 42 and 43. A multileader's words of one line holding
`\T`, `\A`, `\K`, `\C` or `\~` are landed by their width too. Reading an MTEXT's `ActualWidth` of one line takes about
2.5 microseconds more a call with fonts, 13.8 where it took 11.3 for txt.shx on .NET Framework 4.8; nothing changes
without fonts.

**NEW.** The big font of a text style (`DxfTextStyleTableRecord.BigFontFileName`) is read from
`DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` and its letters measured beside the style's SHX font as AutoCAD 2021 draws them (check F3):
TEXT, ATTRIB and ATTDEF places and extents, one-line MTEXT `ActualWidth` and `ActualHeight`, multileaders landed on the
right and attribute definitions in flips. A letter is read in the code page AutoCAD gives the big font's name (GBK for
gbcbig.shx, Big5 for chineset.shx, Shift-JIS for bigfont, extfont, extfont2 and @extfont2.shx, Korean for the four
wh*.shx); a letter of two bytes the big font has is drawn from it before the style's font, but °, ± and ∅; a space is the
big font's where it has one; a height above of nought is 8. "A中B" of txt.shx and gbcbig.shx 4 high, centred on
(100, 50), stands at (95.211, 50) as in AutoCAD. Of 691 letters beside each of AutoCAD's ten CJK big fonts, read in
place, all 6 910 are boxed as AutoCAD boxes them, and of the TEXTs in styles with a big font, 15 382 measured give
AutoCAD's place and box and 68 do not, 64 of them as off without a big font. A big font of another name, or named with
its folder, which AutoCAD reads in no code page, is measured for ASCII only; on .NET the code pages need
`CodePagesEncodingProvider` registered. No public member is added; with an empty `FontSearchPath` nothing changes, to the
byte.

**FIXED.** Beside a big font that is read, a TEXT stands at its bottom on the big font's depth (gbcbig.shx 32 up at 4
high), where it was left where it stood; spaces are the big font's (txt.shx and extfont.shx "A B" 4 high 9.067 wide, not
10.667); a TrueType style's big font, which AutoCAD does not draw, no longer leaves its TEXTs at their bottom unplaced;
and a font of shapes beside a big font, which AutoCAD inks otherwise, is no longer measured. Of check F1a's 5 400 TEXTs of
txt.shx and gbcbig.shx, 3 692 gave AutoCAD's place and box and 1 168 did not; 5 156 do, 4 do not (txt's "i" aligned, as
without a big font), and the 240 of `\M+` codes, which AutoCAD draws by their two bytes, are left unmeasured.

**FIXED.** Where a point, a ray, a segment or a line stands against a solid far out is worked out near the origin, as
its booleans and its measures are (check GR2e): `Locate`, `Contains`, `DistanceTo`, `SignedDistanceTo`,
`GetClosestPointOnBoundary` and `GetShortestLineTo` of a point, and `CollidesWith`, `DistanceTo`, `GetIntersections` and
`GetShortestLineTo` of a ray, a segment and a line, on `GeoSolid3`, on the shapes asked of it and in `Containment3`,
`Distance3`, `Projection3`, `Collision3` and `Intersection3`, move a body reaching more than 2^20 out and more than 1 024
times the size of its box into the frame of the booleans, once, keeping the moved body, and the probe with it; what has a
place comes back moved exactly. `GeoPreparedSolid3` prepares such a body again in the frame the first time it is asked
where a point, a ray or a line stands, and keeps `Material`, `Surface`, `Index` and its questions of another body where
the body stands. Where it stood, its openings were cut and its faces read within a trillionth of the coordinates: of 636
points half a thousandth in and out from a plate 200 by 100 by 3 a thousand million out, with two openings up from its
floor whose ceilings stood 0.0009 apart, 12 had another nearest point than at the origin, and of the segments and lines
from them 32 and 67 of 1 908 other crossings, none now; of 2 080 rays from an L 100 by 80 by 50 with a pocket and a hole
a hundred million out at a hundredth, 9 had other crossings, and 48 asked of its prepared form, 1 and 1 now, and of 2 016
a thousand million out 19 and 52, none now. Of 18 000 points, rays, segments and lines beside
bodies with and without openings, turned about in space, ten million to a thousand million out, against the same body
moved back to the origin exactly, wrong answers at a hundredth, a thousandth and, to a hundred million out, a millionth
209 -> 67, and 1 284 -> 9 of probes the tolerance itself off a face; those left are crossings of rays starting on or
half the tolerance off a face. Within a million of the origin, and below the frame's tolerance, nothing changed, to the
bit, and no boolean, cut, measure, section or cell far out moved: what they ask of a body they ask where they work. The
ray fuzz of check G1e, rays beside turned boxes, U's, cylinders, cones and rings 0 to 1E9 out at nought, a thousandth
and a hundredth, was wrong nowhere in 360 000 before and is wrong nowhere in 180 000 now. Far out, the first question of
a body moves it into the frame, 2 to 14 microseconds for a U, a cylinder, a slab with a duct and a plate with two
openings, and a prepared body is prepared once more at its first such question; after that each question takes as long
as before, and near the origin nothing takes longer.

## 13.6.0 (2026-11-03)

A minor release: no public member is added, removed or renamed in any of the four libraries. Its six entries, 4 FIXED
and 2 CHANGED, are fixes to solids and the meshing of faces and speed in the Clipper2 carried compiled in. The cut of a
solid's openings, the material its volume, area, centroid and mass are read from, a section of it and its cells are
worked out near the origin where it stands far out, as its booleans are since 13.5.0: of 617 prisms with openings ten
million to a thousand million out, 8 answers are wrong at a thousandth where 745 were, and within a million of the
origin nothing changed, to the bit. The cut of openings whose walls stand a fraction of the tolerance apart no longer
leaves a sheet inside the material: of 4 500 prisms with two or three such openings, 576 areas were wrong at a hundredth
and at a thousandth, and 2 are. `GeoFace3.TriangulateSurface` covers what the face covers, to rounding, where its
corners stand within the tolerance of edges they are not on: of 48 904 such faces, 45 307 areas wrong at a hundredth, a
thousandth or a millionth are right, and none that was right moved. A union, a common part or a difference welded
closed takes, of the corners that move the volume by nothing but rounding, the one tilting the faces round the others
least, where it took the first met: a cube of 100 and a block running 0.001 into its top held 1.39 less than the two
less their overlap and holds 0.39 less, and of 210 797 booleans of the gate corpora 5 that were wrong are right and
none is made wrong. Clipper2 unites shapes it joins one after another, and builds polytrees of many holes, without
slowing with the square of their number: 50 000 squares standing on a strip took 9.8 seconds in Clipper2 on .NET 10 and
take 0.3, and 20 000 teeth each with a hole and an island took 33 seconds to unite into a polytree and take 0.44; of
80 000 sets of random paths, no answer moves by a bit. Callers will see results change where they were wrong: the
volumes, areas, sections and cells of bodies far out, the areas of cut openings, the triangles of faces with corners
near other edges and the corner a weld takes. Far out, those queries take 4 to 12 per cent longer at a thousandth and a
hundredth; 13 booleans ten million to a thousand million out, asked below the far frame's gate, that were right come
out wrong, and one plate a thousand million out whose cut keeps sheets 0.00018 thick holds 0.057 too much read as the
triangles in its faces.

**FIXED.** `GeoFace3.TriangulateSurface` covers what the face covers, to rounding, where its corners stand within the
tolerance of edges they are not on (check GR2d). Such a face is cut into strips, and the corners of each of its rings
were read within the tolerance first: corners closer than it were merged and corners within a hundredth of it of a
straight run dropped. The wall of an opening 50 by 1.50015, with corners at 1.5 up both its sides where the ceiling of
another opening 0.00015 lower met it, had those corners merged, one kept on each side, and was meshed 0.00375 short at a
hundredth and at a thousandth; a plate 100 by 30 with a step 0.0005 high in its top and a notch 0.0002 wide in its bottom
was meshed 0.013 short, the step flattened and the notch closed. The plate 200 by 100 by 3 of check GR2c, the ceilings of
its two openings 0.00015 apart, held 0.175 too much read as the triangles lying in its faces (`VolumeMethod.Surface`,
which `GetMassProperties` sums), where fans held it as it is; it holds what it holds now, and a hundred million out too.
A thousand million out, where its cut keeps a sheet 0.00015 by 100, it held 0.33 too much and holds 0.2 too much: the
side of the sheet standing as a face of its own is a seam at the tolerance with no triangle. The corners are read within
rounding; a loop thinner than the tolerance is still a seam at it with no triangle, as the side of a slab thinner than
the tolerance is. Where the clipping is left with a needle of a face, every ear of it blocked by corners within rounding
of its sides, the face is cut into strips too, where the needle was dropped: a plate 81.43 by 17.44 with a hole
0.0000016 above its bottom was meshed 0.000066 short at a millionth. Of
48 904 faces with steps, pairs of corners, notches, spikes and dents 1E-6 to 0.02 across, holes apart from, near and
touching each other and the boundary, turned about in space and up to a thousand out, 24 622 areas wrong at a hundredth,
20 293 at a thousandth and 392 at a millionth are right, and none that was right moved; what is left are triangles of a
ten-millionth of a square unit or less whose middles stand outside by the rounding, where holes touch on faces turned
about in space, as before. Of the GR2c area fuzz, 4 500 cuts near the origin read so, 396 wrong at a hundredth and 227
at a thousandth are right, and none is wrong; of 4 500 ten million to a thousand million out, 385 and 217 are right, and
the cuts themselves are the same to the bit. One plate a thousand million out, whose cut keeps sheets 0.00018 thick,
now holds 0.057 too much where it held what it holds: its sheets are seams at the tolerance and have no triangle on the
side where they stand alone, and the faces beside them, whose corners were merged and lost about as much, no longer
make up for it. Of 288 000 seeds of the mesh fuzz, none moved.

**FIXED.** The cut of a solid's openings no longer leaves a sheet inside the material where walls of two openings stand
a fraction of the tolerance apart (check GR2c). The cut parts the body by the planes of each opening, and between two
such planes leaves cells thinner than the global tolerance; the gluing lays each face out in its plane within that
tolerance however fine the work, so the face of such a cell, a strip, came to nothing there: it shared nothing with the
face against it, nothing was taken from it, and the strip and the part of that face against it stayed, a sheet bounding
no material. The volume held; the area did not. An L 100 by 80 by 50 at the origin with an opening up from its floor and
one down from its top whose far walls stood 0.0009 apart, the openings given down first, kept a sheet 0.0009 by 13 and
measured 0.0234 too much; a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00015 apart
kept one 0.00015 by 100 and measured 0.03 too much, at a hundredth, a thousandth and a millionth alike. A strip still
lying against a face once the gluing has taken what it could is now read again with that face, both laid out within the
tolerance of the work, and what they share goes from both. Of 4 500 prisms with two or three openings whose walls stood
1E-5 to 0.002 apart, within a thousand of the origin, turned about in space or not, 576 areas were wrong at a hundredth
and at a thousandth and 579 at a millionth, and 2, 2 and none are, both a thousand out with walls 1.1E-5 and 1.35E-5
apart and smaller than they were; none that was right moved. A plate 300 by 200 by 12 turned about in space, with twelve
openings 22 by 22 a row of which stood the tolerance off the walls of the others, kept sheets in 23 of 69 cuts at a
thousandth, and 5 of those held 0.024 to 1.46 too little; each holds and measures what it should now. Of the other 190
corpus sets, a union lost its sheet and 344 volumes moved in their last bits, every verdict kept. The booleans glue
their cells the same way: of 25 200 unions, common parts and differences of such prisms and boxes, at nought to a
hundredth, 3 at the origin that were not worked out are right now, and none that was right moved by more than 4.5E-5.
More than a million out a strip is read so only within a tolerance eight times what rounding can move a corner off a
plane there: a boolean asked below the far frame's gate is worked out where the bodies stand, and read so there, 13 ten
million to a thousand million out that were right came out wrong. The cut of a body that far out is worked out a 256th
of its reach from the origin, and of 3 600 cuts of such prisms ten million to a thousand million out, 76 areas wrong at
a hundredth and at a thousandth and 104 at a millionth are 5, 5 and 59, none that was right moved; the plate with
ceilings apart a thousand million out keeps its sheet, its strips too thin to be laid flat 3.9E6 out. Read as the
triangles lying in its faces (`VolumeMethod.Surface`, which `GetMassProperties` sums), the plate with ceilings apart
held 0.175 too much, where fans held it as it is, the triangles of a wall whose corners stood closer than the tolerance
along a side leaving a sliver of it out; see the entry above.

**FIXED.** The cut of a solid's openings, the material its volume, area, centroid and mass are read from, a section of it
and its cells are worked out near the origin where it stands far out, as its booleans are since 13.5.0 (check GR2b):
`TryCutOpenings`, `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume`, `GetSurfaceArea`, `GetCentroid`, `GetMassProperties`, `Section` and
`Mesh3.ToCells` move a body reaching more than 2^20 out and more than 1 024 times the size of its box by whole
coordinates, with its openings, a section's plane or a grid's origin, work it out there, and move the material, the
section or the cells back; a corner kept comes back as it was given, to the bit. Where it stood, walls of openings a
fraction of the tolerance apart were cut in one plane: an L 100 by 80 by 50 a thousand million out, with an opening up
from its floor and one down from its top whose far walls stood 0.0009 apart, measured 153 732.16 within a thousandth,
where it holds 153 731.64, and its cells held 0.52 too much; a plate 200 by 100 by 3 a hundred million out, with two
openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00015 apart, measured 0.525 too much, and a section through the deeper
one cut 0.0105 too much. Each holds what it holds now, to 1.3E-4. Of 617 prisms with two or three such openings ten
million to a thousand million out, each asked its volume, whether that can be trusted, its area, its centroid, its cut,
two sections and its cells along the world's axes and its own, wrong answers at a thousandth 745 -> 8, at a hundredth
853 -> 8, and at a millionth, up to a hundred million out, 73 -> 8; one area that was right is 0.0027 over. Within a
million of the origin, and below the gate's tolerance, nothing changed, to the bit: 47 493 query fuzz lines, 191 corpus
sets, 4 bnear runs and the benchmarks; the booleans are as they were, far out too, in 16 800 fuzz lines, but for the
volume read of a result far out that keeps openings. Such queries far out take 4 to 12 % longer at a thousandth and a
hundredth, and 10 to 13 % less at a millionth; near the origin they take as long as before.

**CHANGED.** Clipper2, which GeometryHelper carries compiled in, builds a polytree of many holes in one path, or of
shapes joined one after another, without slowing with the square of their number, and unites squares in a row into
paths in half the time. Each hole was looked for in the path round it by walking all that path's points, after walking
up the chain of the emptied paths of the shapes joined before its own; each new output path walked the owners of all
the paths to its left before taking the nearest as its own, to make sure it did not own it already; and each path
joined into an older one walked that one's owners the same way. Points are found against a path of 64 points or more
through its crossings with their line now, sorted along it and kept for a line asked for again, those near the point
worked out exactly; the chain is shortened as it is walked; a new path, which owns none, is not looked for; and while
every path is owned by an older one or none, no path is looked for among the owners of an older one. 20 000 teeth
standing on a strip, each with a hole and an island, took 33 seconds to unite into a polytree on .NET 10 and 40 on .NET
Framework: 0.44 and 0.49 now. 100 000 squares of side 10 in a row took 20 and 24 seconds: 0.5 now. 1 000 000 in a row
took 9.7 and 10.0 seconds to unite into paths: 4.4 and 4.7. GeometryHelper's own operations take Clipper2's answers as
paths, so they gain only where Clipper2 alone does, on rows far longer: `Boolean2.Union` of 100 000 squares in a row
takes 1.8 and 1.5 seconds as it did. Small clips take as long as they did, into paths or polytrees, and the other
shapes timed, polytrees of paths of 64 to 4 096 points round 10 to 4 000 small holes among them, to within 3 %. Of
80 000 sets of random paths, combs, zigzags, rows of squares, lattices and strips, each united, cut, intersected and
xored under every fill rule into paths and polytrees, or offset and combined by the library, none moves by a bit, nor
of 20 000 with lines made for every path of three points or more at the first point asked. Of 10 000 of them, with the
crossings near a point judged by their doubles alone, 18 nest a polytree otherwise; without the path's edges along
the line and vertices on it, 197; and with the emptied paths that others split off passed over as well, 72. With no
path looked for among the owners of an older one whatever the owners, the sweep of a set of random paths never ends.
The benchmarks sign as they did.

**CHANGED.** Uniting shapes that Clipper2 joins into one path one after another, squares standing on a strip or in a
row, no longer slows with the square of their number. An output path joined into another kept that path as its owner,
so the paths joined one after another made a chain, and every horizontal segment of the answer walked it from the path
its point was first added to. The walk now points each path it passes at the end of the chain, as the find of a
union-find does, but stops at a path that others split off, which a polytree reads its owners from. 50 000 squares of
side 10 standing on a strip took 10.6 seconds to unite with `Boolean2.Union` on .NET 10 and 10.0 on .NET Framework, 9.8
and 9.4 of them in Clipper2: 1.1 and 0.8 now, 0.3 in Clipper2. 1 000 000 squares of side 10 in a row took 18.6 seconds
in Clipper2 alone, and 9.5 now. Of 80 000 sets of random paths, combs, zigzags, rows of squares, lattices and strips,
each united, cut, intersected and xored under every fill rule into paths and polytrees, or offset and combined by the
library, none moves by a bit; with the walk passing the paths split off as well, 48 of 20 000 sets nest a polytree
otherwise, holes coming out at its top as outer paths. The benchmarks sign as they did.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part or a difference welded closed no longer tilts a face to take one corner to another
that moves the volume by nothing but rounding as well (check GR4). Where the corner the weld took moves the volume by
no more than the rounding of the coordinates times the area the group is weighed by, as corners part way along
straight edges do, whose triangles weigh nothing, the others of the group that move it as little are alike to it; of
those it takes the one tilting the faces round the others least now, then the one moving the volume least, then the
first met, where it took the first met. A corner moving the volume more is taken as before. A cube of 100 and a block
40 by 30 running exactly 0.001 into its top, turned and joined within a thousandth, had two corners 0.0003 apart part
way along the edges of faces of 10 000 square millimetres, weighing 3.3E-18 and 2.1E-17 cubic millimetres; the weld
took the one standing on the other's face to that other, 0.0003 off its own face, and the union held 1.39 less than
the two less their overlap, where the tolerance times the area where they meet is 1.2. It holds 0.39 less now. The
cube came out so turned as .NET 10 turns it, whose cosine of the angle is a bit off .NET Framework 4.8's, and closed as
it was turned as .NET Framework turns it; given the same bodies, the two work them alike, to the bit. Of 210 797
booleans of the gate corpora 346 come out otherwise: 5 that were wrong are right, and none is made wrong. Of 25 200
booleans fuzzed, 17 differ in their bits and none in its class, and of 24 000 of bodies with openings, 2. They take as
long as they did.

## 13.5.0 (2026-11-03)

A minor release: one public member is added, `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath`, and none is removed or renamed in any of the
four libraries. Of its 30 entries, 2 NEW, 16 FIXED and 12 CHANGED, all but three are DXF, each checked against what
AutoCAD 2021 reads, writes or works out; the three are fixes to the booleans of solids. `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath`
names the folders the SHX and TrueType fonts of a drawing's text styles are read from, so that its words are measured as
AutoCAD 2021 measures them: TEXTs placed and boxed, one-line MTEXTs sized, multileaders landed, attribute definitions
flipped and leaders' hooks exploded; empty, as every drawing is opened and made, nothing is read and nothing changes. A
common part and a difference leave out an opening of a body whose material the result does not keep where it shares no
space with the other body: a spiral girder less a spiral ramp holding a spiral tube as an opening, which came apart into
640 222 cells in 202 seconds on .NET 10 and was not worked out, is cut in 1.6. The booleans of solids far out, as at
national-grid coordinates, are worked out near the origin: of 1 196 ten million to a thousand million out, 14 are wrong
at a thousandth where 241 were, and within a million of the origin nothing changed, to the bit. A boolean not worked out
where a body is cracked a hair wide is worked out once more on the bodies welded: of 45 000 booleans of a cracked U and
a box, 1 619 differences, 2 106 common parts and 2 063 unions not worked out are right now, none was made wrong, and
every boolean worked out as the bodies came is as it was, to the bit. Callers will see results change: words given to a
multileader put the base point of its content where a leader from the left meets them, turned words turn its plane, and
mirrored words are moved and kept upright as AutoCAD moves them; a new multileader is of words (`ContentType`
`MTextContent`), its leaders run on to its words (`ExtendLeaderToText`) and words made in code make its `TextColor`
BYLAYER where it was BYBLOCK; `RemoveFirstVertex` and `RemoveLastVertex` take a leader line down to one vertex;
`HandOverTo` keeping the extension dictionary refuses the contexts of another kind of entity; `HasContext` is false on
an object that is never annotative; `AddContext` names a scale's entry `*A1` and on; a table writes its reals with their
point and keeps each row's looks with the row; `Normal` keeps the points and turn of a TEXT, ATTDEF, ATTRIB, INSERT or
SOLID in its plane; an annotative copy added to another drawing keeps its contexts; and with `FontSearchPath` given, a
TEXT justified other than left on its baseline is put about its second point. Far out, booleans at a thousandth and a
hundredth take 17 to 26 per cent longer; one worked out again takes 1.4 to 2.5 ms longer for such a U and box under .NET
Framework 4.8 than refusing it took; a hundred copies with contexts into another drawing take 185 ms where they took 165
on .NET Framework 4.8; and a clear of 0 of a table of 400 rows takes 9 ms there, where 13.4.0 took 22.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part or a difference that is not worked out is worked out once more where either body
closes within the tolerance and not at the rounding of its coordinates, as a body cracked a hair wide does (check GR3):
each such body has its corners within the tolerance of each other made one and its faces lying in one plane merged,
and the boolean is worked out on what that gives, by the same checks, in the frame it is worked out in. A crack
slanting across a plane of the other body within a few thousandths left the cut a gap at the plane wider than it
bridges, and the cell could not be judged: a cracked box dipping 0.088 into an arm of a cracked U, the cracks 1.7E-5
wide and slanting 0.004 either side of the planes of the other, less the U, was not worked out, and leaves 475.54 now,
as it should; the two share 2.55 and join into 3 143.38, neither worked out before. Of 45 000 booleans of such a U and a
box, both cracked 1E-5 to 1E-4 wide, at a thousandth, a hundredth and 0.05, 1 619 differences, 2 106 common parts and
2 063 unions not worked out are right now, and none was made wrong; of 18 000 booleans of prisms of other shapes, 3
more are right. Every boolean worked out as the bodies came is as it was, to the bit, and so is every one still not
worked out. A boolean worked out as the bodies came takes as long as it did; one worked out again takes 1.4 to 2.5
milliseconds longer for such a U and box under .NET Framework 4.8, a quarter to two thirds more than refusing it took,
and the 9 000 booleans of a cracked set 16 % longer in all.

**FIXED.** Words given to a multileader put the base point of its content (10 of the context data) where AutoCAD 2021 puts
it (check D38b): where a leader from the left would meet them, the gap short of the place given and as far below as the left
is met, which needs no font: "ABC" 4 high given at (100, 50), met at the middle of the top line, put it at (98, 48), where the
library put it at the words. AutoCAD lands a leader it adds to the library's file there and leaves the words, where it moved
them: "Ag" of Arial on a multileader of txt.shx stays at (100, 49.92), a leader from the left landed at (90, 47.33), where
AutoCAD moved them to (102, 52.59) and landed it at (92, 50). Of 25 of the library's files given a leader in AutoCAD, with
the fonts on `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath`, the words stayed in all 25; with an empty path, AutoCAD still moves words whose
place needs their font (their depth, or their width where they are held at the top centre or right). Words held at their top
centre or right have their left edge at the place given and line the content up so (176, bits 14 and 26), as AutoCAD puts
them, and are met by leaders from their edges, where the fonts measure them; words given anew where no leader is landed
take the base point with them; words given after the leaders move to meet the first, (10, 2) for a line landed at (0, 0).

**FIXED.** Words turned in code turn the multileader's plane with them where no leader is landed yet, as AutoCAD 2021 turns
it (check D38b): "ABC" turned half round make its x axis (-1, 0, 0), the base point at (102, 52), and a leader from (250, 0)
is landed at (110, 52) along -x, from (0, 0) at (79.33, 52) where the fonts measure them; a dogleg of 15 moves them to
(107, 50). Turned 30 degrees or a quarter alike. The library kept the plane and landed every leader at the words.

**FIXED.** Words mirrored so that they would read upside down are kept upright, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them, where
`DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` measures them (check D38b): across the XZ plane "ABC" at (100, 50) met from (0, 0) stands at
(100, -46) running along x, met again at its attachment by the mirrored leader at (90, -48), where the library turned it
half round at (110.67, -50). Of the two ways to read them, the one kept is the one turned nearer the turn they had, which
gives AutoCAD's way in 54 of 55 mirrors of words tried, across planes in and off the floor, of words turned first or not;
the 55th, words turned 135 degrees mirrored across XZ, is as near both ways and AutoCAD's choice there is left.

**FIXED.** Small readings and writings of a multileader, as AutoCAD 2021 makes them (check D38b): a leader line given
BYBLOCK writes its flag and no 92; `GetLeaderLineColor` of a line of no colour of its own is BYBLOCK, whatever
`LeaderLineColor` it is drawn in; `TextAlignmentType` is read from the context's 176, the right for words lined up on the
left and mirrored across YZ; a block whose plane a mirror turns back says so (294 of 1, then of nought); a new multileader
writes no 295 before R2013; a multileader of no content is of words (`ContentType` `MTextContent`, 172 of 2, `HasContent`
false), and its first leader line is landed at its point, the line of that one vertex. Words of no leader meet the base
point again when they are scaled or the left's attachment is set, and are met 5.33 below their top at attachment 8 where
their ink reaches 1.33 below the baseline.

**CHANGED.** `new DxfMLeader().ContentType` is `MTextContent` (was `NoneContent`), and setting it to `MTextContent` on a
multileader of no words is a no-op where it threw. The base point of the content of words given is no longer their place;
`TextLocation` read on a multileader of no words gives that base point, as before.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part and a difference of solids far out, and each cut of `TrySubtractAll`, are worked out
near the origin (check GR2): bodies reaching more than 2^20 out and more than 1 024 times the size of their box, as at
national-grid coordinates, are moved by whole coordinates, with their openings, until the least corner of their box
stands a 256th of their reach from the origin, worked out there and moved back; a corner kept comes back as it was
given, to the bit. A corner was read on a plane within a trillionth of the coordinates, a thousandth a thousand million
out, and walls of openings a fraction of the tolerance apart were cut in one plane: an L 100 by 80 by 50 a hundred
million out, with two blind openings whose walls stood 0.0009 apart, less a box across both walls, held 130 189.39
within a thousandth, where it holds 130 189.32, and the box less the L 28 457.23, where it holds 28 457.68; they hold
it now, to 3E-5 a thousand million out. Of 1 196 such booleans of prisms with openings and boxes ten million to a
thousand million out, wrong at a thousandth 241 -> 14, at a hundredth 413 -> 15, at a millionth 257 -> 127 and not
worked out 134 -> 49; 3 of 1 200 with a face of the box near a wall's plane, each exactly the tolerance off, came out
otherwise by up to 1.9. Within a million of the origin, and below a trillionth of the coordinates a 256th of the reach
out, nothing changed, to the bit: 12 852 fuzz lines, 191 corpus sets and 4 bnear runs. Such booleans at a thousandth and
a hundredth take 17-26 % longer, at a millionth a third less. `GetVolume`, `TryCutOpenings`, `Section` and
`Mesh3.ToCells` of bodies far out are not moved yet.

**FIXED.** A multileader's words mirrored across their plane, which run against its x axis and say so (294 of 1, as AutoCAD
2021 writes them), are moved as AutoCAD moves them when the dogleg, the gap, the height, the scale, an attachment, the words
or a leader's last vertex are set (check D38): held at their right and their up the other way, "ABC" of txt.shx held at
(110.67, 50) and met from the left stands at (117.67, 50) for a dogleg of 15, where it stayed at (110.67, 50), at
(113.67, 50) for a gap of 5, and at (126.67, 53) 10 high, its left edge kept at 100. Met on the right or on both sides, they
keep the right's landing, and a leader added on their right is landed the gap past them. What needs their width (the
height, the scale, words given anew) is done where `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` measures them; the rest with no font too.
The words the library keeps readable on a mirror now write 294 as AutoCAD does.

**FIXED.** Words given to a multileader in a text style other than its own are moved to where its font would meet them, as
AutoCAD 2021 moves them, where `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` measures both (check D38), so that a leader added is landed by the
multileader's font: "Ag" of arial.ttf 4 high given at (100, 50) to a multileader of txt.shx stand at (100, 49.92), a leader
from the left landed at (90, 47.33) and one from the right at (116.46, 47.33), where they were met at 47.41. SHX and
TrueType alike, given in memory or once the multileader is added. With an empty path nothing changes.

**CHANGED.** A new multileader writes what AutoCAD 2021 writes for one (check D38): its leaders run on to its content
(`ExtendLeaderToText` true, 295 of 1) in a drawing of R2013 or later; a leader line added has no colour of its own (no 92),
drawn in `LeaderLineColor` as before; words given set bit 18 of the overrides, and their colour becomes its `TextColor` (92,
and 90 of its MTEXT), with bit 15 but for BYBLOCK, so that words made in code, BYLAYER, make the text colour BYLAYER where it
was BYBLOCK, and `MText` read back carries a colour of the index or true. A mirror that turns the plane's x axis back (across
the YZ plane), of a block or of words kept readable, sets bit 14 and lines the content up the other way (176 of the context
data, 2 for 0 and 0 for 2). AutoCAD 2021 read 53 of 62 of the library's files of these as it made its own; of round 1's
119 cases, 103 now give AutoCAD's places, vertices and groups, none before.

**NEW.** `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath` reads TrueType fonts too (.ttf, .ttc, .otf of glyf outlines), so that the words of a
style of one are measured as AutoCAD 2021 measures them (check F2) where F1b measured those of an SHX font: TEXT, ATTRIB and
ATTDEF places, aligned and fitted heights and widths and `GeometricExtents`, the `ActualWidth` and `ActualHeight` of an MTEXT
of one line, multileaders met on the right, attribute definitions flipped and leaders' hooks exploded. A text's height is the
top of the font's A, no pair of letters is kerned, a TEXT is boxed from the start of its baseline to its last pen, each
letter as high as it is from the baseline and a space a unit below it, a TEXT at its bottom stands on the font's
usWinDescent, and %%c is the font's U+2205, else its U+00D8: "ABC" of arial.ttf 4 high centred on (100, 50) stands at
(94.259, 50). A style that names a typeface is measured where its file is that face, as AutoCAD draws it, and a collection
by its first face where the style names it. Measured against AutoCAD 2021 on the fonts of Windows read in place: 30 840 of
31 200 TEXTs, 436 of 445 MTEXTs, 280 of 288 multileaders, 142 of 144 flipped attribute definitions and 20 of 20 leaders of
check F2, and 14 400 of 14 460 TEXTs, 152 of 153 MTEXTs and 18 of 18 multileaders of F1a's; the rest are %%c of fonts
Windows links to others (Tahoma, Malgun Gothic, SimSun), which draw it from them, and Calibri's degree sign. Fonts of CFF
outlines and of symbols, a letter the font has not, `%%k`, a change of width or height within an MTEXT, and a style whose
typeface, bold or italic is not its file's are not measured; a style named by its typeface alone is not looked up. Nothing
changes with an empty path.

**FIXED.** A common part of two solids, and a difference, leave out an opening of a body whose material the result does
not keep, either body of the common part or the one taken away, where it shares no space with the other (check GR1): its
box further from the other's box than the tolerance, or the opening and the other both closed, their faces further apart
than twice the tolerance and no corner of either inside the other. A spiral girder less a spiral ramp holding a spiral
tube as an opening, 80 under the girder's top all along it, the tube's box and the girder's both reaching round the half
turn, came apart into 640 222 cells in 202 seconds on .NET 10 and 704 on .NET Framework 4.8 and was not worked out, the
tube cut into the ramp; with the tube left out it is cut into 18 345 in 1.6 and 2.7 seconds and holds what slicing
gives, 10 044 789 407.964 cubic millimetres. Their common part and the take-off of the two, the girder ranked under the
ramp, are cut into the 18 345 cells of the ramp without the tube, where they took 29 681. The openings of either body of
a union, and of the body a difference takes material from, are cut in as before.

**NEW.** `DxfDatabase.FontSearchPath`: folders, separated by semicolons and searched in their order, where the SHX fonts of
the drawing's text styles are read from, so that the words of the drawing are measured as AutoCAD 2021 measures them (checks
F1a and F1b). Empty, as every drawing is opened and made, nothing is read and nothing changes. Fonts of shapes 1.0 and 1.1
and unifonts are read as AutoCAD reads them, where ezdxf reads them otherwise: a shape within a unifont numbered big-endian,
the pen put down marking its point, the angles of an arc of fractions whole degrees, the octants of an arc of a sign and a
size, and an arc boxed by its chord and height up to half a turn and by its circle beyond. Measured against AutoCAD 2021 on
its own fonts (txt, romans, simplex, isocp, gdt, complex, bold, times.shx, read in place): 1 798 of 1 814 letters to 1E-6
of a unit, 21 596 of 21 600 TEXTs of every justification placed and boxed to 1E-9, 170 one-line MTEXTs of 170 measured, 196
of 196 multileaders of SHX words landed, and 90 of 90 attribute definitions and attributes flipped. The results follow the
fonts given and differ between machines and versions of a font. TrueType fonts, big fonts' letters and fonts of shapes in
an MTEXT are not measured; a font not found is said once at Debug, and a file found that is no font once at Warn, and
nothing throws.

**CHANGED.** With `FontSearchPath` given: a TEXT, ATTRIB or ATTDEF justified other than left on its baseline is put about
its second point when its words, second point, height, width factor, turn, justification or style are set, and when one
made in code is added, an aligned one given its height and a fitted one its width factor ("ABC" of txt.shx 4 high centred on
(100, 50) at (94.667, 50)), and its `GeometricExtents` are its words' ink; `DxfMText.ActualWidth` and `ActualHeight` of an
MTEXT of one line are measured; a multileader lands a leader on the right of its words, meets words reaching below their
baseline lower ("Ag" 2.67 below its top at the middle of its top line, where it met 2), moves words met on the right when
their height, the scale or the words change, and keeps mirrored words readable; a flip takes a locked attribute definition,
kept readable as AutoCAD flips it ("L1" 5 high at (20, 60) about x = 45 at (63.33, 60)), where it was refused; and a leader
whose words sit above its line explodes with its hook running on to their end.

**CHANGED.** `DxfMLeader.RemoveFirstVertex` and `RemoveLastVertex` take a leader line down to one vertex, as AutoCAD 2021
does, where the library kept two (check D37). The line from (0, 0, 0) to the words "ABC" at (100, 50, 0) is left (90, 48,
0) by the first, written as a line of no vertex of its own under its landed leader and drawn as its dogleg alone, and
(0, 0, 0) by the last, its dogleg drawn on to (8, 0, 0), the words left where they are. The one vertex is kept
(`InvalidOperationException`): AutoCAD crashed taking it out of a drawing it had read.

**CHANGED.** `DxfMLeader.RemoveLastVertex` refuses the last vertex of a leader of two lines or more
(`InvalidOperationException`), the landing every line of the leader ends at, as AutoCAD 2021 refuses it (eInvalidContext),
where the library moved the landing for them all (check D37). With no dogleg drawn it writes the vertex before the last as
the leader's point, as AutoCAD does: the line from (-10, -10, 0) through (0, 0, 0) to its landing is landed at (0, 0, 0),
its last vertex then read (8, 0, 0), where the library wrote the point (-8, 0, 0).

**FIXED.** A `TransformBy` that scales a `DxfMLeader`, by 2 or by 0.5, turned or mirrored too, marks its scale as its own
(bit 24 of its overrides, `90`), as AutoCAD 2021 marks it (check D37, D31e c3-k-transform2-blockscale1); a move, a turn
or a mirror alone does not, as before.

**FIXED.** `DxfTable` writes the reals it gives a table with their point, as AutoCAD 2021 writes every real of a table
(check D37, D33 to D33g): a row `InsertRows` puts in 9 high is `141 9.0` and a column `InsertColumns` puts in 20 wide `142
20.0`, where the library wrote `141 9` and `142 20`; so are the heights and widths `SetRowHeight`, `SetColumnWidth` and
`SetSize` give, the sizes and text heights `TransformBy` scales, a cell's text height (`140 7.0`), its double (`140
12.0`), its block's scale and its turn. Numbers that are not whole are written as before.

**FIXED.** `HasContext` answers false for an object that is never annotative, as a LINE, a CIRCLE or a layer, whatever
context records it holds, as AutoCAD 2021 answered for eleven kinds of entity handed a TEXT's contexts by `HandOverTo`
(check D37), where the library read the records as its contexts. The records are kept, as before.

**FIXED.** `HandOverTo` keeping the extension dictionary refuses one of contexts of another kind of entity with
`ArgumentException`, before anything is written, where it wrote a drawing AutoCAD 2021 crashed reading (check D35e). A TEXT
of contexts handed over to an MTEXT left the MTEXT the TEXT's records, and AutoCAD stopped with a FATAL access violation on
the drawing; it crashed as well on a TEXT of an MTEXT's or an INSERT's records and on an INSERT of a TEXT's. A TEXT, an
ATTDEF and an ATTRIB still take one another's contexts and a LINE any, as AutoCAD read them; not keeping the dictionary,
the new entity writes contexts of its own, as before.

**CHANGED.** `DxfObjectContextCollection.AddContext` names the entry of a scale `*A1`, `*A2` and on, as AutoCAD 2021
names it, where the library gave the first of `A0`, `A1` and on the list had not: one more than the highest number the
list has or was given while the drawing is open, so that Z4 added once Z3 (`*A3`) is taken out is `*A4` (check D35e).
AutoCAD's own scales, named A0 to B6, are read as before, and AutoCAD read the library's `*A` names beside them.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable` keeps the looks of each row with the row while the drawing is open, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them in
its ROWTABLEFORMAT, the table's own looks of a kind those of its first row of that kind (check D33g, D33f a04, a07, a09).
A row `InsertRows` or `SetSize` puts in keeps none: `ClearTableStyleOverrides(2)` writes its cells `91 0`, where the
library gave them the table's own looks of the data, and a row put in at 0 later leaves it none. A row
`InsertRowsAndInherit` puts in keeps the looks of the row whose look it takes. A cell of a column `InsertColumns` or
`SetSize` puts in takes the looks of its row: none in a row put in, GH_TXT, red, 9 and top left in the row of data that a
row put in at 0 took them from, and the looks of its kind in a title or header moved out of its place (`170 5` and `140
6.0` for the title). Where `DeleteRows` or `SetSize` takes out the first row of data, the table's own looks of the data
are those of the next row of data: the row put in at 0 taken out again writes them back in the table's head as they were
(`93 6886016`), and B-12 taken out after a row put in after it takes them away (`93 2101760`).

**CHANGED.** A title or header moved out of its place writes its kind's text height as AutoCAD 2021 writes it, `140 6.0`
for the title of AutoCAD's Standard, where the library wrote `140 6` (check D33g).

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.RemoveAllOverrides` keeps in a cell of a row of the title's or the header's kind out of its place
the looks of its kind, whether the table shows its title and header or not, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33f, D33e n07): a
row put in taking the title's look (`InsertRowsAndInherit(3, 0, 1)`), the title shown, keeps `170 5` and `140 6.0`, and
one taking the header's look `170 5`, where the library took them away. It read the kinds of the rows only where the
table left its title or header out, since reading them at every cell made the overrides of 397 cells taken away one by
one twice as slow; they are now read once for each writing of the TABLECONTENT.

**CHANGED.** A row of data keeps the table's own looks of the data that a row put in before the first row of data takes
from the table, while the drawing is open, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them with the row (check D33f a01 to a14, D33e n05):
`ClearTableStyleOverrides(2)` and `RemoveAllOverrides` give B-12 and M12 of the table of its own data looks, given a row
at 0, back GH_TXT, red, 9 and top left, after a second row at 0, the row put in taken out again or B-12 given a height of
5, where the library took them away. A clear of 0 or 1 takes them from the rows with the table's own. A drawing read
again holds no such row, as AutoCAD reads a file the library wrote.

**FIXED.** `DxfTable.ClearTableStyleOverrides` of 0 or 2 is as fast again as before it read the kinds of the rows (check
D33f): a clear of 0 of a table of 400 rows and 3 columns takes 9 ms on .NET Framework 4.8 and 5 on .NET 10, where 13.4.0
took 22 and 21, and the library before check D33e 8 and 4. The TABLECONTENT is looked through for rows of the title's or
the header's style, and read whole only where it holds more of them than the table shows, once for each writing of it; a
table's extension dictionary is found without reading its whole record. A table that holds such a row, as one given a
row before its title, still reads it whole once: 24 ms on .NET Framework 4.8.

**CHANGED.** `Normal` set on a TEXT, ATTDEF, ATTRIB, INSERT or SOLID writes the normal alone, its points, turn and contexts
kept in its plane, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them and as the library already kept an annotative INSERT's (check D35d): a TEXT at
(11, 12, 0) turned 0.3 given the normal (0, 0.6, 0.8) stands at (-11, -9.6, 7.2), still turned 0.3, an INSERT at (300, 100,
0) at (-300, -80, 60), and a SOLID's corner (200, 10) at (-200, -8, 6), where the library kept each where it stood in the
world. An INSERT's ATTRIBs are still carried with it. `DxfMText.Normal` keeps the location and makes the MTEXT read along
the x axis of the new plane, turned nought, as an annotative one did already: turned 30 degrees and given (0, 0.6, 0.8), it
reads along (-1, 0, 0), where the library kept its turn. LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE and HATCH were
already as AutoCAD; a DIMENSION is not, and is left as it was. The library's own arrows of leaders and multileaders are
placed as before.

**CHANGED.** An annotative copy added to another drawing, by `AppendEntity`, `WblockCloneObjects` or `Insert`, keeps its
contexts and those of its ATTRIBs, as AutoCAD 2021's `WblockCloneObjects` and `Insert` keep them (check D35d), where the
library left them and gave the copy the placing it was read at. Each stands on that drawing's scale of its scale's name
where the two give the same scale; a scale the list has not is added to it; one of the name of other units is added as the
name and `_1`: a TEXT of S7 of 1:3 copied into a drawing whose S7 is 1:7 stands on an S7_1 of 1:3. The block of an
annotative INSERT comes annotative, where it came not, and the definitions in a block a copy brings keep their contexts. A
drawing older than R2007 takes the copy as before. With contexts to write, a copy into another drawing of a drawing of 35
entities takes 185 ms for a hundred where it took 165 on .NET Framework 4.8; a drawing of 555 entities is within noise.

**FIXED.** An attribute or definition of letters of another width made of several lines (`IsMTextAttribute`,
`IsMTextAttributeDefinition`) keeps its width factor (41), its MTEXT's words opening with it, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them
(check D35d): 0.7 wide, its MTEXT reads `\W0.7000;` and the value, where the library took the width factor out.

**FIXED.** `HandOverTo` writes the contexts of a copy that carries them, as `AppendEntity` writes them, where the old
entity's extension dictionary is not kept, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them (check D35d): a LINE handed over to the copy of a
TEXT shown at (11, 12) 1.25 high at 1:1 is that TEXT so, where the library left it at its record, (40, 12) 2.5 high. Kept,
the old entity's dictionary stands for the copy's. The old entity's extended data kept, where it has none, leaves the new
entity its own, its AcadAnnotative among it, where the library took that away.

## 13.4.0 (2026-11-02)

A minor release: no public member is added, removed or renamed in any of the four libraries. Of its 43 entries, 1 NEW, 7
FIXED and 35 CHANGED, all but one are DXF, each checked against what AutoCAD 2021 reads, writes or works out; the one is
a fix in GeometryHelper.IfcConvert. Annotative texts, attributes, MTEXTs and INSERTs are read where AutoCAD 2021 shows
them and written there, tables merge, clear, reset, fill and copy as it does, multileaders keep their blocks' landings
and land their leaders as it does, and splines fit by its SqrtChord and Uniform parameters too and are cut into
polylines as it cuts them. Callers will see results change: an annotative TEXT, ATTRIB, ATTDEF, MTEXT or INSERT with
contexts reads its place, turn and height from its context of 1:1, else its default, whatever CANNOSCALE says, its
setters write that context, an INSERT's `ScaleFactors` setter writes every context by its scale, and a copy keeps its
original's contexts; an attribute made of several lines is held by the top of its MTEXT; a multileader's `BlockScale`
and `BlockRotation` set, even to the value they have, move the block to be met at the base point and land its leaders
anew, `BlockRotation` reads the multileader's own turn (43), `TransformBy` leaves the block's own scale and turn as they
are, and a leader added by `AddLeader` has no landing until its line is given a vertex; the first edit of a `DxfTable`
merges the rows AutoCAD merges on load, `ClearTableStyleOverrides` keeps the title and header left out, `ResetValue`
takes a cell's looks away with its value and empties a block cell where it threw, a `Fill` with `CopyContent` or a
`CopyFrom` from a cell emptied in the session leaves its target as it was, and a `Fill` above its source repeats it from
the far end; a spline read as the cubic through its fit points gives that cubic's `Degree`, `ControlPoints` and `Knots`,
and `ToPolylineWithPrecision` cuts a spline not periodic evenly where that gives more pieces. `Clone` of plain DXF
entities is some 15 to 20 per cent slower, and a clear of 0 or 2 of a table of 400 rows takes 20 ms on .NET Framework
4.8 where it took 8. In GeometryHelper.IfcConvert, `IfcStoreCache` opened on several threads at once as a process's
first use of xBIM no longer throws on some of them.

**CHANGED.** A copy (`Clone`, `GetTransformedCopy`) of an annotative text, attribute, MTEXT or INSERT keeps the contexts of
its original, and an INSERT's copy those of its ATTRIBs, as AutoCAD 2021's copy keeps them (check D35c): in no file it is
shown at its original's scales (`HasContext`) and reads where its original is read; appended to its original's drawing it
is given an extension dictionary of those contexts, as AutoCAD writes its copy's, where it was given the placing alone and
no contexts; appended to another drawing it is placed where it is read, as before. `TransformBy` of a copy moves every
context, and so does `GetTransformedCopy` of an MTEXT or an INSERT; that of a TEXT, ATTDEF or ATTRIB moves the context it
is shown at alone, and its record's point and angle only where that context is the default, as AutoCAD 2021 moves it:
moved by (10, 5), the TEXT shown at (11, 12) at 1:1 beside its default of 1:2 at (40, 12) is shown at (21, 17), its
context of 1:2 left at (40, 12). `WblockCloneObjects` into the same drawing, and the anonymous blocks of a dynamic block,
copy contexts so too. AutoCAD 2021 read nine drawings the library wrote, copies among them, as the library reads them.
`Clone` of plain entities takes about 0.2 us more an entity, some 15 to 20 per cent; of entities of ezdxf's sample it is
three times as fast as before.

**CHANGED.** An annotative MTEXT's `SetAttachmentMovingLocation` moves it by the width of the context it is read at and
writes that context, and its record where that context is the default, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it (check D35c): the MTEXT
read at (14, 44) at 1:1, 30 wide and held by its middle, held by its middle left stands at (1.01, 36.5). Its `Normal` set
makes it read along the x axis of the new plane, written into that context: turned 30 degrees and given the normal (0, 0.6,
0.8), it reads along (-1, 0, 0). An annotative INSERT's `Normal` set writes the normal alone, its points left in their
plane, and its `BlockTransform` set writes the context it is read at, and its record where that is the default, as its
point, angle and scale factors are; other contexts are left as they are.

**CHANGED.** An attribute made of several lines by `IsMTextAttribute` or `IsMTextAttributeDefinition`, left, centred or
right on its baseline, is held by the top left, centre or right of its MTEXT one text height above its point, or its second
point where it is not left, whatever the font, as AutoCAD 2021 makes it (check D35c): B-12 2.5 high at (50, 59) becomes the
MTEXT held by its top left at (50, 61.5), where the library held it by its bottom left at (50, 59). The text's first point
is kept, where the library made it the MTEXT's location. Existing test changed:
`DxfAttributeReferenceTests.AnAttribOfOneLineMadeOfSeveral_HoldsItsWordsWhereTheyStand_ItsCodesWrittenAsCodes`.

**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of an MTEXT stretches its box (46) with its upright in no columns too, as AutoCAD 2021 scales
it (check D35c): scaled by 2, an MTEXT in a box 20 high is in one 40 high, where the library left 20.

**CHANGED.** An ATTRIB in a block that is not annotative is annotative where its own AcadAnnotative says 1 and it holds a
context, as AutoCAD 2021 read the attribute it made of an annotative definition in such a block (check D35c); flagged 1
and holding none, it is not.

**CHANGED.** An annotative MTEXT or INSERT with contexts is read where AutoCAD 2021 shows it once it has read the drawing,
as a text has been since check D35 (check D35b): at its context of the scale 1:1, else its default. An MTEXT's `Location`,
`Direction`, `Rotation`, `Width`, `Height` (its box) and `Attachment` are that context's own, and its `TextHeight` the
record's times the default's scale over 1:1's: one whose record says (10, 40), 40 wide, and whose context of 1:1 says (14,
44) turned 30 degrees and 30 wide, reads so. An INSERT's `Position`, `Rotation`, `ScaleFactors` and so `BlockTransform`
are its context's: the valve of AutoCAD's sample Mechanical - Metric given a context of 1:1 at (113.883, 279.776) turned
45 degrees and scaled by 2 stands there, as AutoCAD read it. Setting those writes the context shown, and the record where
that context is the default; an INSERT's `ScaleFactors` write every context by its scale, 3 at 1:1 being 6 at 1:2, as
AutoCAD wrote them; `TransformBy` carries every context. An annotative attribute made of several lines writes its MTEXT
into every context, and `TransformBy` carries it; its `MTextAttribute` is the shown context's. An annotative text's
`HorizontalMode` and `Justify` are its context's. A copy (`Clone`, `GetTransformedCopy`) of an annotative text, MTEXT or
INSERT of contexts reads where its original is shown. Of 532
lines AutoCAD gave, 337 read apart before and 47 now. Reading an MTEXT of no contexts takes about 30 ns more a property,
1 to 5 per cent; an INSERT of none reads as fast as before.

**CHANGED.** An ATTRIB is annotative as its INSERT is, whatever its own AcadAnnotative says, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: the
attribute ATT_DVSUP of AutoCAD's sample, flagged 0, is annotative in its annotative valve. An INSERT of a dynamic block is
annotative as the dynamic block is where its anonymous block is not. An INSERT of an annotative block, or an attribute of
one, that holds no context is shown at 1:1 (`HasContext`), whatever CANNOSCALE says, and `RemoveContext` of that scale
refuses it as the last.

**CHANGED.** A `DxfTable.Fill` with `CopyContent`, with `CopyFormat` or not, and a `CopyFrom` of a cell emptied while the
drawing is open (reset, given an empty text, put in by `SetSize` or `InsertRows`, or emptied by a merge) leave the target's
content as it was, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33e): Z filled from B-12 reset stays Z, where the library emptied it. A
format copied from such a cell gives the target its alignment, background and lines alone, the target keeping its text
style, height, colour and kind of value. A cell read of no value from the file is copied as none, as before. With
`GenerateSeries`, `CopyContent` given or not, a source of no value gives the target none of no kind (`91 0`), where the
library kept or gave the flag 0x40000. A cell given a content by a fill or a copy is no longer one emptied in the session,
so `ClearTableStyleOverrides` writes one given none `93 5`, `90 512`.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.ClearTableStyleOverrides` of 0 or 2 and `RemoveAllOverrides` turn a cell's text or block back to
nought (145), as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33e t01 to t11): B-12 turned 90 degrees reads 0 after a clear, where the
library kept the turn. `RemoveAllOverrides` of a block cell takes its flag 0x40000 away too.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.ClearTableStyleOverrides` of any option keeps the title and the header left out (`280`, `281` and
bits 0 and 1 of `93`), where the library took them away; of 0 or 2 it keeps in the cells of a row of the title's or the
header's kind out of its place the looks of its kind, and so does `RemoveAllOverrides` where the table leaves its title or
header out, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33e m01 to m10, n01 to n09): the table given a row before its title and cleared of 0 writes `93 3`, `280 1`, `281 1`, its title cells
`170 5` and `140 6.0` and its header cells `170 5`, and AutoCAD then merges the new first row on load as it merges its
own file's (D33d s08). Existing test changed: `DxfTableD28cTests.TheTablesOwnOverridesInItsHead_AreReadAsAutoCadWritesThem`,
which expected the header shown again after a clear of 1. A clear of 0 or 2 reads the TABLECONTENT for the kinds of the
rows: on a table of 400 rows it takes 20 ms on .NET Framework 4.8, where it took 8, and 12 to 19 ms on .NET 10, where it
took 3 to 4; the other edits of the table are as fast as before.

**CHANGED.** From R2007 on, `DxfTable.SetValue` and `SetTextString` give a cell the flag of its kind of value
(`91 262144`) where it has it not, a cell reset, read of no value or put in, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33e w01 to w10);
the library wrote `91 0`, which AutoCAD read alike.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.MergeCells` writes the block's top left cell `173 0`, and `UnmergeCells` it `175 1`, `176 1`, and
the new cells of `InsertRows`, `InsertColumns`, `SetSize` and a `CopyFrom` that grows the table are written `175 1`,
`176 1`, as AutoCAD 2021 writes them (check D33e w07, w08, w11); the library wrote `173 1` and `175 0`, `176 0`, which
AutoCAD read alike. Existing tests changed: in `DxfTableStructureTests`,
`RowsPutIn_TakeTheirPlaceAndHeight_AndTheRowsBelowMoveDown`,
`RowsAndColumnsTakenOut_ShrinkTheBlocksTheyCross_AndOneLeftOfOneCellIsUnmerged` and
`CellsMerged_AreMarkedInEveryCell_TheirBlockOnItsTopLeft_AndUnmergedTakeAllBack`, which held the old groups.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.ClearTableStyleOverrides` of 0 or 2 leaves every cell emptied while the drawing is open of its value
of none (`93 7`, `90 0`), wherever rows or columns put in or taken out moved it since, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33d:
of 35 edits, AutoCAD read the library's files of 32 as its own): a cell reset or given an empty text, even one of no
value before, one put in by `InsertRows`, `InsertColumns` or `SetSize`, and one a merge emptied, the merge made on load
among them, even unmerged since. The table
given a row before its row 2 and cleared of 0 writes `93 7` in both cells of the new row, where the library wrote `93 5`,
`90 512`, which AutoCAD reads as an empty text; a cell read of no value from the file is written `93 5`, `90 512` as
before. Of 1 it takes from a cell reset the looks it kept as the table's, also after rows went in before it.

**CHANGED.** From R2007 on, `DxfTable.SetTextString` of an empty text leaves the value of none `ResetValue` leaves (`93 7`,
`90 0`, the flag 0x40000 taken out) and takes the looks of the content away as it does, as AutoCAD 2021 wrote it (check
D33d s01 to s10): B-12, 1.5 or the empty text of the title's hidden cell given `""` read as of no value, where the library
wrote an empty text of the kind 4. Before R2007 it writes an empty text, as before.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.ResetValue` (and `DxfCell.ResetValue`) of a block cell makes it a text cell of no value, its block,
attribute values and looks of the content gone as from a text cell and its content taken out of the TABLECONTENT, as
AutoCAD 2021 emptied the block cell M12 (`91 0`, `93 7`, `90 0`, check D33c r04, D33d b01 to b05); it threw
`InvalidOperationException` before. Existing test changed:
`DxfTableCellsTests.AValueSet_IsWrittenOfItsKind_ItsUnitAndFormatKept_AndAsATextBeforeR2007`, which expected the refusal.
`ResetValue` is as fast as before the looks it takes were added: 397 resets of a table of 400 rows take 1.6 to 1.7 s on
.NET 10, where they took 2.0 s, and 4.8 s run alone, and 2.7 s on .NET Framework 4.8, where they took 2.9 s.

**CHANGED.** A change of a `DxfTable`'s own colour, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, visibility or transparency
as an entity is an edit of it too: the first merges the rows AutoCAD 2021 merges when it loads a file, as any other first
edit does (check D33c e02, read back alike). No other entity's setters change.

**FIXED.** In GeometryHelper.IfcConvert, files opened through `IfcStoreCache` on several threads at once, as the first
thing a process does with xBIM, no longer throw "Collection was modified; enumeration operation may not execute." on
some of them (check D36). xBIM sets up its services the first time a store asks for them and takes no lock doing it, so
a store opened on another thread meanwhile read the list of services while it was being written to. The first
`IfcStoreCache` now sets them up before its store is opened, and those on other threads wait for it. With a thread
paused where a pause loses the race, 8 threads opening a file at once in a fresh application domain failed on 30 of 40
threads in 5 rounds out of 5, and fail on none now. Converting on several threads never met it, since conversion starts
once a store is open, and Tekla reference models open their files one at a time.

**CHANGED.** An annotative TEXT, ATTRIB or ATTDEF with contexts is read where AutoCAD 2021 shows it once it has read the
drawing (check D35): its `Position`, `AlignmentPoint` and `Rotation` are those of its context of the scale 1:1, else of
its default context, whatever CANNOSCALE says, at the elevation of its record, and its `Height` is the record's times the
default's scale over 1:1's. The attribute ATT_DVSUP of AutoCAD's sample Mechanical - Metric, whose record says (0.678,
265.33), now stands at (-6.151, 265.33), its context of 1:1, as AutoCAD reads and saves it; a text 3 high whose default
is 1:2 is 1.5 high. Setting those properties writes the context read, and the record where that context is the default
(a height at the default's scale: 5 at 1:1 is written 10 where 1:2 is the default); `SetAttributeFromBlock` places the
attribute so; `TransformBy` of the text or of its INSERT, and the INSERT's moves and dynamic properties that carry
attributes, carry every context with it, as AutoCAD moved ATT_DVSUP's context of 1:2 from (-100, 265.33) to (-90, 270.33)
with the INSERT moved by (10, 5). A text with no context reads and writes as before. Of 1 336 lines AutoCAD 2021 gave on
the sample and on drawings with two contexts, 597 read apart before and 65 now: an MTEXT and an INSERT's own place, still
read from their records, the point of a centred text, which AutoCAD works out from its font, and the INSERT's `Position`
setter, which carries its attributes as the library documents. Reading an annotative attribute for the first time after an edit
takes about a quarter longer, and again after that about a third less; one with no context is as fast as before.

**CHANGED.** The first edit of a `DxfTable` while its drawing is open, whatever it is (`SetValue`, `InsertRows`, `SetSize`,
`Fill`, a look, a line, `TransformBy` and the rest), merges first the rows AutoCAD 2021 merges when it loads a file, where
`DeleteRows` and `DeleteColumns` alone did, and writes them merged, as AutoCAD writes them whenever it saves, edited or not
(check D33c, 20 edits of a table read with its title unmerged, read back): the title Parts left unmerged over an empty
cell comes out merged across the table after a row is put in, a value set or the table moved. Later edits merge nothing,
so that a title unmerged in the session stays so, and a table read and not edited is written as it was read. Existing
test changed to build its states in the session that unmerges the title, as AutoCAD built them: `DxfTableD33bTests.AFirstRowThatHoldsMoreThanItsFirstCell_IsLeftUnmerged`.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.Fill` above (or left of) its source and longer than it repeats the source back from the fill
range's last cell, the source's last next to it, in whole lengths of the source, and leaves the cells of a length that
would reach before the table's first row or column as they are, as AutoCAD 2021 filled them (check D33c, 589 fills, every
one read alike): 2.5 and 3.5 filled into rows 10 to 12 give 3.5, 2.5 and 3.5, where the library gave 2.5, 3.5 and 2.5, and
four sources from column 7 filled into columns 0 to 6 fill 3 to 6 alone. A cell a block of merged cells hides is left as
it is: the title's second cell filled from Parts stays empty. A fill below or right of its source, one no longer than it,
and a series are as they were.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.ResetValue` takes the looks of the content away with the value, as AutoCAD 2021 did (check D33c r01
to r07): the cell's own text style, text height and colour, but those alike the table's own looks of its row's kind, and
its turn, made nought; its alignment, background and lines are kept. B-12 of GH_TXT, 5 high, red, turned 90 degrees and
bottom right on green keeps bottom right on green. `ClearTableStyleOverrides` of 0 or 2 leaves a cell reset while the
drawing is open of its value of none (`93 7`, `90 0`), and of 1 takes from it the looks it kept alike the table's, as
AutoCAD did (D33b c16 to c18); the library wrote `93 5`, `90 512` and kept the looks.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.MergeCells` leaves the hidden cell of a row of the title's kind moved down by a row put in before it
the title's `140 6.0` of AutoCAD's Standard, and gives it back for a height of its own, 3.0 made 6.0, as AutoCAD 2021 wrote
it, merged in the session or on load (check D33c k01 to k05, D33b m18, m23); the library took it away.

**NEW.** `DxfSpline.FitData` fits by the parameters `SqrtChord` and `Uniform` too, as AutoCAD 2021 does (check D32b): the
same cubic, open, closed or periodic, its knots going up by the square root of each chord or by 1, through five points the
knots 0 to 4 and AutoCAD's control points to 3E-14, written as AutoCAD writes it with no fit points, tangents or fit
tolerance and the flag 64 or 128 in place of 32 (70 1096 and 1160, 3147 and 3211 periodic). `FitData.KnotParam` reads
those flags, and 256 as `CustomParameterization`, and a spline not periodic whose fit points are the points at its knots
gives its derivatives at its ends as `StartFitTangent` and `EndFitTangent`, as AutoCAD read its own files and the
library's. Only `CustomParameterization` is refused now.

**FIXED.** `DxfSpline.ToPolylineWithPrecision` cuts a spline not periodic of n control points evenly into (n - 3) + (n - 2) k
pieces, k half the precision rounded down, where that is more pieces than the halving, as AutoCAD 2021 does (check D32b, 448
polylines of closed cubics and 80 of open curves): a closed one then has no last vertex on its first, and a closed one of
fit points as many of its knots in place as its vertices less two. The closed cubic through (0, 0), (40, 0), (40.5, 0.5),
(50, 30) and (10, 25) is at 0 its vertices at 0, 40.71, 55.57, 71.70 and 111.15, the straight cubic of 4 points 3 segments
at 2, and the quintic Bezier over 0 to 50 three at 0. 65 of D32's 72 polylines of AutoCAD's rings now match (52 before) and
