lies round by the whole face: of 8 000 unions and cuts at tolerances 1E-3 to 0.05, wrong or refused results fell from 24
to 4, and none that was right turned wrong.

**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of a `GeoPolygon3`, a `GeoFace3` and a `GeoSolid3` under an even scaling, turned, moved or
mirrored besides, carries the shape as a move does, its area scaled, and checks nothing again: the block 100 by 70 by 40
whose top is 0.0009 off flat, scaled by 10 or by 1 000 as a model in metres is brought into millimetres, stays closed
with its volume scaled, where it was refused as not flat, and a body with a pit 0.00005 deep cut at a millionth, scaled
by a tenth, stays closed, where its walls were refused as having no width. A stretch or a shear has each polygon checked
within the global tolerance loosened as far as the transformation stretches any direction, never made finer than it
was: the block stretched ten times upwards stays closed with its volume ten times. Over 600 random bodies under 16
transformations at the default tolerance, 1 460 of the 9 600 were refused or came back open and none now; over 3 000
polygons and faces, nothing kept before is refused. A projection that flattens a polygon to a line is still refused.
11 new tests.

**FIXED.** Two arcs in one plane whose centres stand a few tenths of a millionth apart cross on both: the line their
crossings lie on, carried along the difference of the centres, leant out of the plane by its rounding, so in a plane
leaning every way the circles of radius 39.7 about centres 1.4E-7 apart crossed up to 1.4E-7 off both and lost a
crossing at a ten-millionth. The line is laid in the plane now: of 9 000 random pairs, 26 lost a crossing, and none do
now. Every crossing of two arcs in one plane moves by its last digits as a result, onto the arcs: the furthest off was
0.998 of the point tolerance, and is now 1E-5 of it. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** The words of a text are read as AutoCAD 2021 reads them, checked headless on its own MTEXT and TEXT: `%%c` is
the diameter sign ∅ (U+2205, `DxfTextSymbols.Diameter`), not ⌀ (U+2300), in `DxfMText.Text`, `DxfReader` and the RTF of
an MTEXT; an MTEXT's `%%%` and `%%nnn` are kept as written, as AutoCAD's `Text` gives them and draws them (an MTEXT
`x%%%y` 10 high is 46.7 wide, against 26.7 for `x%y`), where a TEXT still reads them as a per cent sign and the character
of that code; and an MTEXT's `\~` is the space that does not break, U+00A0, not a plain space. A DIMENSION written without
its group 70, as AutoCAD 2021's DxfOut writes a rotated dimension on a named block, is opened as a rotated dimension, its
missing 50 an angle of 0, not as a `DxfUnknownEntity`. 8 new tests, 6 changed.

**NEW.** `DxfTextSymbols`, the symbols of AutoCAD's text editor as constants, for the words of a TEXT, an MTEXT, an
attribute or a dimension: the 21 letters its Symbol menu enters and its help lists, from `Degree` (°) and `Diameter` (∅,
U+2205, not the Latin letter Ø) to `Subscript2`, `Squared`, `Cubed` and `NonBreakingSpace`, and the menu's control codes
`DegreeCode` (`%%d`), `PlusMinusCode` (`%%p`) and `DiameterCode` (`%%c`). The writer is as it was:
`DxfTextSymbols.Diameter + "20"` in an MTEXT of R2004 is written `\U+220520`, and in one of R2018 as the letter. Checked
headless against AutoCAD 2021: each of the 21, written by the library into an MTEXT, a TEXT, an attribute and a dimension
of R2004 and of R2018, was read back as the same letter in all 210 readings, and AutoCAD wrote its own texts of them in
the same bytes. 8 new tests.

**FIXED.** A table cell of R2000 or R2004 longer than 250 letters is written in pieces of 250 letters in groups 3, the last
in 1, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it: written in groups 2, as the DXF reference has it, AutoCAD read the cell as empty, 251
letters as well as 600. A letter the code page lacks is written as its escape within its piece, and an escape given counts
as its one letter, as AutoCAD reads the escapes of each piece alone: 300 D with stroke, given as letters or as escapes, are
a 3 of 250 escapes, 1 750 characters, and a 1 of 50, where 250 escapes cut at 250 characters read as 286 letters. From
R2007 on a long text is written in 303 and a last 302 as well as in the value's 2 and 1, and read whole: the library read
only the last piece of AutoCAD's own cells of 600 letters, 100 of them. `SetTextString` and `SetValue` given the words a
cell has as they read, `xĐy` for a cell written `x\U+0110y`, change nothing, as `Contents` of an MTEXT does. 5 new tests,
1 changed.

**FIXED.** `DxfDatabase.Parse` of a drawing before R2007 with letters beyond ASCII keeps it in the code page its header
names, ANSI_1252 where it names none, each letter the page lacks as its escape, as AutoCAD would have saved it, and writes
what is changed so too: a string of R2004 with an MTEXT café Đ on a layer Thép é Đ is saved as caf, the byte E9 and
`\U+0110`, which AutoCAD 2021 reads as café Đ. It kept the UTF-8 of the string, which AutoCAD read as cafÃ© and refused
outright for the name of the layer (eInvalidSymbolTableName). A string of R2007 or later, or one all ASCII, is kept as
UTF-8 as before. Saving such a string costs more: 6 MB of R2004 with 20 000 letters é parsed and saved in 30 ms where
21 ms on .NET Framework 4.8, and 18 ms where 12 on .NET 10. 4 new tests, one a guard; the 47 tests that saved a parsed
drawing of R2000 with the layer Wand€Außen and compared the UTF-8 of its text compare the text now.

**FIXED.** A multibyte code, `\M+`, the number of a code page (1 Shift-JIS, 2 Big5, 3 Wansung, 4 Johab, 5 GB 2312) and
two bytes, is read as the letter of those bytes in every text and name, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it in a drawing of R2004 or
R2018: `\M+182A0` is あ, `\M+2A440` 一 and `\M+10041` an A, in an MTEXT, a TEXT, an attribute, a dimension, a MULTILEADER,
a table cell and a layer's name. One whose first byte is a letter alone, as `\M+1A4A1`, of bytes that are no letter, or of
a code page the runtime has not is kept as written. An MTEXT's `Text` leaves `\U+0000` out, as AutoCAD's does, and reads
`\M+1A4A1` as the letter of its first byte, U+FF64. 4 new tests, one a guard, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** `ApproxNumObjects` and `GetObject` find the records of the tables by handle under the lock the entities by
handle take, so that several threads looking objects up at once walk the drawing once. 1 new test, a guard.

**FIXED.** An arc in space meets a segment, and another arc, where they cross however short the segment or however near
the two centres, below the vector tolerance of 1E-5 too. The points of an arc on a line were taken for the one point the
line starts from wherever its direction was no longer than the vector tolerance, read as a length: at a millionth, the
segment from (0, 9.9999995, 0) to (0, 10.0000015, 0) met the arc of radius 10 about the origin at its start, where it
meets it at (0, 10, 0) as it did a hundred times larger, and the arcs of radius 10 about the origin and of radius
9.999999 about (0.000002, 0, 0) crossed once, where they cross at (5.0000007, ±8.6602536, 0). A line is read as a point
now only where it is no longer than the vector tolerance or the point tolerance, whichever is the finer, as a segment
crossing a segment and an ellipse are read. Of 759 segments longer than the point tolerance and no longer than 1E-5,
crossing arcs at tolerances from a hundred-millionth to a thousandth and compared a hundred and ten thousand times
larger, 190 met them at their start or nowhere at one size; none does now. Of 462 pairs of circles whose centres stand
closer than 1E-5 and further apart than the point tolerance, 42 lost a crossing, and 26 still do: each at a point
tolerance of 1E-7 or finer with the centres within three and a half tolerances, so that the circles cross at under
3E-8 radians. 5 490 segments longer than 1E-5, pairs further apart and pairs about one centre give the same bits, and
segments no longer than the point tolerance the same points to 8E-14. 2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `Flatten` of a `GeoPolygonArc3` checks the polygon of its corners enclosing an area within the global
tolerance, as the constructor of `GeoPolygon3` checks one and as `ToPolygon` and `TransformBy` of a polygon in space do,
while still keeping every corner however short a side. Since the last fix but one it took a sliver for an area: the half
disc of radius 1 built at a millionth with its diameter bent to (1, 0.000002, 0), whose three corners enclose 0.000002
square units, flattened to that sliver and is refused now, as the polygon of those corners is; the half disc of radius
50 bent so, whose corners enclose 0.0001 square units, flattens to them. Of 3 000 loops built within the global
tolerance none changes; of 4 000 built at a ten-millionth, 0.0001 to 10 across with chords up to 0.01 apart, 1 209 are
refused now, each enclosing under 1E-5 square units and under about a thousandth wide, and the rest give the same bits.
2 new tests, one a guard.

**FIXED.** A corner between two arcs, or between a straight piece and an arc, filleted by the radius at which the two
moved by it only touch is left square at any size. The arc about the one point they share would sweep half a turn,
which a fillet never draws; where they touched was read to nought, so a shade of overlap left by the rounding of the
numbers gave a centre whose arc swept a hair under half a turn, drawn at one size and not at another. It is read to the
rounding, 1E-12 of the largest coordinate or radius: the arcs of radii 10 and 7 about centres 12 apart, filleted where
they cross at 2.5, the radius of the circle filling the lens between them, were rounded by a half circle at that size
and left square at a thousandth of it and at a thousand times it, and the cap of the circle of radius 12 above a chord 4
from its centre, filleted at exactly 4, was rounded by a half circle at a thousand times its size. Of 4 013 corners
between two arcs and 999 between a straight piece and an arc filleted at such a radius, each at a thousandth, the whole
and a thousand times the size, 45 and 86 were rounded at one size and not at another; none is now, and only half
circles went. Of 2 455 radii a billionth to a hundredth off such a radius and the 8 000 corners of the last fix, two
lines crossing a circle less deep than the rounding were rounded by a hair under a half circle at every size and are
left square, and the rest give the same bits. 3 new tests, one a guard.

**FIXED.** `Reverse` of a `GeoPolygon3` turns it round corner for corner, `ToPolyline` of a `GeoPolygon2` and of a
`GeoPolygon3` writes it out side for side, and `ToPolygon` of a `GeoPolyline2` and of a `GeoPolyline3` closes it corner
for corner, however short a side, as the reversals in the plane do since the last fix. They were put back together within
the global tolerance of a thousandth: at a millionth, the triangle (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0, 10) with every corner cut
by 0.0003 reversed or closed from its chain came back three corners, where it keeps six, and written out a chain of four
vertices, where it is seven; and a reversed polygon was checked flat within the global tolerance again, so a square 100
across built at a hundredth with one corner 0.005 off the plane of the others was refused. A last vertex of a chain on the
first, or off it by no more than the rounding of its coordinates, 1E-12 of the largest of them and of one at the least,
is the chain written closed and goes: the chain round the square 10 across from (100, 100) ending 1E-12 off its start
is that square, and one ending 0.0001 off keeps the side back to its start, which the global tolerance dropped. Of 4 950
polygons in space, chamfered at tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth,
with a side between ten tolerances and 0.0009 long, built at a hundredth up to 0.009 off flat, or plain, 3 791 reversals
lost a corner or were refused; of the same shapes in the plane and in space, 4 808 of 7 944 chains written out and
14 814 of 23 944 polygons closed from chains lost a corner; none does now, but for 4 open chains that, closed, enclose no
area within the global tolerance. Plain shapes give the same bits, and so does `ToPolygon3` of a `GeoPolygonArc3`, which
still closes its last chord onto the first corner within the global tolerance: sampled, it can end further off than the
rounding, 1.8E-10 at coordinates near 50. 13 new tests, three of them guards.

**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of a `GeoPolyline3`, and of a `GeoPolygon3` and a `GeoFace3` under a transformation that does not
keep lengths, a scaling, a stretch or a shear, transform side for side, however short a side, as a rigid move of a polygon
or a face carried them already: at a millionth, the triangle (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0, 10) with every corner cut by
0.0003 keeps its six corners scaled by 2 or sheared, where it came back three, the chain (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0),
(10, 0, 10) with its corner cut by 0.0003 turns at both ends of the cut turned and moved, where it turned once, and the
same chain uncut scaled by 1E-5 is 0.0002 long, where it was refused as having fewer than two vertices. Only a corner
the transformation lands on the very same point as the one before it goes. A polygon is still checked flat and enclosing
an area within the global tolerance, so one shrunk under about a thousandth across is still refused as having no width.
Of the chains of the survey above, 15 883 of 24 438 transforms lost a leg or were refused, 5 184 of 8 146 of them turns,
moves and mirrors; none does now. Of the polygons and of the faces with them for holes, 6 243 of 11 781 scaled by a half
to two, stretched or sheared lost a corner, each; none does now, and of 3 927 shrunk by a millionth to a hundredth 3 494
lost a corner or were refused, where 2 598 are, every one for having no width. Rigid moves of polygons and faces, and
plain shapes, give the same bits. 6 new tests, one a guard.

**FIXED.** A corner where a straight piece runs into an arc is filleted alike at any size by a radius at which the straight
piece's parallel line only touches the arc's moved circle, or misses it: it is left square. The circle about the point
of touching would round the corner by half a circle, which a fillet never draws; it was let in where the difference of the
squared radius and the squared distance, an area, was within the tolerance, a length, and its arc then drawn or not as the
rounding of its sweep fell. The cap of the circle of radius 12 above a chord 4 from its centre, turned by half a radian
and moved to (30, 40), filleted where the chord runs into the arc by 4.000025 within 1E-4 was left square, and the same
cap 1 000 times smaller within 1E-7 rounded by a half circle. Of 1 335 such caps filleted by up to half a tolerance more
than the largest circle in them, each at a thousandth, the whole and a thousand times the size, 588 were rounded at one
size and not at another; none is now, and 6 665 filleted by a radius that fits or by more give the same bits. 2 new
tests, one a guard.

**FIXED.** `DxfMText.Contents` reads a letter written as its escape as the letter, as AutoCAD 2021 reads the MTEXT of a
drawing of R2004 or older, which writes so each letter its code page has not: `a\U+0110b` is aĐb, and the escapes of the
two halves of a letter beyond U+FFFF, `\U+D83D\U+DE00`, are that letter, U+1F600. It gave the escapes, so that an MTEXT of
R2004 set to aĐb read back as `a\U+0110b`, where `Text` and a TEXT's `TextString` gave the letters. Set, the letters are
written as they are from R2007 on and as escapes before, as they were; and the pieces of 250 characters an MTEXT is
written in no longer part the two halves of such a letter, which a drawing of R2007 or later wrote as two escapes. 8 new
tests.

**FIXED.** Every text reads its escapes as AutoCAD 2021 reads them, checked headless on drawings of R2004 and R2018 the
library wrote: each escape of four digits is the letter it stands for, in a drawing of any version, `\u+0110` as well as
`\U+0110`, and before an MTEXT's formatting, so that `\\U+0110` is a backslash and Đ, `\U+0041` an A, `\U+005CP` a new
paragraph and `\U+D83D` that half alone; `\U+0000` and an escape of fewer digits are kept as written. `DxfMText.Contents`
kept the escaped backslash, the escape of a letter of ASCII and half a letter alone as written; a dimension's
`DimensionText`, a table cell's `TextString` and `Value` and the value `GetBlockAttributeValue` gives kept every escape;
a MULTILEADER's words were read as `Contents`; an MTEXT's `Text` read `\\U+0110` as Đ; a TEXT's `TextString` read
`\U+0000` as a null character and kept `\u+0110`. Of 320 readings of 20 kinds of escape in seven texts, the library gave
what AutoCAD gives in 172 and gives it in 310; the ten left are a cell AutoCAD reads empty, a line break AutoCAD's `Text`
gives as a carriage return and line feed, `\M+` codes and `\U+0000` in an MTEXT's `Text`. 5 new tests, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** A letter beyond U+FFFF, such as the face U+1F600, is written into a drawing of R2007 or later as the escapes
of its two halves, `\U+D83D\U+DE00`, as before R2007: AutoCAD 2021 opened no drawing of R2018 the library wrote with such
a letter in it ("DXF read error" on the line after it), and reads the escapes as the letter. 1 new test, 4 changed.

**CHANGED.** The entities of a drawing by handle are looked up under a lock, and its objects by handle kept by the first
thread to read them, so that several threads copying from one drawing at once, dynamic blocks and all, make nothing of it
twice: eight threads copying a drawing of four dynamic blocks and twelve INSERTs of them, 60 times over by `Insert`,
`Insert(name)`, `WblockCloneObjects` and `WblockCloneObjects` of one entity at a time, each give the drawing it gives
alone, as they did in 1 500 rounds before. `ApproxNumObjects` counts the entities under the same lock. 2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** An INSERT of an anonymous block standing for a dynamic block finds that block through the block table by
handle, not by reading every block record: `IsDynamicBlock`, `DynamicBlockTableRecord` and `AnonymousBlockTableRecord` of
500 such INSERTs among 5 000 blocks took 71 ms under .NET Framework 4.8 and 68 under .NET 10, and take 18 under both, the
same blocks found.

**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of a `GeoPolygon2`, a `GeoPolyline2` and a `GeoFace2`, and `GeoTransform2.Transform` of them,
transform side for side, however short a side and however small the transformation leaves it, and `Reverse` of a
`GeoPolygon2` and of a `GeoPolyline2` turns it round corner for corner, as `Translate` and `RotateBy` move it since the
last fix. They were put back together within the global tolerance of a thousandth: at a millionth, the triangle (0, 0),
(10, 0), (10, 10) with every corner cut by 0.0003, turned, moved, mirrored or reversed, came back three corners, where it
keeps six, and the square 10 by 10 scaled by 1E-5 was refused for having fewer than three corners, where it is the square
0.0001 across. Only a corner the transformation lands on the very same point as the one before it goes. Of 8 000
polygons and chains, two in three chamfered at tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth or with a side between ten
tolerances and 0.0009 long, and of the faces with the polygons for holes, each turned and moved, mirrored, scaled by a
half to two and shrunk by a millionth to a hundredth, 31 989 of 47 820 transforms lost a corner or were refused, and
4 966 of 8 000 reversals lost one; none does now. Shapes the merge left whole give the same bits. 7 new tests.

**FIXED.** `Flatten` of a `GeoPolygonArc3` and of a `GeoPolylineArc3` keeps every corner, however short a side: at a
millionth, the rectangle 100 by 50 standing in the plane x = 20 filleted at 0.0005 flattens to its eight corners, where it
was put back together within the global tolerance of a thousandth and came back four, and the chain (0, 0, 0),
(10, 0, 0), (10, 0, 10) filleted at 0.0005 turns at both ends of its arc, where it turned once. They keep the chords, each
arc the straight side between its ends, as they always did, where `Flatten` of their twins in the plane cuts each arc
into pieces; `ToPolygon3(chordTolerance)` and `ToPolyline3(chordTolerance)` follow the arcs. Of 8 000 loops and chains in
space, two in three filleted at tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth or with a side between ten tolerances and
0.0009 long, 4 808 lost a corner; none does now. Loops and chains with no side under a thousandth give the same bits.
2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GeoCoordinateSystem3` and `GeoCoordinateSystem2` take an X axis of any length but none: (0, 6E-7, 8E-7)
points the X axis in space along (0, 0.6, 0.8), and (6E-7, 8E-7) the one in the plane along (0.6, 0.8), where an axis
shorter than the global vector tolerance of 1E-5, read as a length, was refused as having none. Of 3 949 X axes from
1E-150 to 1E-5 long, each tried in space and in the plane, every one was refused; none is now, and axes of unit length
give the same frames to the bit. So `TransformBy` of a `GeoCoordinateSystem3` follows a scaling however small: 4 688 of
5 349 scalings from 1E-12 to 1E-4 were refused; none is now. 5 new tests.

**FIXED.** A curved chain or loop offset with miters meets a straight piece and an arc's moved circle where they cross,
or where the line misses the circle by no more than the tolerance, alike at any size. The miss was read as the difference
of the squared radius and the squared distance from the centre, an area, against the tolerance, a length, so a small
drawing took a line for touching a circle it missed by many tolerances: the chain (-0.001165, -0.002711),
(0.00062, -0.001059), (0.002589, 0.00029), (0.000415, 0.000801), (-0.00214, 0.003174), (-0.001103, 0.000257), its third
and fourth edges bowed by 0.24 and -0.24, offset by -0.0000702 with miters at 1.5 within 2E-6, met at its fifth corner a
line that missed the moved arc by 0.00014, seventy times the tolerance, and broke in two, where it is one chain of eight
corners, as the same chain 64 times larger is. Of 9 000 chains and loops 0.0002 to 0.01 across offset by 1E-7 to 3E-5
within a ten-billionth to a ten-millionth, 3 broke apart where the same shape scaled up did not; none does now, and the
other 8 997 give the same bits. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** A boolean welded closed no longer tilts a face round a corner the face lies round, a hole's corner, one where
its edge turns back into a notch or one part way along a straight edge, where a weld that keeps the face flat closes it
moving the volume less. A weld takes each group of corners within the tolerance of each other to the one of them that
takes the most of the group and, of those, moves the volume least, each corner weighed by the triangle it makes with the
corners its faces turn at; such a corner makes no triangle of the face and weighed next to nothing taken off it. A column
300 by 300 by 1 000 and a beam 160.1 by 160.8 whose end stood exactly 0.01 clear of its side, turned and joined within a
hundredth, had two corners of the hole in the column's face taken 0.01 off it to the beam's: the face, 274 255 square
millimetres, came out tilted, and the union held the two and 918.9 cubic millimetres, closed and valid, where filling the
gap holds 257.4. It holds the two and 214.5 now, the beam's corners taken onto the column's face along its sides. Where a
weld tilts faces by more than a hundredth of the tolerance and moves the volume by more than a tenth of the tolerance
times their area, or tilts one and does not close, it is made again with such a corner, taken off the face's plane
further than a hundredth of the tolerance, weighed by the whole face, once taking each group to the corner that takes the
most of it and once to the corner that moves the volume least; of those that close wound alike and tilt less of the faces
than the first, the one moving the volume less is taken where it moves it less than the tilt, or, laying no face over
another, where the first did not close. A
beam 141.8 by 164.8 running exactly 0.01 into the column came out 1 216.9 short of the two less their overlap and holds
the two; and unions only such a tilt closed, refused as moving the volume too far or coming out open as `Validate`
reads it, are made: the beam 377.4 wide and 107.5 high running exactly 0.01 into the column holds the two less 364.0,
the slab where they overlap being 322.4, and one 245.9 by 327.5 running exactly 0.001 into it, joined within a
thousandth, the two. A weld whose corners go where they went is made as before: the column whose faces come in 1 to 1 000
strips, joined to a beam framing 0.002 into its flange, holds the two less 18.96 at every count, to the bit.

Of 8 000 columns 300 by 300 by 1 000 joined to beams their end 0.8 to 2 tolerances into or clear of them, turned and
moved, the 8 unions wrong at 0.01 are right and the 3 refused made, at 0.05 the 4 wrong are right and one of 3 refused
is made, and at 0.001 the 4 refused are made; 17 unions within the band come out on the exact reading, and none right
moved out of it. Of 5 400 booleans of a cube and boxes exactly the tolerance into, onto or beside it, 6 unions wrong
are right and one refused is made, and 13 right moved within the band, 7 of them nearer the exact volume and the rest
to the two read as touching; within half, 0.8, 1.25, 1.5 and 2 times the tolerance none moved. 600 plates with twelve
openings cut in at once, 400 bands, 70 bent bars, the columns in strips, 150 000 bodies with openings, prisms and bodies
far from the origin, 216 000 booleans near the rounding of the coordinates, and the cracked bodies worked out at a
tolerance of nought are the same to the bit; of 70 252 booleans and cuts of cubes, tilted and tapered bodies and boxes,
45 moved within the class each was in, 37 nearer the exact volume and 8 further, the furthest by 1.7, and of 72 000 of
U bodies 127, 114 nearer, the furthest by 1.2. On .NET Framework 4.8 the union of the beam 160.1 by 160.8 and the column
takes 1.07 milliseconds where it took 0.85, welded twice more, and the one 245.9 by 327.5 3.6 where it took 7.3; the
column in 150 and 300 strips takes 4 % more, and twelve openings cut out of a plate at once up to 7 % more. Booleans
that weld nothing take what they took.

**FIXED.** A curved chain is copied, moved and turned edge for edge, every arc and leg however small, by `Clone`,
`Translate` and `RotateBy` of `GeoPolylineArc2` and `Clone` and `Translate` of `GeoPolylineArc3`, as a curved loop has
been since the last fix; a straight polygon or chain is moved and turned side for side by `Translate` and `RotateBy` of
`GeoPolygon2` and `GeoPolyline2`, and so of `GeoFace2` and by the `+` and `-` operators. They were put back together
within the global tolerance of a thousandth: at a millionth, the chain (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 10) filleted at 0.0005, in
the plane or standing in space, came back turning at a corner, where it keeps its arc 0.0007 across, and the triangle
through the same corners with every corner cut by 0.0003 came back three corners, where it keeps six. Of 8 000 chains,
two in three filleted at tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth or with a leg between ten tolerances and 0.0009
long, 12 536 copies lost an edge, and of 8 000 polygons and chains, two in three chamfered or with a side as short,
10 046 moves and turns lost a corner; none does now. `TransformBy` of a curved chain went edge for edge already. Shapes
with no edge shorter than a thousandth give the same bits. 9 new tests.

**FIXED.** The centroid of a `GeoFace2`, a `GeoFace3` and a `GeoPolygon3` weighs the area however small, as that of a
`GeoPolygon2` has since the last fix: an area of a millionth or less was taken for none, so a face gave its boundary's
centroid, its holes left out, and a polygon in space its first corner. The square 0.001 by 0.001 with a hole 0.0004 by
0.0004 in its corner, of 8.4E-7 square units, balances at (0.000538, 0.000538), where it gave (0.0005, 0.0005); the
triangle (10, 20, 30), (10.0009, 20, 30), (10, 20, 30.0009) balances at (10.0003, 20, 30.0003), where it gave
(10, 20, 30). Only an area lost in the rounding of the sums it comes from is none. Of the centroids of 8 000 faces
0.00001 to 10 across, with up to two holes, in the plane and in space, and of their boundaries in space, 7 236 stood off
the same face scaled up; none does now. Those over a millionth in area give the same bits, and a face with no holes
under it gives its boundary's centroid to the last digit, as it did. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GeoCoordinateSystem3` judges its two directions parallel by the angle between them, the sine of it within
the global vector tolerance of 1E-5, where it read the length of their cross product against that tolerance: two
directions 0.002 long and square to each other span a frame, where they were refused as parallel, and two 10 long and
5E-6 of a radian apart are parallel, where they spanned a frame. Of 8 000 pairs of directions 0.0001 to 10 long, 1 259
short ones were refused and 12 long ones taken; none is now. Directions of unit length give the same frame to the bit.
So `TransformBy` of a `GeoCoordinateSystem3` follows a scaling down to 1E-5, where one by less than 0.0032, which leaves
its axes as short, was refused as leaving them parallel. `GeoCoordinateSystem2.TransformBy` keeps the axes under a
scaling however small, where it refused one by 1E-5 or less as leaving no axes: 4 608 of 5 266 scalings from 1E-12 to
1E-4 were refused; none is now. 5 new tests.

**FIXED.** `Flatten` of a `GeoPolygonArc2` and of a `GeoPolylineArc2` flattens a loop or a chain too small for the merge
of its corners within the point tolerance to leave a polygon or a chain: it keeps every corner of its chords, where it
was refused for having too few. The square 0.0005 by 0.0005 flattens to its four corners, and with its sides bowed by a
bulge of 0.2 to the corners of their chords. Of 8 000 loops 0.000002 to 200 across, 4 220 could not be flattened, and of
4 072 chains under a thousandth 4 042; none now. Loops and chains the merge leaves a polygon or a chain give the same
bits. 3 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfDatabase.Insert` and `WblockCloneObjects` copy a block AutoCAD names itself once for the call, however
many INSERTs place it, as AutoCAD's own insert keeps one `*U` for two INSERTs that share it (AutoCAD's saves of the checks
24d-d and 24d-g, inserted by AutoCAD in its check v23), where they copied it once for each INSERT: two INSERTs of one `*U`
come as two INSERTs of one copy, dynamic or not, and each is set as the INSERT it was copied from. Two calls of
`WblockCloneObjects` copy it once each, as two calls of AutoCAD's do. 31 of the 226 drawings of dynamic blocks of the
checks hold such a pair; each copy of them now has as many `*U` as its source. A block placed by one INSERT comes as
before, to the bit: 11 700 copies of the 492 drawings without dynamic blocks of the checks, three ways by `Insert` and two
by `WblockCloneObjects` into five drawings each, write the same but for the code page of a new drawing below, and 600 more
are refused alike.

**CHANGED.** `WblockCloneObjects` of a dynamic INSERT into another drawing of R2010 or later keeps it dynamic, as `Insert`
does since the last change, where it brought a static copy: the dynamic block it places comes with it, or the one its
anonymous block stands for where it places a `*U`, which AutoCAD's deep clone brings by the pointer of the INSERT's
representation, and then what makes them dynamic, as `Insert` copies it. An INSERT of GH_PANEL set to a Width of 200,
copied alone into a new drawing, brings `*U1` and GH_PANEL, reads Width 200 and is set again as the one it was copied
from. A drawing that has a block of the name keeps its own, the copies standing for it where it is dynamic and static
otherwise; a drawing older than R2010 takes a static copy of the INSERT's block alone, as before. The 226 drawings of
dynamic blocks, their model space copied by one call and by a call for each entity into new drawings of R2018 and R2010,
give every INSERT the dynamic properties, values and drawing it had, no handle naming what the drawing has not, and
nothing for ezdxf's recover and audit to fix; the sets of a value on those copies give what they give on the originals.
Copied one by one, 4 000 INSERTs of GH_PANEL of which 2 000 are set take about 0.6 seconds under .NET 10 and 1.1 under
.NET Framework 4.8, where their static copies took 0.4 and 0.7; the dynamic block an INSERT stands for is found through
the block table, which reads the blocks by handle once, not once for each call.

**FIXED.** A new drawing, `new DxfDatabase(version)`, names its code page in its header after its version,
`$DWGCODEPAGE` ANSI_1252, as AutoCAD's own empty drawings of R2000 to R2018 name it. Without it, ezdxf took a drawing of
R2007 or later for one in ANSI_1252, though its text is UTF-8, so that Korean text copied into it read as other letters
and its recover said "Fixed unicode decoding error" for each line of it; it reads the letters written now, with nothing
to fix. The text is written as before: in UTF-8 from R2007, and as its escapes (`\U+CCA0`) before. `new
DxfDatabase("AC1015")` is the drawing `DxfWriter` writes but for that variable.

**FIXED.** A curved loop is copied, moved, turned and transformed edge for edge, every arc and side however small, by
`Clone`, `Translate`, `RotateBy` and `TransformBy` of `GeoPolygonArc2`, and `Clone`, `Translate` and `TransformBy` of
`GeoPolygonArc3`, as its fillets, chamfers and offsets have kept it since the last fixes. The copy was put back together
within the global tolerance of a thousandth: at a millionth, the rectangle 100 by 50 filleted at 0.0005 came back its
four corners, where it keeps its eight edges, four of them arcs 0.0007 across, in the plane and
standing in space; scaled to a tenth it keeps arcs 0.00007 across. Of 6 000 loops filleted at tolerances from a billionth
to a ten-thousandth or with a side between ten tolerances and 0.0009 long, copied, moved, turned, mirrored and scaled in
the plane and in space, 19 831 copies lost an edge; none does now. Loops with no edge shorter than a thousandth give the
same bits, 10 918 copies of them; an offset by no more than the tolerance, which gives the loop back, gives it back
whole. 9 new tests.

**FIXED.** A straight chain or polygon cut by `Corner2.Chamfer` or `TryChamferAt` is put back together within the
tolerance asked, as a curved one is and as a straight chain in space has been since the last fix, so a cut longer than
the tolerance stays. It was put back together within the global tolerance: at a millionth, the chain (0, 0), (10, 0),
(10, 10) cut by 0.0003 turned at (9.9997, 0) alone, the two ends of the cut 0.00042 apart taken for one corner, where it
turns at (9.9997, 0) and (10, 0.0003); the triangle through the same corners came back three corners, where it has six.
Within a coarser tolerance than the global one, a cut no longer than it is no edge and the shape turns where the cut
starts: the chain cut by 0.03 at a tenth turns once, where it turned twice. Of 6 000 chains and polygons cut at
tolerances from a billionth to a tenth, every corner at once and one corner alone, 6 489 of 24 000 came out unlike the
same cut in space; none does now. At the global tolerance every cut is the same to the bit; 975 of the 6 016 cut at a
hundredth or a tenth lose a cut no longer than the tolerance. 5 new tests.

**FIXED.** An offset of a curved loop or chain by less than 1E-5, `Offset2.Offset` and the `Offset` of `GeoPolygonArc2`,
`GeoPolylineArc2` and `GeoPolygonArc3`, is squared off past the miter limit and cut by its chamfers as a larger one is.
The ways out from a corner to the moved ends, as long as the distance, were read within the vector tolerance of 1E-5 as
having no direction: a corner past the limit was rounded and a chamfer cut across its chord. At a billionth, the square
of side 0.00001 grown by 0.000002 with chamfers is cut 0.000002 from every corner, where it enclosed 1.88E-10 square
units, short of 1.93255E-10; the triangle with a 10 degree tip a millionth the size grown by a millionth is squared off
0.00001 from the tip. Of 6 000 stars and chains 0.0002 to 0.01 across offset with a miter limit of 1.5 or chamfers at
tolerances from 1E-10 to 1E-7, 1 613 offsets by less than 1E-5 came out unlike the same shape scaled until the distance
is 1; none does now, and one chain shrunk into two pieces where the scaled one stays whole still does, as it did.
Offsets by 1E-5 or more give the same bits but one, beside a side shorter than 1E-5, now like the scaled shape too, and
so does every one of 20 000 stars and wavy rings offset with miters, limited miters and chamfers, but for those offset by
no more than the tolerance, which come back whole as the copy above. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GeoTransform2.Mirror` takes a segment of any length as the line to reflect across, where one shorter than
1E-5 was read within the global vector tolerance as having no direction and refused: the segment from (0, 0) to
(0.000007, 0.000007) mirrors (1, 0) to (0, 1). Of 4 531 segments between a billionth and 1E-5 long, every one was
refused; none is now, and each mirrors as the line through its two ends does. Longer segments give the same bits. 1 new
test.

**FIXED.** `GeoPolygon2.Centroid` weighs the area however small. An area of a millionth or less, read against the global
tolerance, was taken for none and the corners were averaged: the L 0.001 by 0.001 with legs 0.00025 wide, of 4.4E-7
square units, balanced at (0.000417, 0.000417), where it balances at (0.000339, 0.000339). Only corners on one line,
whose area is lost in the rounding of their coordinates, are averaged now, as they were. The centroid of a curved loop,
`GeoPolygonArc2.Centroid`, which weighs the straight loop through its corners, is right for small loops with it. Of
2 446 polygons enclosing a millionth or less, 1 950 had their centroid off, and of 1 165 curved loops less than a
thousandth across, 867; none has now. Polygons enclosing more give the same bits, and so do 1 150 sets of corners on one line.
2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfDatabase.Insert` of another drawing keeps its dynamic blocks dynamic, as AutoCAD's own insert keeps them,
where it brought them as static copies before. The extended data of a dynamic block's BLOCK_RECORD (its true name, its
GUID and its tags) and the evaluation graph with its nodes and the purge preventer of its extension dictionary come with
the block, the AcDbBlockRepBTag with each anonymous block standing for it, and the representation data, the values and
any history of grip edits with each INSERT. Every object is copied under a handle of its own, and every handle among
them names the copy of what it named, an entity of the block, a node of the graph or the block itself, so that nothing
points into the other drawing or at nothing; the classes of the objects are listed and the applications of their
extended data registered. A block GH_PANEL of a Width of 100 with an INSERT of it set to 200 comes as GH_PANEL, dynamic,
its INSERT reading Width 200, and Width set to 270 on the copy stretches its anonymous block as the same set stretches the
original's. A dynamic block of a name the drawing has is the drawing's own, as any block of the name is: the INSERTs
copied stand for it where it is dynamic, and are static copies otherwise; a drawing older than R2010, into which the
library writes no dynamic block, takes them static as before. Both overloads do so, `Insert("SHEET", other, true)` too.
226 drawings of dynamic blocks (ACadSharp's AutoCAD samples, AutoCAD's saves of the checks v16 to v22, the library's
own), each inserted into new drawings of R2018 and R2010, moved and not, give every INSERT the dynamic properties and
values it had, no handle naming what the drawing has not, and nothing new for ezdxf's recover and audit to fix; 2 150 sets of
a value on the copies give what the same sets give on the originals, 2 008 of them drawn and the rest refused alike. A
drawing with no dynamic block is inserted as before, to the bit: 7 380 inserts of 492 drawings, three ways into five
drawings each, write the same. Inserting a drawing of 1 000 INSERTs of which 500 are set, the 4 000 objects of their
representations copied, takes about 75 milliseconds under .NET 10 where it took 45, and 195 under .NET Framework 4.8
where it took 130; ACadSharp's linear sample, of two INSERTs, takes 0.8 where it took 0.5 (1.5 and 0.8); a drawing with
no dynamic block takes what it took.

**FIXED.** The area, the winding, the centroid and the check for crossings of a curved loop in space,
`GeoPolygonArc3.Area`, `SignedArea`, `IsClockwise`, `Centroid` and `IsSimple`, read the loop as it is, every arc and
side however small, and `Reverse` turns it round edge for edge, as its fillets, chamfers and offsets have worked on it
since the last fix. The loop was laid out in its plane within the global tolerance, which dropped the arcs and sides
shorter than a thousandth that work at a finer tolerance leaves, and reversing put it back together within it: at a
millionth, the rectangle 100 by 50 standing in the plane x = 20 filleted at 0.0005 read 4 999.9375, where it encloses
4 999.99999979, and reversed to its four corners; with only its corner (20, 100, 50) rounded, its centroid was 0.00008
off (20, 50, 25). In the plane, `GeoPolygonArc2.Reverse` put the loop back together within the global tolerance as well,
and `Centroid` weighed the straight loop through corners merged within it and left out an arc of radius 0.00001 or
less; both read the loop as it is now. Of 6 000 loops standing in planes at random, filleted or chamfered at
tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth or with a side between ten tolerances and 0.0009 long, 3 497 read an
area off the formula, 3 331 a centroid off, 3 539 reversed to fewer edges in space and in the plane, and 24 read simple
where the same loop in the plane crosses itself; none does now. Loops with no arc or side shorter than a thousandth
give the same bits. Within a tolerance coarser than an edge, the edges either side of it meet across it, so a loop
holding such an edge is not simple at the global tolerance, as it is not in the plane: 3 366 of the 6 000, read simple
before, are not; within a tolerance finer than their edges they are. Each takes the time it took, within the noise,
and a centroid 6 to 9 % less. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** A corner beside a side shorter than a hundredth of a millimetre is rounded by `Corner2.Fillet` and
`TryFilletAt`, the members that call them and `Corner3.Fillet` and `TryFilletAt` of a loop in space, and such a side
moves with the rest when a loop or a chain that may curve is grown or shrunk by `Offset2.Offset` or the `Offset` of
`GeoPolygonArc2` and `GeoPolygonArc3`. The side was read within the global vector tolerance of 1E-5 as having no
direction: the fillet found no circle touching it and left the corner alone, and the offset left the side where it was
and squared the corner off. At a millionth, the square 10 by 10 at the origin with its corner (0, 0) cut off by a side 0.000007 long is rounded by 0.00001 at (0.000005, 0),
where it was left alone, and grown by a half it keeps that side, 0.41422 long now. Of 6 000 loops with a side between
ten tolerances and 0.00005 long, at tolerances from a billionth to a tenth, the 369 corners beside a side shorter than
1E-5 with room for the radius were left alone and the 385 grown lost that side; none is now. Loops with no side shorter
than 1E-5 give the same bits, and so does every one of 20 000 stars and wavy rings offset with miters, limited miters
and chamfers. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** A straight chain in space cut by `Corner3.Chamfer` or `TryChamferAt` is put back together within the
tolerance asked, as a loop's cut corners and a curved chain's are, so a cut longer than that tolerance stays. It was put
back together within the global tolerance: at a millionth, the chain (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 10, 0) cut by 0.0003
turned at (9.9997, 0, 0) alone, the two ends of the cut 0.00042 apart taken for one corner, where it turns at
(9.9997, 0, 0) and (10, 0.0003, 0). Within a coarser tolerance than the global one, a cut no longer than it is no edge
and the chain turns where the cut starts, as a loop and a curved chain turn: a chain cut by 0.03 at a tenth turns once
at each corner, where it turned twice. Of 6 000 chains cut at tolerances from a billionth to a tenth, 906 came out with
a cut missing or a corner moved; none does now. At the global tolerance every chain is the same to the bit; 470 cut at
a hundredth or a tenth lose a cut no longer than the tolerance. A chain is cut in 8 to 20 % less time. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `TrySubtract`, `TryIntersect` and `TryUnion` asked below four tenths of the rounding of the coordinates,
nought among it, of a body that does not close within that rounding, as one with cracks in its faces does not, no
longer keep what they give within the rounding where it does not hold up and the tolerance alone gives something too:
what the tolerance alone gives is taken where it holds up by the same checks, and the boolean is not worked out
otherwise. At nought a cube 10 across cracked 0.0001 wide, turned, less a slab thousands long through it, sharing
249.85, came back whole, 999.998, where 750.15 is left. A difference or a union of two such bodies, neither of which
closes, holds up only where the common part it is checked by has no corner outside either and leaves out no corner of
one inside the other, as a common part of them does since the last change; a difference said to be nothing is checked
as one holding nothing, and a common part said to be nothing holds up only where the skin of neither body runs into the
other. A U 30 by 10 by 10 and a box through its notch, both cracked 2.7E-5 wide, came out each less the other and
joined 25.6 over; such a U less a box dipping 0.81 into its notch's floor was said to leave nothing, where it leaves
2 402.34; and the cube and a slab cutting 15.23 off its corner were said to share nothing. None is worked out now. The
volumes a difference or a union is checked by may miss by twice a third of each open body's open area times the
diagonal of its box, two thirds of what they could, as no reading of a volume moves by more than a third of it and the
result and the common part, sharing the body's open faces, by as much again; and a difference no longer allows for the
faces of the body taken away lying off flat, as that body's volume does not enter it. The cube joined to a box through
its corner held 1 010.4075, 0.0115 short of the two, and less a slab five million long came back whole, 27.28 over; neither
is worked out now. Of 17 178 booleans of such a cube and a body through it at nought, 742 made more than 0.01, what the
cracks move, from what the uncracked cube gives and 126 said to be nothing were trusted: 14 unions with slabs thousands
long still are, less wrong than the slab's faces off flat move its volume, and 4 of the 15 698 made within 0.01 are not
worked out now. With the cube cracked 0.001 wide, of 715 made more than 0.1 off and 123 said to be nothing, 7 unions
still are, one difference is right, and 29 of 15 880 within 0.1 are not worked out now. Of 36 000 of a U so cracked and
a box, 5 381 made wrong and 799 said to be nothing were trusted, and 36 still are; 231 of 13 630 within 0.01 of the
uncracked U, none of them valid at nought, are not worked out now, most because the common part they are checked by is
not worked out within the rounding either. Nothing that was right comes out wrong, and every boolean of bodies that
close, or asked at four tenths of the rounding and above, is worked out as it was, to the bit. Booleans that come out
as they did take what they took, within the noise. Turned down, the cracked U less a box dipping into its floor takes
2.8 milliseconds, where it took 4.0 to come out whole (7.9 and 11.2 on .NET Framework 4.8), and the cube less the slab
6.3, where it took 5.1 (17.8 and 15.0). A difference said to be nothing is checked by the common part it should add up
with: the U less a box in its notch takes 3.6 milliseconds, where it took 1.0 to be said to leave nothing (9.8 and
3.0), and two closed bodies at nought whose common part or difference is nothing take 0.19, where they took 0.07 (0.054
and 0.016), whether each closes being read once.

**FIXED.** `TryIntersect` asked below four tenths of the rounding of the coordinates, nought among it, of two bodies
neither of which closes within that rounding, as two with cracks in their faces do not, is not worked out where the
common part it gives has a corner outside either, each read as though it closed, or leaves out a corner of one lying
inside the other; nothing checked it, and at nought a U 30 by 10 by 10 and a box through its notch, both cracked 1.5E-5
wide, came out sharing 3.66 where they share 34.02. Of 36 000 booleans of such a U and a box at nought, the 21 common
parts made wrong where the tolerance alone gave nothing are not worked out now, and none that held what the two share
is turned down. `TryUnion` and `TrySubtract` of such a body, checked by the volumes adding up with the common part of
the two, allow as well for what faces lying off flat move a volume, a third of how far a corner of each stands off its
plane times its area: a cube 10 across cracked 0.0001 wide, turned, joined to a slab a million long through it, whose
corners stand off its faces where planes a millionth of a radian apart meet, holds 59 169 796.05, what the two hold
within 0.01, and is made again, where the check turned it down for missing the two less their common part by 0.57, as
much as the slab read whole is short of what it holds. Of 17 178 booleans of such a cube and a body through it at
nought, the 2 unions turned down so are made again, and none turned down before is made wrong. Every other boolean is
worked out as it was, to the bit. Whether a body closes is read once for each tolerance it is asked within in turn, so
two closed bodies asked below the rounding take what they took, within the noise, and the same two asked again up to a
fifth less: a plate and a slot 1E6 out sharing 3 000 at nought, 0.048 milliseconds where 0.056 on .NET 10, 0.130 where
0.164 on .NET Framework 4.8. Turned down, the common part of the cracked U and box takes 6.3 milliseconds, where it took
3.2 to come out wrong (16.3 and 8.0 on .NET Framework 4.8); the cube and the slab joined take 7.5, where they took 14.7
to be turned down (17.5 and 41.1).

**NEW.** `DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` sets INSERTs of dynamic blocks drawn in AutoCAD's Block Editor that hold
more than the library writes, where it refused them before. A stretch or a move tied to a parameter's base grip
(BaseXDelta and BaseYDelta) moves nothing when a value is set, as a value set moves the end point only. A move whose
selection holds other linear parameters carries them: AutoCAD writes their node ids (91) after the count 70 of the
action's head, which the library had read as a flag and refused; the parameter's base point and end point move by the
move, its grips with it, its distance kept, and its own actions do not follow, as it chains none (281 of 0). A frame whose
Depth from (40, 60) down to (40, 0) is set to 100 takes its bottom corners down to y -40 and carries Bottom from
(0, 0)-(100, 0) to (0, -40)-(100, -40), still 100; Bottom set next to 150 takes the bottom right corner to (150, -40), and the
INSERT's base point of Bottom, where the move took it, is not taken for a grip edit. An attribute definition a point
parameter's move holds moves in the anonymous block, and each ATTRIB of the INSERT of its tag moves by the change of that
move, carried by the INSERT's placing: Mark set from x 20 to 30 on an INSERT turned a quarter turn at the scale 2 moves
the ATTRIB 20 along y in the world, keeping a place the user gave it. A block of three linear parameters, a point
parameter, six stretches and five moves of these kinds, drawn in AutoCAD and refused before, is set now, in 2 to 4
milliseconds a set, its anonymous block at the INSERT's own values the same as the one AutoCAD saved, entity for entity to
1E-9; AutoCAD's own sets of it are yet to be checked (check v22). Still refused, nothing written: a move carrying a parameter other than a linear one, its own, or one that chains its
actions or that a scale or an array follows; a move holding a grip of a parameter it does not carry; any other action
holding a parameter; an attribute definition worked on by an action other than a move; attribute definitions of one tag
moved apart where the INSERT has an ATTRIB of that tag; and, as before, a base point a grip moved. Every other set gives
what it gave, to the bit: 839 sets of every property of every INSERT of the AutoCAD check files and samples to the value
it reads draw the same, and a drawing of the kinds the library wrote before is the same 64 670 bytes. The guide's examples
of dynamic blocks are each a block of statements of their own, of names and block names no other example uses, so that
any of them may be pasted after the first together.

**NEW.** The last kinds of AutoCAD's dynamic blocks are made in code, each written as AutoCAD 2021 saved ACadSharp's sample
of it. `DxfBlockTableRecord.AddArrayAction(linear, entities, columnSpacing)` and `AddArrayAction(xy, entities,
columnSpacing, rowSpacing)` copy entities as the distance grows, as many as the spacing goes whole into it: AutoCAD 2021
read such blocks as dynamic and, setting the values itself, drew four posts every 60 of a fence at a Length of 250 and one
at 119, one column of three rows of a plate's bolts every 25 by 20 at 40 by 70 and two bolts at 60 by 30 (check v21).
`AddAlignmentParameter(basePoint, endPoint)` and `AddBasePointParameter(location)` give the grips AutoCAD uses when the
block is placed; they give no property, and AutoCAD 2021 read them so (check v21). `AddLookupParameter(name, description,
location, inputs, rows)` gives a lookup parameter and its table, the new `DxfBlockLookupInput` (the distance of a linear
parameter, the x or the y of a point parameter) and `DxfBlockLookupRow` (a label and a value for each input): Size set to
Large sets Width to 200 and Height to 80, and Width set to 150 then reads Custom; an INSERT of the block itself, of no saved
label, reads the first row of the block's own values, Small for 100 by 50, else Custom, as AutoCAD 2021 read it (check
v21b). The edges between a lookup action and its
parameters are flagged 4, as AutoCAD's sample flags them: AutoCAD 2021 read a lookup block of edges flagged nought as no
dynamic INSERT (check v21), and read every INSERT of the blocks of edges flagged 4 as dynamic, setting Size to Small to
give 100 by 50, to Large 200 by 80, and Width to 150 to read Custom, as the library sets them (check v21b).
`DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` sets each as AutoCAD sets it: the copies of an array follow the block's entities,
each but the first tagged as AutoCAD tags its own (AcDbBlockArrayActionTag), and an XY array of a count of nought copies
nothing, as AutoCAD 2021 drew the one circle of its sample at 80 by 5. AutoCAD refused to set again an INSERT the library
had set while the copies were untagged (eInvalidInput, check v21); with the tags it set each again, the fence of four posts
at 250 to one at 119 and three at 222, the plate of 12 bolts at 100 by 70 to six at 60 by 70 (check v21b). A lookup is set
by a row's label, letters of either case the same, and reads back as the table holds it,
a space after it kept, as AutoCAD 2021 read "Size 6 " of its sample after the library set it (check v21). A lookup property
was read only before.

**NEW.** A stretch action takes an arc with one end only in its frame, numbered as AutoCAD numbers it (its start 0, its end
1), lying flat in the block: that end moves and the arc is drawn anew through its ends, keeping the height of its middle off
its chord, as AutoCAD 2021 kept 2.929 for an arc of the radius 10 whose start went from (100, 25) to (200, 25), its radius
becoming 522.13. It was refused before.

**NEW.** `AddStretchAction` and `AddMoveAction` take a distance multiplier and an angle offset, AutoCAD's Distance
Multiplier and Angle Offset (140 and 141 of the action): a mark moved of the multiplier 0.5 stays in the middle of a panel
whose Width goes from 100 to 200, and an offset of Math.PI / 2 turns a move along x to one along y, as AutoCAD 2021 read
them, the offset in radians (check v21). The overloads without them write what they wrote before.
`DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` works such actions out, keeping the offset in the INSERT's cache as AutoCAD keeps
it (AutoCAD moved along x, unturned, a circle of an INSERT whose cache held nought), and a move that lists its own
parameter's grip among what it moves, as AutoCAD's point sample and drawings from AutoCAD do, which AutoCAD 2021 read and
set right after the library set it (check v21); both were refused before.

**CHANGED.** A flip parameter is written alone in its block: `AddFlipParameter` in a block of any parameter, and any other
`Add...Parameter` in a block of a flip parameter, are refused with `NotSupportedException`, where before only an entity
both flipped and moved was refused. AutoCAD 2021 flipped a door of the flip alone both ways (check v20), but set Hand to 1
on INSERTs of a door that also had a linear parameter of no action, and of a panel whose flip and stretch held other
entities, it read 0 back each time and left the leaf as it was (checks v20b and v21).

**CHANGED.** A rotate or a scale action and a stretch or a move action of one entity are refused with
`NotSupportedException`, either given second, and `DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` refuses an INSERT of a block of
such an entity: AutoCAD 2021 worked such an entity out from where its last set left it, stretching a shaft turned a quarter
turn along x to (0, 155) for a Reach of 150 set after 200, where the block's values give (50, 105), and scaling a stretched
line to (40, 20)-(180, 20) where they give (40, 20)-(200, 20) (check v21).

**CHANGED.** `DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` refuses with `NotSupportedException`, writing nothing, an INSERT that
keeps the base point of a linear, an XY, a rotation or a flip parameter away from the block's own, beyond the point
tolerance of `Tolerance.Default`, as a grip moved it. AutoCAD's XY sample keeps such an INSERT, its base point taken from
(0, 5) to (0, 104.30) and its end point at (100.59, 0), and draws its array from there, at y 99.30 down to 19.30; the
library, which works a block out from its own base points, drew it at 0 down to -80. Of 844 properties of the INSERTs of
AutoCAD's samples, of the files of checks v17 to v21b with AutoCAD's saves of them, and of a user's drawing, each set to the
value it reads, the 16 of that INSERT, two in each of the eight files that hold it, are refused now, and the others draw
what they drew or are refused as they were.

**NEW.** The other dynamic blocks of AutoCAD's Block Editor are made in code, each written as AutoCAD 2021 saved
ACadSharp's sample of it, its graph number for number. `DxfBlockTableRecord.AddPointParameter(name, description,
location)` gives a block a position, the properties Tag X and Tag Y of a parameter named Tag, and `AddMoveAction(point,
entities)` moves entities with it: a tag circle at (80, 20) goes to (120, 20) as Tag X is set to 120.
`AddRotationParameter(name, description, basePoint, radius, angle)` gives an angle in radians about a base point, and
`AddRotateAction(rotation, entities)` turns entities by it: an arrow from (50, 25) to (80, 25) set to Math.PI / 2 points
to (50, 55). `AddFlipParameter(name, description, basePoint, endPoint)` gives a reflection line, the property 0 or 1, and
`AddFlipAction(flip, entities)` mirrors entities about it: a door leaf from (0, 0) to (90, 0) flipped about the y axis runs
to (-90, 0). `AddXYParameter(xName, xDescription, yName, yDescription, basePoint, endPoint)` gives the distances along x
and y to an end point, with four grips, and `AddStretchAction(xy, ...)` and `AddMoveAction(xy, entities)` follow its end
point both ways: Width 160 and Depth 80 take the corner (100, 50) of a plate to (160, 80). A linear parameter is given
`AddMoveAction(linear, entities)`, the entities following its end point (a circle at (90, 25) goes to (190, 25) at Width
200), and `AddScaleAction(linear, entities)`, the entities scaled alike about its base point by the distance over the
block's own (a disc of the radius 25 at (50, 25) is of the radius 50 at (100, 50) at Size 200). Each returns, or takes,
the new `DxfBlockPointParameter`, `DxfBlockRotationParameter`, `DxfBlockFlipParameter` or `DxfBlockXYParameter`.
`DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` sets each on an INSERT as AutoCAD sets it, the actions worked out in the order
they were added into the anonymous block the INSERT places, and the cache records of each kind written as AutoCAD writes
them; an angle is taken into a turn, a flip state is a whole number 0 or 1 read back as a `short`. A drawing of 1 000
INSERTs takes about half a millisecond for a set under .NET 10 and one under .NET Framework 4.8. ezdxf 1.4.5 recovers and
audits the files of AutoCAD check v20 with nothing to fix, where AutoCAD 2021 read and set the move, the scale, the point,
the flip and the XY blocks right. A scale or a rotate is written with 1012 nought, as AutoCAD's samples write it: AutoCAD
adds 1012 to the base point, and turned an arrow about (100, 50) instead of (50, 25) while the library wrote the base point
there. A polar parameter and its polar stretch are not written.

**NEW.** A stretch action takes, besides lines and polylines, an arc with both its ends in the frame, a circle by its
centre, a text by the point it is held by, a multiline text by its location and an INSERT by its insertion point, each
moving whole, numbered as AutoCAD's files number them (an arc 0 and 1, the others 0); a text aligned or fitted between two
points, an attribute definition and an INSERT of rows and columns are refused.
A frame over the right side of a rectangle 100 by 50 set to Width 200 moves an arc, a circle, two texts, a multiline text
and an INSERT there by 100 along x.

**CHANGED.** A value of a linear parameter half way between two steps of an increment set goes to the step below, as
AutoCAD 2021 took it in plugin v19: 85 to 80 (from 250), 65 to 60 (from 80) and 75 to 70 (from 60) of 50 to 300 by 10,
where the library took 85 to 90 and 65 to 70 before, by the even step; AutoCAD check v20 took all seven further ties so. A
value half way between two values of a list goes to the one farther from the value the property had, beyond the value asked
in the way it changes: of 50, 100 ... 300, 125 to 100 from 300 and 225 to 250 from 50, as AutoCAD 2021 took 8 of the 11 ties
of check v20, where the library took the one nearer the old value before. AutoCAD was not consistent here: it took the
other value in the other three, and in three of the four ties of the rounds before.

**NEW.** `new DxfDatabase(version)` makes a new drawing with nothing in it, of the version named as `Version` names one:
AC1015 (R2000), AC1018, AC1021, AC1024 (R2010), AC1027 or AC1032 (R2018), as AutoCAD's `new Database(true, true)` makes one
of its own. It is the drawing `DxfWriter` writes with no shape, in millimetres, its header naming the version, so that a
dynamic block, which wants R2010 or later, is made from nothing: `new DxfDatabase("AC1024")`. `new DxfDatabase("AC1015")` is
the very text of `DxfDatabase.Parse(new DxfWriter().ToString())`; a version of R12 to R14 is refused. A later version gives
its records what that version added to them, as AutoCAD's own saves give them: from R2004 on each class says how many
objects of it there are (91), without which AutoCAD 2021 opens no drawing of R2004 or later ("Group 91 (db instance count)
expected", which it gave for the five such drawings and for every dynamic block made in them before this was written), and
each layout gives its shade plot (76 to 78); from R2007 on model space and paper space give their unit, explodability and
scaling (70, 280, 281). ezdxf 1.4.5 recovers and audits each of the six with nothing to fix.

**NEW.** `DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` is set, as AutoCAD's `DynamicBlockReferenceProperty.Value` sets it, on the
distance of a linear parameter whose actions are stretches of lines and polylines and on the state of a visibility
parameter. The value is taken to the value set as AutoCAD 2021 took it (plugins v17 and v18): of 50 to 300 by 10, 75 to 70,
77 to 80 and 400 to 300; of the list 50, 100 ... 300, 75 to 100 from 100, a tie going to the value nearer the one the
property had. The block is then worked out at the values of all its properties into an anonymous block of AutoCAD's (`*U1`
and on) the INSERT places, the points each stretch holds moved and each entity a visibility parameter governs shown or
hidden, and the INSERT's representation data and the cache AutoCAD reads the values from (ACAD_ENHANCEDBLOCKDATA) are
written as AutoCAD writes them when it sets a value, with no history. A rectangle 100 by 50 whose Width is set to 200 places
a copy with its right edge at x = 200 and reads Width 200 back; the dynamic block keeps 100. A property of another kind, or
of a block holding other parameters or actions, is refused with `NotSupportedException`. Setting Width takes under a
millisecond.

**NEW.** `DxfBlockTableRecord.AddVisibilityParameter(name, description, location, states)` gives a block a visibility
parameter, its states each a new `DxfBlockVisibilityState` of a name and the entities shown in it, as AutoCAD 2021 saved
the visibility parameter of ACadSharp's sample, its graph of four nodes and three edges number for number. Each INSERT shows
the first state until its property is set, and the block is kept in that state; an entity named in no state is shown in
every state. A sign of a frame, a cross and a tick given the states Cross, Tick and Blank shows the cross in Cross, the
tick in Tick and neither in Blank, the frame in all three. A block takes one visibility parameter, and linear parameters
besides. 23 new tests (32 cases) in `DxfDynamicBlockD24cTests` for the three.

**NEW.** A dynamic block is made in code. `DxfBlockTableRecord.AddLinearParameter(name, description, basePoint, endPoint,
labelOffset, valueSet)` gives a block of a drawing of R2010 or later a linear parameter, the property of its name on every
INSERT of the block, its values free or held by the new `DxfBlockParameterValueSet` (`Increments(minimum, maximum,
increment)` or `List(values)`), and returns the new `DxfBlockLinearParameter`; `AddStretchAction(parameter, frameCorner,
oppositeCorner, entities)` ties lines and polylines to it, the points inside the frame moving as the distance grows. The
block is written as AutoCAD's Block Editor saves one, its extended data, entity tags, evaluation graph with both grips,
purge preventer and classes; a block may hold several parameters, each with its actions. A rectangle 100 by 50 given Width
from 50 to 300 by 10 and the stretch of its right edge comes out with the graph AutoCAD 2021 saved of the same block
written by a script, number for number, which AutoCAD read as dynamic, stretched to x = 200 for a Width of 200, and kept
through a DXF and a DWG saved and opened again (plugin v17); every INSERT reads `Width = 100.0` through
`DynamicBlockReferencePropertyCollection`, and ezdxf 1.4.5 recovers and audits the files with no error. An INSERT shows the
block's own distance until its property is set. Other parameters and actions, other entities and a frame of a polygon are
not written. 11 new tests.

**NEW.** `DxfBlockReference.DynamicBlockReferencePropertyCollection` reads the dynamic properties of an INSERT of a dynamic
block as AutoCAD saved them, read only: each a `DxfDynamicBlockReferenceProperty` with AutoCAD's `PropertyName`, `Value`,
`PropertyTypeCode`, `UnitsType` (the new `DxfDynamicBlockReferencePropertyUnitsType`), `ReadOnly`, `Description` and
`GetAllowedValues()`. Each parameter of the block's evaluation graph gives its own, in the order of the graph: a linear one
its distance, a polar one its distance and angle, an XY one its distances along x and y, a rotation one its angle, a point
one its position's x and y, a flip one 0 or 1, a visibility one its state with every state allowed, a lookup one the value
its table gives. The value is the one AutoCAD saved for the INSERT in its representation data, else the block's own: of
ACadSharp's ten samples saved by AutoCAD, the linear parameter reads 5 for the block and 7.5 for the INSERT AutoCAD
stretched, the rotation one 90 and 50 degrees (in radians), as acadrust reads them. Lengths are scaled by the largest of
the INSERT's scale factors, as AutoCAD 2021 read 7.5 as 22.5 at the scale (2, 3, 2), where an INSERT scaled unlike along
its axes is not `IsDynamicBlock`, as AutoCAD read it; a value set's list is allowed only under the flags 8, as AutoCAD
gave none under 1, 2 or 4. AutoCAD (plugin v16) read the same names, values, types, units, flags, descriptions and allowed
values on every sample and on a user's drawing, leaving out its hidden `Origin` points as the library does. Nothing is
worked out anew, nor set. The five properties of ACadSharp's lookup sample, a graph of 19 nodes, are read in 41
microseconds an INSERT under .NET 10 and 86 under .NET Framework 4.8. 16 new tests, 1 changed (an INSERT of BOLT scaled
(1.5, -1.5, 2) is not `IsDynamicBlock`).

**FIXED.** A curved loop in space filleted, chamfered or moved sideways by `GeoPolygonArc3.Fillet`, `Chamfer`,
`TryFilletAt`, `TryChamferAt` or `Offset` keeps what the same work keeps on the loop in its plane: every arc however
small, every cut and side the tolerance keeps, and a corner named by its vertex. The loop was laid out in its plane and
put back together within the global tolerance, which dropped a side shorter than a thousandth that the loop kept within
a finer tolerance, and the arcs and cuts the plane now keeps: at a millionth, the rectangle 100 by 50 standing in the
plane x = 20 filleted at 0.0005 came back its four corners, 0.0625 square units short, and the loop (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0),
(10.0004, 0.0004, 0), (10.0004, 10, 0), (0, 10, 0) asked to round vertex 3 rounded (0, 10, 0). Of 7 982 convex loops
standing in planes at random, half with a corner cut off by a side between six tolerances and 0.0009 long, worked at
tolerances from a billionth to a tenth, 3 192 came out other than the same work in the plane and 139 threw; none does
now, and those off the area the corners give went from 2 030 to 125 (offsets of a distance about the tolerance, and
sides lost inside the offset in the plane). Loops whose work leaves nothing shorter than the global tolerance are the
same to the bit, and so is every offset of a loop of long sides; a fillet or a cut below a thousandth is kept at the
global and coarser tolerances, as in the plane. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** A straight loop in space rounded by `Corner3.Fillet` or `TryFilletAt` into a `GeoPolygonArc3` is read corner
for corner, a side shorter than the global tolerance and all, so a corner is named by its vertex. It was read through
the constructor, which drops such a side first: at a millionth, the loop (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10.0004, 0.0004, 0),
(10.0004, 10, 0), (0, 10, 0) filleted at 0.0001 came back its four corners, the side 0.00057 long and its two arcs gone.
Of 2 404 such loops, 1 187 came out other than the same work in the plane and 64 threw; none does now. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** A chain or loop that may curve, grown or shrunk by `Offset2.Offset` with miters or chamfers, reads what a
miter fills within the tolerance given, however small the miter. A miter smaller than the global tolerance went unread,
and a piece inside it was kept: a chain of nine corners some 0.005 across, grown by 0.00137 at a billionth, came out with
a stray piece 0.00004 long beside the chain the same shape a million times larger gives within a thousandth. Of 62 000
stars and wavy rings, open and closed, grown and shrunk with miters, limited miters and chamfers at tolerances from
nought to a tenth, 2 answers changed, both at a finer tolerance than a thousandth and both now as the larger shape; none
changed at the global tolerance or a coarser one. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** A loop in the plane filleted or chamfered by `Corner2.Fillet`, `Chamfer`, `TryFilletAt` or `TryChamferAt`, or
the members of `GeoPolygonArc2` that call them, and a loop grown or shrunk by `Offset2.Offset` keeping its arcs, keeps
every arc and every cut the work leaves, as a chain does, and every side the tolerance keeps; only its corners are
counted within the tolerance. The loop was put back together within the global tolerance, which dropped an arc or a cut
shorter than a thousandth, or a side the loop had kept within a finer tolerance, and ran the next side on from the
corner before: the rectangle 100 by 50 filleted at 0.0005 came back its four corners, 0.0625 square units short, where
the chain round the same corners kept its three arcs, and grown by 0.0004 with round joins at a millionth it came back
without its arcs. Of 24 000 convex loops, half with a side cut off a corner between six tolerances and 0.0009 long,
rounded, cut or grown at tolerances from nought to a tenth, 3 864 rounded or cut came out of the area the corners give
and 1 712 grown or shrunk; 216 and 1 120 do now, the same as before (a fillet at a tolerance of nought, refused corner
by corner, and offsets of a distance about the tolerance). Loops whose work leaves nothing shorter than the global
tolerance are the same to the bit; at a tolerance coarser than it, an offset is the same to the bit, and a fillet or a
single cut keeps an arc or a cut it dropped below a thousandth, as the chain does. 7 new tests, 1 changed (the rectangle
filleted at 0.0005 at a ten-thousandth keeps its four arcs).

**FIXED.** A straight chain or loop filleted by `Corner2.Fillet` or `TryFilletAt`, or the `Fillet` of `GeoPolyline2` and
`GeoPolygon2`, is rounded corner for corner, a leg shorter than the global tolerance and all, so a corner is named by
its vertex. The chain was read as a curved one through the constructor, which drops such a leg first: at a millionth,
the chain (0, 0), (10, 0), (10.0004, 0.0004), (10.0004, 10), (0, 10) asked to round vertex 3 by 1 answered false, vertex
3 being its end once the leg 0.00057 long was gone. Of 24 000 chains and loops with a leg from a twentieth of the
tolerance to 1 long, 10 233 came out other than the same work on the chain read corner for corner and 372 threw; none
does now. Legs longer than the global tolerance give the same bits. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** The shortest line from a curved loop in space, `GeoPolygonArc3.GetShortestLineTo`, to a chain, a polygon, a
face or another curved loop in its plane is measured to every side the other shape has, however short. The other shape
was laid out in the loop's plane within the global tolerance, which dropped a side shorter than a thousandth that the
shape kept within a finer tolerance: at a millionth, the square 10 by 10 at the origin read 0.5004 from the polygon
(10.5004, 5), (16, 2), (16, 8), (10.5, 5), where it is 0.5. Of 16 000 such shapes at tolerances from a ten-millionth to
0.03, 6 192 were measured off the exact distance, 2 730 by more than the tolerance; none is now, and shapes of sides
longer than the global tolerance give the same bits. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** A loop in the plane cut along a chain or by a line, by `Splition2.TrySplitBy` or the `TrySplitBy` of
`GeoPolygon2`, is cut at the tolerance asked, corner for corner, as a polygon in space is. The loop, the chain and the
pieces went into space and back through constructors that read the global tolerance, which dropped a side shorter than a
thousandth before the cut was asked and a side of a piece shorter than that after it. At a millionth, a chain starting on a
side 0.00057 long was refused, a chain ending 0.0005 from a corner gave a piece that lost the place it ended and 0.0025
square units with it, and a loop or a cut-off corner smaller than a thousandth threw; the line through (0.0005, 0) and
(0, 0.0005) now cuts the square 10 by 10 at the origin into its corner, a triangle of 0.000000125 square units, and the
rest. Of 18 000 polygons, half of them in the plane, cut along a chain from mid-side, beside a corner or on one at
tolerances from a millionth to 0.03, 337 in the plane started or ended the cut off its place and 2 started it apart in the
two pieces; of 12 000 with sides and ends from six tolerances to 0.0009 long or away, at tolerances from a ten-millionth to
a ten-thousandth, 1 598 in the plane lost area, 699 started or ended apart and 47 threw. Of 16 000 loops cut by a line, 723
threw, 3 211 of sides longer than the tolerance lost area and 5 850 came out other than the same cut in space. None does
now, but for 4 chain cuts and 3 line cuts whose pieces add up to more than the loop, as 3 chain cuts in space do; a loop cut
by a line gives the answer of space to the bit. Loops of sides longer than the global tolerance cut from mid-side, across
or on a corner are the same to the bit, and both cuts take 7 to 19 % less time. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** A polygon cut along a chain by `Splition3.TrySplitBy` or the `TrySplitBy` of `GeoPolygon3`, and a loop in the
plane by `Splition2.TrySplitBy` or the `TrySplitBy` of `GeoPolygon2`, is cut from a corner where an end of the chain meets
the outline within the tolerance of it, as a polyline cut within the tolerance of a vertex is: both pieces keep the corner,
and they add up to the polygon. The corner was cut off, and the two pieces could start the cut at different places. At a
hundredth, the square 10 by 10 cut from (0.004, 0, 0) to (10, 5, 0) gives the triangle of 25 square units from the corner
(0, 0, 0) and the rest, of 75, where the rest ran from (0, 10, 0) straight to (0.004, 0, 0) and a sliver of 0.02 square
units was in neither piece. Of two corners within the tolerance the nearer is taken, and a chain whose two ends land on one
corner is refused, as it meets the outline at one place. Of 12 000 polygons, in space and in the plane, cut from mid-side,
beside a corner or on one at tolerances from a millionth to 0.03, 3 081 of the 3 222 cut beside a corner of sides longer
than the tolerance lost more than a billionth of their area, and 15 cut beside a side shorter than the tolerance started
the cut in the two pieces up to 1.3 tolerances apart; none does. An answer moves by the snap, at most the tolerance; cut
from mid-side it is the same to the bit. One chain from beside a corner to the far end of a side shorter than the
tolerance, running within the tolerance of the outline, is now refused. 9 new tests, 1 changed: a polygon cut from beside
a side 0.006 long at a hundredth meets the outline at a corner of the side, not at the foot of the chain.

**FIXED.** A segment in the plane shorter than the global tolerance, cut within a tolerance finer than that by
`Splition2.TrySplitBy` or the `TrySplitBy` of `GeoLine2`, is cut where a point, a line, lines, a polyline, points or polygons
cut it: the place was measured at the global tolerance, which reads a segment no longer than that as its start, so it came
out nought along and the segment came back whole. At a billionth, the segment from (5, 0.0004) to (5, -0.0005) is cut at
(5, 0) by the point (5, 0) or by the line from (4, 0) to (6, 0). Of 2 634 segments from four tolerances to the global one
