long, at tolerances from a billionth to a ten-thousandth, each cut those six ways, 15 543 cuts were not made; every one is,
at the place.
The 32 196 answers for segments longer than the global tolerance are the same to the bit. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** A polyline cut at a distance in space, by `SplitAtDistances` or any cut that goes through it (by a point, a
plane, a polygon, a face, a box or a body), ends its last piece where the polyline ends however short its last leg: a last
leg no longer than the tolerance takes the corner before it, as a first one is taken by the start. At a hundredth, the
polyline from (0, 0, 0) to (10, 0, 0) and on to (10, 0.006, 0) cut at 5 ended its second piece at the corner (10, 0, 0)
and lost the end; it ends at (10, 0.006, 0). Cut at 9.995, which would leave only that leg after the cut, it came back as
one piece ending at the corner, and comes back whole. Of 4 000 cuts of polylines with a leg shorter than the tolerance, 539
lost the end; none does, no piece is shorter than the tolerance, and the answers with no short last leg are the same to
the bit. 3 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GetDistanceAtPoint` and `GetParameterAtPoint` of `GeoPolyline3` and `GeoPolygon3` (and of
`Parametrization3`) read a side as it is however short, as the closest point does, where a side no longer than the
tolerance was read as its start; so do those of `GeoPolyline2`, `GeoPolygon2`, `GeoTriangle2` and `GeoRectangle2`, which
read a side shorter than the global tolerance so. At a hundredth, the polyline (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0.006, 0),
(0, 0.006, 0) put (10.03, 0.003, 0) 10 along, at the start of the leg 0.006 long; it puts it 10.003 along, halfway. A
polygon cut by a chain from beside such a side meets its outline at the chain's foot, where it met it at the side's start,
and a 2D polyline is cut on such a leg where a point on it or a line crossing it asks, where it was cut at the leg's start.
Against an exact oracle, 5 898 of 51 632 answers in space and 4 796 of 25 592 in the plane put the point farther than the
nearest, and 1 830 of 2 116 cuts of a 2D polyline on a leg between the tolerance and the global one were made more than
the tolerance off; none is. Of 4 796 polygons cut from beside a short side, 1 194 met the outline away from the foot, 15
do, where the foot lies within the tolerance of a corner. The answers for sides longer than the tolerance are the same
to the bit. 9 new tests.

**FIXED.** In space, a polyline, a polygon or a face gives a point beside a side its closest point on the side as it is
however short, as its shortest line already did: `Projection3.ProjectToPolyline`, `ProjectToPolygonBoundary`,
`ProjectToPolygon` and `ProjectToFace`, `GetClosestPointOnBoundary` of `GeoPolyline3`, `GeoPolygon3` and `GeoFace3`, and
the members of `GeoPoint3` that answer the same. A side no longer than the tolerance offered its start: at a hundredth, the
polygon (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0.006, 0), (0, 10, 0) gave (10.03, 0.003, 0) the closest point (10, 0, 0), 0.0301496
away; it gives (10, 0.003, 0), 0.03 away. In the plane, `GeoBvh2.GetClosestPoint` and `DistanceTo(GeoPoint2)` read a
straight edge so, as a curved chain does, and an arc within the tolerance as before: the index over the polygon (0, 0),
(10, 0), (10, 0.006), (0, 10) gives (10.03, 0.003) the point (10, 0.003), 0.03 away, where it gave (10, 0). Of 10 824
points beside a short side of a random polyline, polygon or face, 1 176 were given a closest point farther than the exact
distance, and none is; of 12 988 beside a short edge of an index, 2 260, and none is. Whether a point lies on a face, which
the booleans read, and the shortest line from a ray still take the side's start, to the bit, and so does
`ProjectToSolid`, found within 3E-10 of the exact distance beside such sides. Shapes whose sides are all longer than the
tolerance answer as before, to the bit; the index's closest point takes 3 to 6 % longer, one more look at each edge. 4 new
tests.

**FIXED.** In space, a polyline cut at distances starts every piece where the one before it ended, on the polyline, and

corner the first ended at; both meet at the corner. A cut on a leg no longer than the tolerance is made where the piece
before it ends, and the pieces keep what the tolerance asked keeps: at a billionth, a piece 0.0005 long between two cuts
threw, rebuilt at the global thousandth. Cut by a point, a plane, a polygon, a face or a box, a segment or a leg no longer
than the global tolerance was measured from its start: at a billionth, the segment from (5, 5, 0.0004) to
(5, 5, -0.0005) came back whole from the top of the box 10 by 10 by 10 standing under the floor, and is cut at (5, 5, 0).
Of 4 000 random polylines cut at a seed, 1 021 started a piece off the polyline, by up to 0.92 of the tolerance, 2 271
left pieces apart, and 44 threw; none does. Of 1 803 segments and legs between the tolerance and the global one, 1 712
were cut off the crossing or not at all, and none is. Pieces whose cuts lie further than the tolerance from every corner
and whose legs are all longer than the global tolerance, and segments longer than it, answer as before, to the bit; `SplitAtDistances` takes 40 % less time, its pieces
no longer rebuilt. 8 new tests.

**FIXED.** In the plane, a straight polygon, polyline, face or triangle gives a point beside a side its closest point on
the side as it is however short, as a curved chain or loop has since the entry below: `Projection2.ProjectToPolygon`,

point of a triangle read the global tolerance so: the triangle (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 0.0006) gave (10.03, 0.0003) the
side's start, and gives the foot (10, 0.0003). Of 3 000 random polygons, polylines, faces and triangles with a side
shorter than tolerances from 1E-6 to 3E-2, 4 246 answers broke against the exact distance, and none does; a segment you
give no longer than the tolerance, joined from its start, is joined to such a side as it is, by a line no longer than it
was. Shapes whose sides are all longer than the tolerance answer as before, to the bit, in the time they took. 4 new
tests; 1 test that pinned the start now expects the side.

**FIXED.** In space, a short leg of a polyline crosses a body where `TrySplitBy` cuts the polyline, and a short side of

(5, 5, -0.005) and on level to (8, 5, -0.005) met it nowhere, and meets it at (5, 5, 0). A chain whose corner comes
within the tolerance of a region is still given the corner. Of 8 000 random chains, loops and polylines a seed against a
box and its top, 956 of 956 whose short side alone passes through the region met nothing, and none does; 187 of 193
polylines cut by a box through a leg no longer than the tolerance came back whole or cut further off than the tolerance,
and none does; of those whose leg is between the tolerance and the global one, 120 of 140, and 7 do, each a piece within

**FIXED.** In the plane, a curved chain or loop, `GeoPolylineArc2` or `GeoPolygonArc2`, gives a point beside a straight

its reading near the centre of its arc; a polygon and a polyline in the plane follow in the entry above. Of 3 000 random chains and loops a seed with a straight side shorter than tolerances from 1E-6 to
3E-2, 5 268 and 5 292 answers in the plane and 1 660 and 1 660 in space broke against the exact distance, and none does.
Chains whose sides are all longer than the tolerance answer as before, to the bit, in the time they took. 4 new tests;
1 test that pinned the start now expects the side.

**FIXED.** In space, a side of a shape crosses the surface of a body as the side it is. A triangle, a polygon or a face
with a side shorter than the global tolerance, asked at a finer one, crossed a body at that side's start: at a billionth,

box; it crosses it, and `TrySplitBy` cuts it, at (5, 5, 0). Of 3 000 random regions a seed against a box, 597 and 633
answers named the crossing of the short side further off than the tolerance, and none does; of 3 000 chains, loops and
polylines a seed whose short side alone crosses the top of a box, 617 and 586 named nothing within the tolerance of it,
and none does. Regions whose sides are all longer than the global tolerance, and chains whose sides are all longer than
the point one, cross as before, to the bit, in the time they took. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** In space, a segment you give is measured against the tolerance you ask for where the global one was read in

and to a segment longer than the global tolerance is as before, to the bit: none of 883 200 moved. Each takes the time
it took. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** A curved chain or loop, `GeoPolylineArc3` or `GeoPolygonArc3`, touches a shape by the gap to each straight
side as it is however short, as `DistanceTo` measures it, and gives its closest point to a point on such a side. A

some 10 % longer, and up to 9 % longer on .NET Framework 4.8 against a polygon or a face, as each side is asked first
whether it is short; the closest point 8 % longer there. 3 new tests.

(0.006, 0.02, 5), (3, 3, 5) by a line 0.0209 long, to its corner, and is joined by one 0.02 long, to its short side, as

**FIXED.** In space, `GetIntersections` and `TryIntersectWith` read a segment you give, a `GeoLine3` or a straight

its start; it meets each at its start. Of the 368 intersection queries in space that take a segment, asked about four
stubs, 808 answers broke that rule and none does now; of 33 600 random stubs and segments a seed aimed at every shape in
space, some 15 300 answers a seed broke it, and none does now. A segment longer than the tolerance, a line or a ray cut
past a shape, and the sides of chains, polylines, boxes and bodies crossed inside the library, splitting and cutting
among them, are read as before, to the bit: of 347 962 answers to longer segments none moved, nor any of 100 800
intersections of shapes with a side shorter than the tolerance. Two segments longer than the tolerance are crossed in 0.10
microseconds where 0.07 on .NET 10, and in the time they took on .NET Framework 4.8; every other longer segment in the
time it took. A stub takes longer, as its true meeting is looked for first: against a polygon of 40 sides 0.46
microseconds where 0.005 on .NET 10. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** In space, `GetShortestLineTo` joins a segment, a ray, a point or a ball to a side of a polygon, a triangle, a
face, a polyline or a body, and two triangles' sides to each other, as the side it is however short, as `DistanceTo`
measures it. A side no longer than the point tolerance was read as its start: at a hundredth, the chain from (-7, -7, 0)

standing up through it, by a line 0.0201 long from the corner (0.008, 0, 0), where they are 0.02 from its short side; so

lines 0.02 long. `Distance3.DistanceTo(GeoPolyline3, GeoPoint3)`, and with it the distance of a point and of a ball to a
polyline and `Containment3.IsPointOn(GeoPolyline3, GeoPoint3)`, measured the chain so too, and measures each side as it
is, as the plane does. Of 10 500 random shapes with a side 1E-4 to 1E-2 long beside 15 kinds of shape, 2 692 lines and
distances broke and 722 do, all of them read on purpose or left for later: a plane and a box reading a shape within the
tolerance as on them, a foot kept within the tolerance past the rim of a face of a body, a polygon joined to a polyline
through its triangles, and the closest point of a curved chain or loop. Shapes whose sides are all longer than the
tolerance are joined as before, to the bit, and so are the triangles of a body's index, which the clash reads. Each line
takes the time it took, but a polyline's to a ray: 2.35 microseconds where 2.0 on .NET 10, as it was on .NET Framework
4.8. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `DxfSpline.FitData` set on a closed spline keeps it closed, where fit data not periodic opened it, and gives
it the flags 32 and 1024 of fit data, as AutoCAD 2021 does: its closed cubic of 70 1035 given fit data not periodic, a
fit point moved, was saved 70 1067, closed, where the library wrote 70 8, open. Fit data set periodic give AutoCAD's
periodic spline through the points taken round, each point on the curve at its knot and the knots the lengths of the
chords, clamped into as many control points as the points and 3 and written 70 3115 with no fit points, tangents or fit
tolerance, its fit points read back as the points at its knots; AutoCAD's control points of its 1035 and 3115 given
periodic fit data are the library's to 1E-14, where the library wrote a closed spline of 70 9 up to 3 off them. The
periodic spline is the cubic whatever degree is asked, as AutoCAD wrote its cubic asked a degree 2 through (0, 0),
(40, 0), (50, 30) and (10, 25), an even degree through an even count of points; three points give a quadratic and two a
line there and back. Where two of the points are one, within 1E-3, which make no periodic spline, the closed spline is fitted
as before. Of 4 000 random rings of 3 to 60 points, degree 1 to 10 asked, sizes 0.01 to a million and up to a million
from the origin, every one of distinct points fits the periodic cubic and reads periodic with its fit points within
7.9E-16 of its size; 5 000 points are fitted in 50 milliseconds. Setting the fit data takes what it took, 0.6
milliseconds with the reading of the drawing on .NET Framework 4.8. 5 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfSpline.SetNurbsData`, `NurbsData` set and the constructor write the flags 1 and 2 of group 70 as
AutoCAD 2021 writes them: a curve whose ends meet is closed, the flag 1, and one that leaves its start in the direction
it reaches its end, within 1E-12 of a radian whatever its size, has the flag 2 as well, whatever `closed` and `periodic`
say; the flags 32 and 1024 of fit data go with the fit data. AutoCAD's closed cubic of 70 11 given its own NURBS data
not periodic, or not closed, was saved 70 11 and read closed, where the library wrote 9 and 8, and with its seam turned
by a hundredth of a degree, or by a hundred-millionth (1.75E-10 of a radian), saved 70 9: its closed splines of the flag
2 turn by 4E-16 of a radian at most. Its periodic
cubic of 70 3115 given its own data back was saved 70 2059, where the library wrote 2091. A curve closed round a corner
is written 1, as AutoCAD wrote its 1065 of a corner at the seam. `periodic` still puts the flag 2 on any curve, and the
flag 2048 is kept or taken off by it as before. What writes NURBS data anew (raising the degree, putting control points
in and out, cutting, `Spline`) follows the same rule. No polyline made of a spline in the AutoCAD checks moved, to the
bit. 5 new tests, 1 changed to AutoCAD's answers.

**CHANGED.** `DxfSpline.IsPeriodic` is true where the flag 2048 of group 70 is set on a curve that runs on round its
seam, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: its 2059 with the control point 1 moved down by 5, or the point 5 up by 5, a corner at
the seam, read as not periodic, 7 control points and 11 knots, and so did its 2059 of a control point moved by a
millionth. The seam is read as AutoCAD's periodic form is made, the curve unclamped at its start and at its end, the
first degree of its points the same as the degree a period on, within 1E-10, AutoCAD's own point tolerance, and 1E-14 of
the spline's size, one and its largest coordinate, for rounding: AutoCAD's periodic splines, a rational one among them,
are so to 1.3E-15 of theirs, and stay so scaled to millions or moved far from the origin; of its 2059 of size 61.5 with
a control point moved it read the seam off by 4.1E-11 as periodic and off by 4.1E-10 as not.
`IsPeriodic` of a spline of the flag 2048 takes 5.7 microseconds where 1.5 on .NET Framework 4.8, and 2.6 where 0.6 on
.NET 10; of any other spline, what it took. 4 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.IsLinked` of a cell in no range linked in the TABLECONTENT is true where the cell's state there has
the flag 4 of a linked cell and the cell holds a content (its 95 above nought), as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: the title (0, 0)
of Parts and a cell of data (2, 1) of no text, given the state 4 beside a range over (1, 0) to (1, 1), it read as linked
with no range and no link, where the library read them not linked; (0, 1) of the state 4 and no content it read as not
linked, as before. `IsLinked` of the six cells takes what it took, 0.9 microseconds on .NET Framework 4.8 and 1.5 on .NET
10. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** In space, `GetShortestLineTo` reads a segment you give, a `GeoLine3` no longer than the point tolerance, as
its start where it does not truly meet the other shape, and joins it where it does, as `DistanceTo` has read it and as

0.0006 above the square 10 by 10 in the floor, was joined to it from its end by a line 0.0006 long, and so to a
triangle, a face, a body and a ray so aimed; it is joined from its start by one 0.0015 long, as long as its distance.
The one from (5, 5, 0.0004) to (5, 5, -0.0005), passing through the square, was joined from its start by a line 0.0004
long, and so to a segment, a polyline, a line without ends or a ray it crossed; it is joined by a line of no length
where it passes. One pointing at a side of the square in its plane, from (10.0015, 5, 0) to (10.0006, 5, 0), was joined
by a line of no length; it is joined from its start. A ball read a stub reaching into it as its start, 0.0004 from it
where it is nought, and a spline read one by its nearer end in `DistanceTo`, `CollidesWith` and `GetShortestLineTo`;
both read it as every other shape does now, and a straight `GeoEdge3` that short with it. Of the 736 queries in space
that take a segment, asked about four stubs, 178 answers broke that rule and 34 do now, all of a plane, which measures a
segment exactly by its nearer end, or of a point, measured to a stub's start. Of 112 000 random segments aimed at every
shape in space, four in five of them stubs, asked either way round at a thousandth and a hundredth and out to 100 000,
47 264 answers broke it and none does now. A side of a shape, however short, a segment longer than the tolerance, the
plane, the point and `GetIntersections` are read as before, to the bit: of the 2 944 000 answers, none to a longer
segment moved. The shortest line between two segments longer than the tolerance takes 0.054 microseconds where 0.029 on
.NET 10, and 0.08 where 0.07 on .NET Framework 4.8, and from a ray 0.05 where 0.035; every other is asked in the time it
took. A stub takes longer, as its true meeting is looked for first: against a polygon of 40 sides 2.2 microseconds
where 1.5, and against a segment 0.05 where 0.01. 7 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GeoBvh2.DistanceTo(GeoBvh2)` and `CollidesWith(GeoBvh2)` measure every edge of the two indexes as the side of
a shape it is, however short, as the shapes measure their sides. They measured the edges as segments you give, so a
straight edge no longer than the point tolerance was read as its start: at a thousandth, the index over the chain coming
down from (5, 5) to (5, 0.0015) and on to (5, 0.0006) was 0.0015 from the one over the segment from the origin to
(10, 0), and did not collide with it, where the two chains are 0.0006 apart and collide. Of 78 916 random pairs of
indexes over polylines, polygons, chains, loops, faces and rings of edges with sides shorter than the tolerance, at a
thousandth and a hundredth, 3 486 distances and 445 collisions differed from the shapes' own, and none does now; no pair
without such a side moved, to the bit, and the two take the time they took. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part and a difference of a body whose openings, cut in at once as a boolean cuts them, come
out open are worked out again on the material `TryCutOpenings` gives, asked at a millionth or below. The planes of an
opening cut only the pieces of the body its box reaches, and a piece beside one so cut kept a face the other's faces did
not match: a plate 200 by 100 by 3 with two blind openings up from its floor whose ceilings stood 0.00095 apart, at the

across both openings held 22 717.96, 1.05 short, and was not valid, and the two joined were not worked out; both hold
what they should now. What the operation gives worked out again is taken where what came as before is not made, not
valid, or holds another volume than it, beyond the planar tolerance and the rounding of the coordinates times its area.
Of 12 000 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with two or three openings whose walls stood 0.000 15 to 0.03
apart and boxes, turned about in space or not, at nought, 1E-12, the rounding, 1E-9 and 1E-6, the 6 020 at the origin
and up to a million out held 221 wrong and trusted, 806 not worked out and 751 not valid; 38, 55 and 21 do now, and none
that was right came out otherwise. Further out, where rounding moves a corner off a plane by more than a millionth and
the material cannot tell such walls apart, worked out again 106 that were not worked out or not valid came out wrong and
trusted; there only what came out made and valid is worked out again, and 125 of 780 wrong and trusted are right. Asked
above a millionth, the default tolerance among it, a boolean is worked out as it was, to the bit, in the time it took.
At a millionth and below, a boolean of a body with openings takes two fifths to a half longer, on .NET 10 and on .NET
Framework 4.8, its openings cut in at once to look: the four booleans of a plate with twelve holes and a box 18.5
milliseconds at a millionth, 27 now. Of the prisms above, many of whose booleans are worked out again, they take half
as long again at 1E-9 and 1E-6, and 2.3 to 2.4 times as long at nought. 24 new tests.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part and a difference of a body whose openings, cut in at once by the pieces of the body
each opening's box reaches, come out open or with a piece judged whole cut the openings in again, asked below a
thousandth and within a million of the origin, with every plane of each opening carried through every piece it
crosses, as the cut once was, so that the faces of pieces side by side match. A piece beside one so cut kept a face the
other's faces did not match, and where two walls stood a hair apart the strip of a face between them was lost when the
two were glued: the plate 200 by 100 by 3 above, its ceilings 0.00095 apart, came out of that cut open at every
tolerance from a ten-thousandth down, and less the box across both openings, at a ten-thousandth or a
hundred-thousandth, where the boolean is not worked out again on the material, held 22 717.96, 1.05 short, and was not
valid, and the two joined held as much too little or were not worked out; they hold what they should now. The cut
again is taken where it closes with no piece judged whole, and given up where it comes to more than four times the
pieces; at a millionth and below the boolean is still worked out again on the material where the cut came out open the
first time. Of 7 200 unions, common parts and differences of prisms with two or three openings whose walls stood
0.000 15 to 0.03 apart and boxes, at 1E-5 and 1E-4, the 3 672 within a million of the origin held 96 wrong and trusted,
60 not worked out and 293 not valid, and hold 83, 4 and none; of 18 000 between nought and a millionth, the 9 180
within a million held 218, 226 and 56, and hold 203, 210 and 29. Four that were right, of two prisms close to a million
out, came out wrong, three by 6E-5 and one by 0.0034. Further out nothing moved, to the bit; cut again there, 1 700
more came out right but 27 that were right came out wrong, by as much as two tenths. At 1E-3 and 1E-2 nothing moved,
to the bit: cut again at a hundredth, a plate 300 by 200 by 12 a hundred thousand out whose twelve openings stood the
tolerance inside its faces, joined to a box at its corner, held 106 too much. 176 sets of booleans of bodies with and
without openings did not move. The booleans of 60 such prisms and boxes take a quarter less
time at 1E-4 and 1E-5, a sixth less at a millionth, an eighth less at 1E-9 and a twentieth less at nought, on .NET 10
and on .NET Framework 4.8, and the time they took at 1E-3 and 1E-2; those of a plate with twelve holes and a box take
the time they took. 16 new tests.

**CHANGED.** A union, a common part and a difference asked at a millionth and below of a body with openings are faster:
the body keeps the openings the boolean cut in at once, so that asking afterwards whether that cut came out open reads
it rather than cutting them again. Of the four booleans of 60 prisms with two or three openings and boxes, at a
millionth 308 of 549 such cuts are read from the body, at 1E-9 303 of 621 and at nought 283 of 755; the booleans give
what they gave, to the bit, and take a quarter less time at a millionth, a sixth less at 1E-9 and a twentieth to a
tenth less at nought, on .NET 10 and on .NET Framework 4.8, and the time they took at 1E-5 and above; those of a plate
with twelve holes and a box take a quarter less at a millionth and at 1E-9. 8 new tests.

**FIXED.** A union, a common part and a difference of a body whose openings' walls stand apart within the tolerance of
one plane keep each wall in its own plane, as `TryCutOpenings` keeps it. A boolean cut the openings of its bodies in at
once within the tolerance, and the plane of one opening, cutting all it reached, took in the wall of another within the
tolerance of it, however far away, and which of the two kept its own hung on their order. An L 100 by 80 by 50 with two
blind openings 27 apart whose walls stood 0.0009 apart across it, less a box 65 by 20 by 40 across both walls, within a
thousandth or a hundredth, held 130 189.39 one way round and 130 189.26 the other, where it holds 130 189.32; the box
less the L held 28 457.23 and 28 457.88, where it holds 28 457.68, and their union and common part were as far off. The
openings of both bodies are cut in, and the operation worked out, within the finer tolerance the cut of openings takes
for such walls, and what that gives is taken where it closes within the tolerance asked. Of 4 800 unions, common parts
and differences of prisms with two or three such openings and boxes, turned about in space or not, at the origin and a
thousand to a thousand million out, at 1E-3 and 1E-2, 1 363 that were wrong are right now, every one a million out and
nearer among them, and none that was right moved but in its last bits; at a millionth and below none moved, to the bit.
Where a wall of the other body lies within the tolerance of the plane of a wall of the one, the boolean is worked out as
before: of 4 800 more, each box with a face a tenth to six tenths of the tolerance off the plane of a wall, 5 changed,
all to right. So it is too ten million and more out where the finer tolerance would come within eight trillionths of
the size of the coordinates: worked out within it, 3 that were right came out wrong, the worst 0.98 off a thousand
million out. A wall of an opening turned the other way from a wall of the body, or of another opening, whose plane it
stands within the tolerance of, is found standing apart too, by `TryCutOpenings`, `GetVolume`, `Section` and
`Mesh3.ToCells` as well: an L with an opening's wall 0.0004 off its inner wall, 5 along it, measured 0.09 too little.
A boolean worked out within the finer tolerance takes a tenth to a quarter longer, on .NET 10 and on .NET Framework
4.8, its openings cut first; every other is worked out in the time it took. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume`, `GetSurfaceArea`, `GetCentroid` and `GetMassProperties` of a body whose openings
`TryCutOpenings` will not cut in closed within the rounding of the coordinates, asked at a point tolerance below that
rounding, nought among it, cut them within what rounding can move a corner off a plane, a trillionth of the size of the
coordinates, as `Section` and `Mesh3.ToCells` cut them, before they are cut at the tolerance asked and not trusted. A
plate 200 by 100 by 3 at the origin, turned about in space, with an opening 32.7 by 51 down from its top to 0.9 over its
bottom, measured nought at nought, its area nought too, and the whole plate, 60 000, at 1E-15, neither trusted; it
measures 56 497.83 at both, and is trusted. Of 4 000 prisms with up to three openings, turned about in space or not, at
the origin and a thousand to a thousand million out, 22 measured nought or the whole body at nought and 7 between 1E-12
and 9E-7, all untrusted; every one measures what it holds now, and all but one star are trusted. Nothing else moved at any
tolerance from nought to 1E-3. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** `GeoCellGrid3.GetAdjacentCells` of a grid cut at a fine tolerance gives the cells beside each along the grid's
axes, not the cells a place over across the plane between them as well, which share no more than an edge. The rounding
let the extents of two such cells overlap by a hair along that edge, and they were read as meeting over the sliver, more
than the point tolerance squared, which is nought at nought. Asked below a millionth, two cells meet now over more than
a strip as wide as the point tolerance, or as what rounding can move a corner, a trillionth of the size of the
coordinates, where that is more, along where they overlap. At nought a plate 200 by 100 by 3 turned about in space, cut
into twelve cells, gave 25 pairs of neighbours; it gives 17. Of 2 000 grids of prisms with up to three openings, turned
about in space or not, at the origin and a thousand to a thousand million out, 482 had other neighbours at nought than at
1E-3, and 526 to 546 between the rounding and 1E-7; of 2 000 boxes turned against a grid along the world's axes, 138 at
nought and up to 183; one grid does now. At a millionth and above, the default tolerance among them, where the cells are
cut as they were, they meet as they did, to the bit: a cell of a ledge 0.109 thick meets the column it stands out of
over 0.000 44 at a thousandth, a strip narrower than the tolerance, and is its neighbour, and at a millionth 181 of the
2 000 grids still have other neighbours than at 1E-3. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** A segment you give in the plane, a `GeoLine2` or a straight `GeoEdge2` no longer than the point tolerance, is
read as its start where it does not truly meet the other shape, and is in contact where it does, as the guide has said
and as space reads it. `DistanceTo`, `CollidesWith` and `GetShortestLineTo` measured such a stub by its nearer end
against nearly every shape: at a thousandth, the segment from (5, 0.0015) to (5, 0.0006), pointing at the segment from
the origin to (10, 0) and stopping 0.0006 short of it, was 0.0006 from it and collided with it, as it did with a ray, a
line without ends, a polyline, a polygon, a rectangle, a triangle, a chain, a loop, a face, an arc, an ellipse, a spline
and an edge so aimed; it is 0.0015 from each, joined to it from its start, and collides with none. A stub that truly
meets a shape is in contact however short: the one from (5, 0.0004) to (5, -0.0005), crossing that segment, was 0.0004
from it, from a ray, a line without ends and a straight edge, and joined by a line 0.0004 long to every straight shape;
it is nought from each and joined where it crosses, at (5, 0), and `GetIntersections` and `TryIntersectWith` of the
straight shapes, which gave it no crossing at all, give that one. One running into a circle, an arc, an ellipse, a chain
or a loop is joined to it where it crosses the rim, not at its start up to the tolerance off it, and is nought from a
circle. Of 40 864 random stubs aimed at every shape in the plane, asked of it either way round at a thousandth and a
hundredth and out to 100 000, 292 492 of the 1 425 400 answers broke that rule, and none does now. A side of a shape,
however short, a segment longer than the tolerance and a point are read as before, to the bit: no answer to a longer
segment moved, and of 400 000 random pairs of segments, arcs, circles, polylines, polygons, rectangles, chains, loops
and edges, many with sides shorter than the tolerance, only answers to a stub did. A segment longer than the tolerance is
asked in the time it took, to within the noise, on .NET 10 and on .NET Framework 4.8; a stub, whose true meeting is now
looked for before its start is measured, takes up to half as long again: against a polygon of 40 sides, 1.69
microseconds where 1.25 on .NET 10, and the shortest line to a chain of 40 edges 7.0 where 4.4. 9 new tests.

**FIXED.** Walls of two openings of a body, or of an opening and the body, standing apart within the tolerance of one
plane are each cut in their own plane by `TryCutOpenings`, and so by `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume`, `Section`,
`Mesh3.ToCells` and the queries that read the material. The plane of one opening cuts all of the body it reaches, and the
plane of another within the tolerance of it found the corners of that cut on it and was not made: its wall was cut in
the first one's plane, however far away, and which of the two kept its own hung on their order. An L 100 by 80 by 50, a
million out, with two blind openings 27 apart whose walls stood 0.0009 apart across it, measured 153 674.08 within a
thousandth where it holds 153 673.56, its section 0.014 off, and 153 673.30 with the openings the other way round. Such
openings are cut within a finer tolerance, between that gap and the most that walls meeting within the tolerance, or a
face off flat, stand off one plane, where the body and its openings close within it and what it gives closes within the
tolerance asked, and `ToCells` cuts its cells within it too; walls that meet are made one plane, as before. Of 8 000
planes through 4 000 prisms with up to three openings, turned about in space or not, at the origin and a thousand to a
thousand million out, 2 cut the wrong area at 1E-3 and 2 of the prisms measured the wrong volume; of 2 000 more cut
into cells, 1 came out in the wrong cells. None does now. Nothing else changed at any tolerance from nought to 1E-3 but
a star whose volume and section were within the slack and are exact now, and one section changed in its last bits. Of
600 plates 300 by 200 by 12 with twelve holes, the walls of a row of them within the tolerance, 1E-3 or 1E-2, of the
planes of their neighbours' walls, 62 came out as much as 12.2 cubic millimetres off what they hold, and are within
0.002 of it now. The booleans read their operands as before. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `Section` and `Mesh3.ToCells` asked at or a little above the rounding of the coordinates, at a point tolerance
below both what rounding can move a corner off a plane, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates, and a millionth,
are cut within that trillionth, as they are below the rounding. Cut within the tolerance asked, the rims a plane left did
not close there either: of 8 000 planes through prisms with up to three openings, turned about in space or not, at the
origin and a thousand to a thousand million out, 871 cut nothing or the wrong area at the rounding, 547 at twice it, 136
at 1E-12 where that is above it and 125 at 1E-7; of 2 000 of the bodies cut into cells, 668, 452, 110 and 110 came out in
the wrong cells, and 5 of 2 000 boxes turned about in space and cut along the world's axes at the rounding. None does
now, but for 86 planes and 73 bodies a thousand million out at twice the rounding, 2E-6, and 1 box. At a millionth and
above, the default tolerance among them, a section and the cells are cut as they were, to the bit, however far out the
body stands: of the planes, 139 a hundred million and more out still cut nothing at a millionth. 4 new tests.

**FIXED.** `Section`, and `Mesh3.ToCells` of a body or of a box turned against the grid, asked at a point tolerance below
the rounding of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of them, nought among it, cut within what rounding can
move a corner off a plane, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates: `Section` cuts the material by its plane so, and
`ToCells` the body and its openings, each cell whose corners that leaves a rounding apart welded to close within the
tolerance asked. Within the tolerance asked, the two
faces beside an edge each cut their own copy of it a rounding apart, and no cut closed: at nought a plate 200 by 100 by 3
turned about in space, at the origin or a million out, had no section, where a plane square to its face cuts 20 000 of
it; cut into cells 60 by 40 along it, it came out one cell of 60 000, where twelve hold it, and with a hole 20 by 20
through it one cell of 60 000, the hole left in, where they hold 58 800; and a box 100 by 60 by 40 so turned, cut by a
grid along the world's axes, came out one cell, where the grid lays 19 through it. Of 8 000 planes through plates, boxes
and prisms shaped as an L or a star with up to three openings, turned about in space or not, at the origin and a
thousand to a thousand million out, 7 383 cut nothing at nought and 73 cut the wrong area, as 4 974 of 5 534 did at
1E-12 below the rounding; of 2 000 of the bodies cut into cells at nought, 1 918 came out in the wrong cells, 85 with
nothing said in the log, as 1 282 of 1 370 did at 1E-12; and so did each of 2 000 boxes turned about in space and cut
along the world's axes at nought, and 1 338 of 1 409 at 1E-12. None does now: 2 of the bodies, a thousand million out,
have a cell closed along its edges and holding what it should whose corners the weld leaves apart at nought. Which
bodies `ToCells` refuses is read at the tolerance asked, as before. At and above the rounding, 1E-3 and 1E-2 among them,
this change left every section and every cell the same to the bit; the band up to a millionth and walls of openings
within the tolerance of one plane are fixed on their own, see above. On .NET 10, 300 of the bodies are cut into cells in
1.03 seconds at nought where they took 1.71, and 2.38 where 3.95 on .NET Framework 4.8; two sections of each take what
they took, 2.38 seconds where 2.40, and 5.87 where 5.91; at a thousandth both take what they took. 8 new tests.

**FIXED.** `DxfTable.RemoveDataLink()` and `RemoveDataLink(row, column)` clear the flag 4 of a linked cell from the state of
every cell of the range they take the link from, where they cleared it from the top left cell alone. The library's range
(1, 0) to (2, 1) with the state 4 given to (2, 1) as well kept it at (2, 1) once its link was taken away, and AutoCAD 2021
read (2, 1) as linked with no range, and saved it so; now no cell of the range keeps it, and that one byte is all that
changes in the file. A cell of the flag 4 outside every range, which AutoCAD reads as not linked, is left as it is. Taking
the links away takes what it took, 1.3 milliseconds with the reading of the drawing on .NET Framework 4.8. 3 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfSpline.IsPeriodic` is the flag 2048 of group 70, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it, where it was the flag 2:
AutoCAD writes the flag 2 on its closed splines too and reads no period from it. Its periodic cubic of 70 3115 is periodic
and its closed cubic of 70 11 is not, and either turns into the other with the flag 2048 alone taken out or put in, the
flags 1024 and 32 changing nothing; the library's own periodic spline, written with the flag 2 (70 3), is not periodic, as
AutoCAD read it. The flag 2 is still written for `periodic` and is what `NurbsData.Periodic` and `FitData.Periodic` give,
and a polyline made of a spline, its extension refused, its pieces and copies are what they were. NURBS data set not
periodic (`SetNurbsData`, `Degree`, and what writes them anew) take the flag 2048 off with the flag 2. 3 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfSpline.NumFitPoints`, `HasFitData`, `FitPoints`, `GetFitPointAt`, `FitData` and `Type` of a spline of the flag
1024 of its group 70 and no fit points in its record give the points of its curve at its knots, from its start to its end,
as AutoCAD 2021 gives them: its periodic cubic of the knots 0, 30, 45, 55 and 80, saved with 70 3115 and 74 0, has the 5
fit points (0, 0), (30, 0), (30, 15), (20, 15) and (0, 0), and its closed cubic of 70 11 given the flag 1024 the 5 points
(0, 0), (40, 0), (50, 30), (10, 25) and (0, 0) it runs through; a spline whose record holds fit points gives them, as before.
Its fit data taken out (`SetNurbsData`, `PurgeFitData`) take the flag 1024 off with them. `NumFitPoints` of a spline of no
fit points takes 3.0 microseconds where 1.9 on .NET Framework 4.8, 1.5 where 1.0 on .NET 10, as it reads the flag; of the
3115, which works out its knots, 10 where 2.6. 2 new tests, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.IsLinked` of a cell of a range linked in the TABLECONTENT, not its top left, is true where the cell's
own state there (its 90) has the flag 4 of a linked cell, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: the library's range (1, 0) to (2, 1)
with the state 4 given to (2, 1) as well is linked at (1, 0) and (2, 1), where the library read (1, 0) alone; the top left
cell is linked whatever its state, as AutoCAD read it with the state 0. The states are read with the links, so `IsLinked`
of the six cells takes what it took, 1.0 microsecond on .NET Framework 4.8 and 1.7 on .NET 10. 2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfMText.Width` set on an MTEXT in columns before R2018 leaves its 41 and its columns as they are, as AutoCAD
2021 saves one: it read its 8D of two static columns 50 wide with a gutter of 10, of R2000 and of R2007, given the width 80
as 80 until it saved it, and saved 41 50 and the columns as they were, which read 110 wide again. The library's drawing is
its file, so the MTEXT reads 110 wide straight away, where 80 was written into its 41. A width below nought is refused, as
before; an MTEXT of R2018, or of no columns, has its 41 set as before. Setting it takes 6 microseconds where 8 on .NET
Framework 4.8. 2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.IsLinked` of a range linked in the TABLECONTENT is true at the range's top left cell alone, as
AutoCAD 2021 reads it: the range (1, 0) to (2, 1) the library linked AutoCAD read as linked at (1, 0) and not at (1, 1),
(2, 0) or (2, 1), where the library read all four linked; each of them still gives the range and the link by
`GetDataLinkRange` and `GetDataLink`, as AutoCAD's do. A range named in the cells of the ACAD_TABLE, which AutoCAD reads no
link from, is linked at every cell, as before, and `SetDataLink` writes the other cells of a range as AutoCAD saved them
again, as it did. `IsLinked` of the six cells takes what it took, 1.0 microsecond on .NET Framework 4.8 and 1.9 on .NET 10.
2 new tests.

**FIXED.** `DxfMText.Width` of an MTEXT in columns before R2018, whose 41 holds a column's width as AutoCAD writes it, is the
width of all its columns with the gutters between them, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: two static columns 50 wide with a gutter of
10, in R2007 or in AutoCAD's own R2000, are 110 wide, AutoCAD's thirteen dynamic columns of R2000 770 and its three of their
own heights 170, where each read 50. The 41 written is AutoCAD's, a column's, as before; a width given back changes nothing,
and an MTEXT of R2018, or of no columns, reads its 41 as before. `Height` of an MTEXT of R2000 in dynamic columns of their
own heights is its `ACAD_MTEXT_DEFINED_HEIGHT`, the first column's, 15 for AutoCAD's columns 15, 25 and 0 high, where it read
nought, and a column added to them takes that height; from R2007, with no group 46, they are of no height, as AutoCAD read
them. Reading the width of such an MTEXT takes 4 microseconds where 1.3 on .NET Framework 4.8, 1.6 where 0.5 on .NET 10, as
it reads the columns; of R2018 it takes what it took. 4 new tests, 5 changed.

**NEW.** `DxfTable.SetDataLink(row, column, dataLink)` and `SetDataLink(range, dataLink)` link cells to a DATALINK of the
drawing, as AutoCAD 2021's `SetDataLink` links them: in the TABLECONTENT AutoCAD keeps for the table, the range's top left
cell given the flag 4 of a linked cell, its 92 made odd and the run `340` link, `93` rows, `94` columns, `96 1` after it,
and the DATALINK tied to the table and to its TABLECONTENT (`94 2`, `330 F6`, `330` of the TABLECONTENT), as AutoCAD wrote
its 73; AutoCAD's linked table, its link taken away and set again, is AutoCAD's file to the byte. The cells keep what they
hold, for AutoCAD to fill when it updates the link. A table of no TABLECONTENT, as a program other than AutoCAD writes one,
and a range that meets a linked one are refused. Linking a cell takes 0.46 ms after the table's parse of 0.68 on .NET
Framework 4.8, 0.35 after 0.57 on .NET 10. 3 new tests, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** A table's data link is read where AutoCAD 2021 keeps it, in the TABLECONTENT of the table's extension dictionary
(ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP, an XRECORD of ACAD_ROUNDTRIP_2008_TABLE_ENTITY), from the cell whose 92 after its custom data is odd:
`GetDataLink`, `GetDataLinkRange`, `IsLinked` and `GetTargets` read AutoCAD's link of the table F6 over (1, 0) to (1, 0),
as AutoCAD reads it back, where they read none; a cell of the TABLECONTENT is the table's of its row and column, whatever
rows the TABLECONTENT has, as AutoCAD read the link of (1, 0) of a table given a fourth row by a program that left its
TABLECONTENT of three, and one past the table's last row or column names none.
`RemoveDataLink` takes such a link away in place, the cell's 92 made even, its run 340, 93, 94, 96 taken out and the flag 4
of a linked cell cleared, the DATALINK kept and tied to nothing (`94 0`), as AutoCAD's `RemoveDataLink` leaves it. A link
of the cells of the ACAD_TABLE, the library's guess of before, is still read. `GetFormula` of a cell whose 344 names no
record, as AutoCAD wrote its linked cell's, reads the field of the cell in the TABLECONTENT, `=1+2` where it read none;
`RemoveDataLink` writes that formula in the cell, a FIELD of its own owned by the table as `SetFormula` writes one, as
AutoCAD read no formula there once the link was taken away and read the one of a cell of its own. Taking the link of
AutoCAD's 78 away takes 1.8 ms with the parse where 1.2 on .NET Framework 4.8, the FIELD written; one of no formula is as
before.
Reading a cell of AutoCAD's linked table first takes 0.71 ms with the drawing's parse where 0.65 on .NET Framework 4.8, 0.51
where 0.44 on .NET 10. 8 new tests, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** `SetFormula` writes the cell's 344 after its 145 and before its 92, as AutoCAD 2021 wrote the formula of a cell,
where it went after the 92. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** An MTEXT of R2018 set in columns by `SetStaticColumns`, `SetDynamicColumns`, `ColumnCount`, `ColumnWidth` or
`ColumnGutterWidth` is given the width of all the columns it counts with their gutters (41, and 40 of its embedded object),
as AutoCAD 2021 writes it: two columns 50 wide with a gutter of 10 make 110, where 50; one of R2000 keeps a column's, and a
copy into the other form takes the other width. Before R2018 `ACAD_MTEXT_DEFINED_HEIGHT` is written only for a height
above nought, and for dynamic columns of their own heights holds the first column's, each linked column MTEXT its own, as
AutoCAD writes them, where a height of nought was written and columns of their own heights had none; their `Height` is
nought from R2007. Setting columns takes 180 microseconds where 134 on .NET Framework 4.8, 190 where 137 on .NET 10. 4 new tests, 4
changed.

**CHANGED.** In a drawing older than R2007, which brought columns, the column data of an MTEXT (`ACAD_MTEXT_COLUMN_INFO`)
are columns only with the MTEXTs of its later columns linked (`ACAD_MTEXT_COLUMNS`), as AutoCAD and ezdxf write them:
AutoCAD 2021 read three MTEXTs of R2000 given the column data alone, two static columns 50 wide among them, as of no columns,
each 50 wide, and the one of a defined height of 15 that high. `ColumnType` of such an MTEXT is `NoColumns` and `Height` its
`ACAD_MTEXT_DEFINED_HEIGHT`, where they read the columns; `SetStaticColumns`, `SetDynamicColumns` and `ColumnType` refuse
it columns, as the library makes no column MTEXT, where they wrote data AutoCAD did not read. From R2007 on, and with linked
column MTEXTs in R2000, nothing changes. 2 new tests, 7 changed.

**CHANGED.** `DxfViewport.Number` is -1 for a viewport turned off, as AutoCAD 2021 gives it, where it gave the id of group 69;
a viewport on keeps its id, and the id of one off is still not given to a new one. 1 new test, 5 changed.

**CHANGED.** `SummaryInfo` of a drawing of R2004 or later is kept in its header, as AutoCAD 2021 saves one of R2018: set, its
texts go to `$TITLE`, `$SUBJECT`, `$AUTHOR`, `$KEYWORDS`, `$COMMENTS` and `$REVISIONNUMBER`, an empty one leaving its
variable out, and each custom property to a `$CUSTOMPROPERTYTAG` followed by a `$CUSTOMPROPERTY`, as many as there are,
after `$DWGCODEPAGE`, the header's `$LASTSAVEDBY` kept before `$REVISIONNUMBER` as AutoCAD 2021 orders them in R2004,
R2010 and R2018, where they went to a DWGPROPS of ten at most; a DWGPROPS the drawing had is taken out, as AutoCAD saved the library's 26-a
of R2018 without it. Read, a drawing with no DWGPROPS gives the custom properties of its header in their order, Project and
Checked by of AutoCAD's 26-a, where it gave none. A drawing of R2000 keeps its DWGPROPS, as AutoCAD saves one. Reading the
properties of a drawing of R2018 takes 16 microseconds where 13 on .NET Framework 4.8, and 19 where 13 on .NET 10. 5 new
tests, 4 changed.

**CHANGED.** `Explode()` of a MINSERT, of one cell or more, throws `NotSupportedException`, as AutoCAD 2021's refused a
MINSERT of a circle in 2 rows by 3 columns and one of one cell (eNotApplicable), where it gave the block in every cell, six
circles; its `ExplodeToOwnerSpace()` appends the first cell's entities, one circle at the insertion point, as AutoCAD's did,
where it was refused. Its `TreatAsBlockRefForExplode` is false, its `GeometryExtentsBestFit` throws
`InvalidOperationException` (AutoCAD: eInvalidExtents) and its `GeometricExtents` is its first cell's, (-3, -3, 0) to (3, 3,
0) for the circle of radius 3, where they measured every cell; `UpdateExt` still takes in every cell. An INSERT of the
subclass AcDbMInsertBlock is a `DxfMInsertBlock` of one cell too, as AutoCAD reads it, where it was a `DxfBlockReference`.
Reading a drawing of 20 000 INSERTs takes 46 ms where 53 on .NET Framework 4.8, 24 where 26 on .NET 10. 5 new tests, 6
changed.

**FIXED.** `ToPolylineWithPrecision` of a periodic spline of fit points has each of its knots, one after another, in the
place of the vertex nearest it, the later of two as near, a later knot taking the place an earlier one took, and of a closed
spline its last vertex on its first, the polyline closed, as AutoCAD 2021 gives them; a closed spline of no fit points, as a
DXF of AutoCAD keeps one, is the halving alone, (0, 0), (34.42, -3.51), (50.86, 28.40), (18.15, 30.49) at 0, as AutoCAD read
it back; a periodic spline AutoCAD keeps by its fit points, the flag 1024 of its 70 set (its 3115), has its knots in place
though its DXF holds no fit points, as AutoCAD read its own again: the 26 polylines AutoCAD made of its three periodic cubics
of v7 and v8, at 0 to 99, are the library's to 1E-9, where 24 were not; at 10 they take 0.32 ms where 0.30 on .NET Framework
4.8, the knots now placed. The closed cubic through
(0, 0), (40, 0), (50, 30) and (10, 25), its knots the lengths of the chords, gives 5, 9, 15, 17, 30, 48, 86, 252 and 493
vertices at 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 99, where 4, 8, 14, 16, 29, 47, 85, 251 and 492, and at 0 the four points it runs
through and the first again, where its points at a quarter, a half and three quarters of its range, (34.42, -3.51) the
first, stood in their place; each arc is bent by
the turn over the piece the halving made, 0.418 from (0, 0) to (40, 0), as AutoCAD's. An open spline is given what it was.
6 new tests.

**FIXED.** `TrySubtract`, `TryIntersect` and `TryUnion` asked below four tenths of the rounding of the coordinates,
nought among it, of a body that does not close within that rounding, as one with cracks in its faces does not, take what
they work out within the rounding where it holds up, or where they give something within the tolerance alone too, and
are not worked out otherwise. Nothing such a body gives is checked on the way, and worked out within the rounding, the
booleans the tolerance alone did not work out came out wrong and were trusted: at nought a cube 10 across, cracked
0.0001 wide along its top, its bottom and a side, less a box 3 across turned inside it, came back whole, 999.998, where
973 is left; turned and joined to a box 7.5 by 6.2 through its corner, it held 1 232.638, where the two hold 1 107.64;
and its common part with a slab leaning through it was the whole cube, where they share 76.79. A difference or a union
holds up where it adds up with the common part of the two, itself lying within the body that closes, the volumes read
as `GetVolume` reads them, within what the open area of each body that does not close, the faces' areas summed with
their normals, times the diagonal of its box moves a volume; where the common part comes out as nothing the skins of
the two may not run into each other. A common part holds up where no corner of it lies outside the body that closes. Of
17 178 booleans of such a cube and a body through it at nought, 433 the tolerance alone did not work out and 51 it said
were nothing came out wrong: 9 still do, unions 0.0102 to 0.0125 from what the uncracked cube gives against the 0.01
the cracks move, and 15 696 hold what it does within 0.01, where 15 698 did, the 2 not worked out now open by holes the
cube does not have. Of 36 000 differences, common parts and unions of a U so cracked and a box, 1 342 unions, 201
differences and 21 common parts came out wrong where the tolerance alone gave nothing: 54 unions and 21 common parts
still do, and 25 of the 13 655 differences and unions that held what they should are not worked out now. Wherever both
bodies close within the rounding, and at four tenths of it and above, 1E-3, 1E-2 and 0.05 among them, every boolean is
worked out as it was, to the bit; below it, of two bodies that close, a boolean takes up to 0.03 milliseconds more, a
slot 1E6 out at three tenths of the rounding 0.149 where it took 0.127 on .NET 10, and 0.354 where 0.315 on .NET
Framework 4.8. Turned down, the cracked cube less the box inside it takes 4.2 milliseconds, where it took 2.2 to come
back whole (9.1 and 4.1 on .NET Framework 4.8).

**FIXED.** `TrySubtract`, `TryIntersect` and `TryUnion` of two bodies, asked below four tenths of the rounding of their
coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of them, nought among it, are worked out as though asked at that rounding,
reading a corner as on a plane within what rounding adds as they do just above it, and what they give is welded to close
within the tolerance asked, as `TryCutOpenings` welds its material there. Within the tolerance alone they came out wrong
and were trusted: at nought a plate 200 by 100 by 3 at the origin, turned, less a hole 20 by 20 through it, came back
whole, 60 000, where 58 800 is left; a hundred thousand out, less a slot 20 wide across it, it came back whole too, where
54 000 is left; a million out, it and a slot 100 by 10 along it were said to share nothing, where they share 3 000; and
a thousand out, joined to a box 50 by 20 standing through it, it held 68 588.24 where the two hold 74 000. A cube 100
across less a box through it, far out and turned, not worked out at nought, leaves 800 000. Of 71 820 of each, plates
and blocks less, sharing and joined to each of their openings taken as a plain body, turned at random, at the origin and
a thousand to a hundred million out, at nought and a tenth to four tenths of the rounding, 17 489 differences, 11 373
common parts and 9 785 unions wrong or said to be nothing, all trusted, are right now and valid at the tolerance asked,
as are 16 990 differences, 20 078 common parts and 21 741 unions that were not worked out; 6 unions are not worked out,
5 of them as before, and none that was right moved. A body open at nought, a cube or a U with cracks up to 0.0001 wide
in its faces, is as open within the rounding, and what a boolean of it gives is taken where it holds up, as the entry
above says: of 17 178 booleans of such a cube and a box at nought, 15 696 hold what the closed cube would within 0.01,
where 1 578 did, and 742 hold further from it, not valid at nought, where 7 921 did. At four tenths of the rounding and
above, 1E-3, 1E-2 and 0.05 among them, every boolean is worked out as it was, to the bit. The hole at the origin takes
3.3 milliseconds at nought, where it took 3.7 to come back whole, on .NET 10, and 1.2 where 1.6 on .NET Framework 4.8; a
plate 400 by 200 by 10 less 20 holes one after another takes 86 at nought, where it took 10 to take none of them out,
and 50 at a thousandth (174, 28 and 104 on .NET Framework 4.8); at a thousandth the operations take what they took.

**FIXED.** `TrySubtract`, `TryIntersect` and `TryUnion` of two bodies, asked within a few roundings of their coordinates,
a quadrillionth of the largest of them, read a corner as on a plane within what rounding adds to the planar tolerance, a
trillionth of the size of the coordinates, as the cut of openings does. Within the tolerance alone, rounding put the
corners of a face lying in a plane of the other body on either side of it: a plate 200 by 100 by 3, turned and a hundred
thousand out, less a slot 20 wide across all of it, within its rounding of 9.5E-11, was said to leave nothing, where
54 000 is left; a hundred million out, less a notch 20 by 20 through one end, within 4.9E-8, it came back closed and 320
short, wound two ways along its sides; and a thousand out, joined to a box 50 by 20 standing through it, within half its
rounding, it held the two whole, 77 000 where they hold 74 000, and was trusted. A union is taken so where it closes wound
alike and holds the two less what they share read the same way, and is worked out as before otherwise. Of 136 800 of
each, plates and blocks less, sharing and joined to each of their openings taken as a plain body, turned at random, a
thousand to a hundred million out, within half the rounding to a thousand times it, 583 differences said to leave nothing
and 82 unions holding the wrong volume, all trusted, are right now, as are 5 637 differences, 4 196 common parts and
4 678 unions that were not worked out; 40 unions still are not, and none that was right moved. At every tolerance at or
above a trillionth of the coordinates, 1E-3 and 1E-2 among them, a boolean is worked out as it was, to the bit; below
four tenths of the rounding, nought among it, see the entry above. The slot takes
0.94 milliseconds at its rounding where it took 6.4 to say nothing was left, on .NET 10, and 0.39 where 2.3 on .NET
Framework 4.8; at a thousandth the operations take what they took.

**FIXED.** A dimension copied into a drawing of R2000 no longer makes a file AutoCAD 2021 will not open. It kept its
version (280 of AcDbDimension), which R2010 brought, and AutoCAD's DxfIn refuses the file ("in AcDbRotatedDimension ...
Unexpected DXF group code: 280"): the dimension 4D of R2018 copied by `WblockCloneObjects` into the R2000 `DxfWriter`
writes. It is written without it into a drawing before R2010 now, as AutoCAD's SAVEAS writes one, and with it into R2010 or
later. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** A dimension style copied into a drawing of R12 no longer makes a file AutoCAD 2021 will not open. Its arrows by
name (5, 6 and 7) were written only where a block was named, and AutoCAD's DxfIn refuses a DIMSTYLE of R12 without its 5
("Omitted group 5"): GH_DIM, whose arrows are those of AutoCAD's own, had none. Its texts (3, 4) and its three arrows are
written after its flags now, each empty where it has none, as AutoCAD's own R12 writes them. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** A face of a polyface mesh written by GeometryHelper 13.0.0 or 13.1.0, with the marker AcDbVertex before its
AcDbFaceRecord, which AutoCAD 2021 refuses, is read with its own marker alone and saved so: such a file opened and saved
again opens in AutoCAD, every other record of it as it was. A file with no such face is saved byte for byte as before.
2 new tests.

**CHANGED.** The offset of a closed polyline that crosses itself is none, as AutoCAD 2021's `GetOffsetCurves` gives none of
a bow tie (the maintainer's decision, point 79 of the AutoCAD checks): `GetOffsetCurves` and
`GetOffsetCurvesGivenPlaneNormal` of a `DxfPolyline`, a `DxfPolyline2d` and a `DxfPolyline3d` give an empty list, either
way, and say why in one Debug line. A polyline crosses itself where a side passes through another, from one side of it to
the other: the bow tie (-10, 1), (10, -1), (10, 1), (-10, -1), grown by 1, was one polyline joined at (0, 1.004988), and
the square (0, 0), (6, 0.06), (4, 0.06), (10, 0), (10, 10), (0, 10), whose bottom curls into a loop of 0.01 square units
about (5, 0.05), was the square from (-1, -1.01005) to (11, 11), where AutoCAD gave one running out to x = 206. A corner
that only touches another side, a spike narrower than the point tolerance at its foot, a corner given twice, and an open
polyline that crosses itself are offset as before. `Offset2.Offset` is not changed. 4 new tests, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of a table scaled alike scales the text heights its table style gives too, as AutoCAD 2021's
does: each cell that has no text height of its own takes the height of its kind of row, scaled, as its own (its 140 with
its flag 0x20), as AutoCAD's own save of the table it scaled keeps them, one in each cell. The height of a kind of row is
the table's own where it has one, else its style's: the style the table names, else the drawing's Standard, else
AutoCAD's own Standard, the title 6 and the header and the data 4.5 in a drawing of millimetres and 0.25 and 0.18 in one of
inches, as the 43 drawings AutoCAD 2021 saved for the checks have it. The table of rows 10, 8 and 8 that names no style,
scaled by 2, has the two cells of its title 12 high and its other four 9, its cell of its own 3.5 now 7, as AutoCAD reads
it, where they stayed 6 and 4.5; AutoCAD read the heights first written as the table's own, after its last cell, as 0.18
in every cell, and none is written there now. Its rows are still 20, 16 and 16, where AutoCAD measures them by its font as
22, 18 and 18. 8 new tests.

**CHANGED.** A table mirrored so that the image of its direction still reads left to right or upwards stands at the image
of its point along that image, its rows running up (`FlowDirection` `BottomToTop`, 70 of 1 in its head with the flag 0x04
of 93), as AutoCAD 2021's `TransformBy` leaves it: mirrored in y = -150 the table at (300, -100) stands at (300, -200)
along (1, 0, 0), where it stood at (370, -200) along (-1, 0, 0), and in the line at 45 degrees through (280, -100) at
(280, -80) along (0, 1, 0). A table mirrored in x = 280 stands at (190, -100) as before. `FlowDirection` reads a 70 of the
table's head, where AutoCAD writes it. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** The snap angle of a viewport of R12 to R14, in its extended data MVIEW, is written and read in radians, as
AutoCAD 2021 writes and reads it, as the twist is: a snap of 30 degrees is written 0.5235987755982988, where 30 was written
and AutoCAD read 30 radians. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** An anonymous group left empty is kept when the drawing is saved, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps *A1, *A2 and *A3
emptied by an erase, by `Remove` and made with no member; they were dropped. No group is dropped for being empty now, one
whose only member is erased among them, which the saving still dropped: *A1 of ezdxf's drawing, its text erased, is in the
drawing saved, anonymous, of no member. 2 new tests, 3 changed.

**CHANGED.** `Explode()` gives what AutoCAD 2021's `Explode()` gives of a few more:
- A face of a polyface mesh takes the mesh's colour and layer, not its face record's: the face of colour 1 of its own in a
  mesh of BYLAYER is BYLAYER, where it was 1, and the faces of a mesh on INPUT_PFACE_LAYER whose records stand on
  FACE_OWN_LAYER are on INPUT_PFACE_LAYER, where they were on FACE_OWN_LAYER. 2 new tests, 1 changed.
- A polygon mesh smoothed breaks as AutoCAD breaks one, its points of the surface read as a grid of the densities from the
  first: the mesh 4 by 4 smoothed at 6 and 6, its 7 by 7 points, gives 25 faces, the first of the points 0, 1, 7 and 6,
  where it gave 36 of the 7 by 7 grid. 1 new test, 2 changed.
- A MESH face of more than four corners breaks into AutoCAD's strip of triangles: two corners, then the rest by turns from
  the far end and the near one, from the face's first two, or from its last two back where it faces into a closed MESH,
  whose faces AutoCAD turns to face out. The face 0 to 5 alone, or in an open MESH, gives (0, 1, 5), (2, 5, 1), (5, 2, 4),
  (3, 4, 2), and as the base of a pyramid facing up into it (5, 4, 0), (3, 0, 4), (0, 3, 1), (2, 1, 3), where it gave
  (0, 3, 2) and (2, 1, 0) last; the face 0 to 4 alone (0, 1, 4), (2, 4, 1), (4, 2, 3). An open MESH of a face of six corners
  and one of five sharing an edge breaks each from its first two corners, as AutoCAD 2021 breaks it. A face of four
  corners or three that faces into a closed MESH is turned too, its corners read from its last back, as AutoCAD turns every
  such face: the square base (0, 1, 2, 3) of a pyramid facing up into it gives the 3DFACE (3, 2, 1, 0) and a side (0, 3, 4)
  facing in (4, 3, 0), where they were given as held, and the tetrahedron of ezdxf's drawing has the two of its four faces
  that face in turned. 7 new tests, 2 changed.
- The SPLINE of a splined LEADER or MULTILEADER line keeps its fit data, the points it runs through and its directions at
  the ends, as AutoCAD's has three fit points: through (1.77, 1.77), (10, 10) and (20, 10), leaving along (0.7071, 0.7071)
  and reaching along (1, 0), its control points and knots as they were. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** The definition of an attribute of several lines writes its default value (group 1) as the contents of its
MTEXT, its lines apart by `\P`, as AutoCAD 2021 writes the ATTDEF of three lines it makes: `LINE ONE\PLINE TWO\PLINE THREE`,
where it wrote `LINE ONE`, as ezdxf does. Made one of one line, by `IsMTextAttributeDefinition`, the definition keeps its
first line as before. An ATTRIB of several lines still writes the words of its lines joined by spaces
(`LINE ONE LINE TWO LINE THREE`), which AutoCAD reads as its own though it writes the group empty, so that a reader that
does not read the MTEXT has the words. The `TextString` of an ATTDEF or ATTRIB of several lines is the words of the lines of
its MTEXT joined by spaces, as AutoCAD 2021 reads both whatever their group 1 holds: `LINE ONE LINE TWO LINE THREE` of the
definition above, where it read `LINE ONE\PLINE TWO\PLINE THREE`, and of an ATTRIB whose group 1 AutoCAD left empty, where
it read nothing. Setting it sets the words of the MTEXT, which kept the old ones, its group 1 made to agree: the ATTRIB of
three lines set to `M24 GALV` is an MTEXT of one line `M24 GALV` where it stood. 4 new tests, 2 changed.

**CHANGED.** `ToPolylineWithPrecision` of a spline made lines gives AutoCAD 2021's vertices: its whole parameter range is
halved until the spline's point halfway along each piece lies within 1 / (M (p + 1)^2) of the middle of the piece's chord,
M the largest length of the spline's second derivative and p the precision. The cubic of one span on (0, 0), (10, 10),
(20, 10), (30, 0) gives 33, 65, 257, 513, 1 025 and 4 097 vertices at 0, 1, 10, 20, 30 and 99, where it gave 17, 27, 65,
257, 513 and 513; the cubic of two spans of the checks 50, 513 and 4 750 at 0, 10 and 99, where 21, 53 and 632; and of three
spans 78, 835 and 7 562, where 29, 91 and 843: every one of the 30 counts AutoCAD gave for the three, to the vertex; a
quadratic of three spans and a cubic of a double knot are given AutoCAD's counts too (29 and 76 at 0, 2 732 and 8 011 at 99).
A spline of degree 5 and a rational one are still given more than AutoCAD gives (117 and 371 vertices at 0, where 96 and
130). Made arcs, for a flat spline, it has the same vertices, each segment the arc that turns as the spline's tangent turns
along it, its bulge the tangent of a quarter of that turn, as AutoCAD 2021 bends the arcs of all seven splines of the
checks: the cubic of one span gives 33, 257 and 4 097 vertices at 0, 10 and 99, where 5, 9 and 47, its first arc at 0 of bulge
-0.00806. The finer polylines take longer, about as long per vertex: the three spans at 10 take 3.9 milliseconds made lines
where 1.1 (91 vertices) on .NET 10, and 2.7 where 0.54 on .NET Framework 4.8; made arcs 2.4 milliseconds where 0.13 (20
vertices) on .NET 10, and 4.4 where 0.20 on .NET Framework 4.8. 15 new tests, 2 changed.

**FIXED.** `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume`, `GetSurfaceArea`, `GetCentroid`, `GetMassProperties` and `Measure3` of a body
with openings, asked at a point tolerance below the rounding of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of them,
nought among them, measure the material `TryCutOpenings` gives at that tolerance, cut within the rounding. They cut the
openings their own way at the tolerance given, and within the rounding that came out wrong and was trusted: at nought a
plate 200 by 100 by 3 turned about in space, with a hole 20 by 20 through it, measured 60 000, the hole not taken out,
and `TryGetVolume` said that could be trusted; it measures 58 800, trusted. With a notch 20 by 20 through one end and
one 20 wide and 1 deep across the other, flush with three faces, a thousand out, it measured nought, trusted too; it
measures 56 800. Where `TryCutOpenings` refuses the openings they are cut as they were, and `TryGetVolume` says the
volume cannot be trusted; it says so too of a body whose own faces do not close within the rounding, whatever its cut
gives: a cube 10 across with cracks 0.0001 wide in its faces, less a tetrahedron, cut within the rounding at nought, is
a closed sliver of 0.000042 cubic millimetres, where the cube less the tetrahedron holds 888.41. Of 5 000 plates, boxes
and prisms shaped as an L or a star with one to three openings, turned about in space or not and 0 to 1E9 out, measured
at nought, 3 912 measured wrong and 3 178 of them were trusted; 29 measure wrong now, those whose openings
`TryCutOpenings` refuses, and none is trusted, where 4 820 are trusted and right and 1 028 were. Of the 3 417 of them
measured at 1E-12 below the rounding, 2 407 measured wrong and 163 were trusted; 1 measures wrong now, refused, and 2
measured right are refused, their cut refused. Of 6 000 cubes 10 across with cracks 0.0001 to 0.005 wide in their faces,
less one or two bodies, measured at nought, 37 trusted and wrong are refused now, and no other moves. The material costs
one cut now where it cost a cut and differences: the volume of a plate 400 by 200 by 10 turned about in space, with
twenty holes through it, takes 6.8 milliseconds at nought at the origin where it took 13.7, and 7.0 where 20.0 a million
out, on .NET 10, and 15.2 where 35.3 and 16.5 where 53.7 on .NET Framework 4.8; at a thousandth it takes what it took.

**FIXED.** `GetVolume` and the measures of a body with openings at or above the rounding of the coordinates no longer
leave an opening in, or measure the material as nothing, where a difference at the tolerance alone will not take it
out, or says it takes all that is left where cutting the openings in at once left material, and `TryCutOpenings` cuts
them. A difference at a tolerance at or just above the rounding reads corners the rounding puts either side of a plane:
the plate with the two notches a million out measured 58 800 at the rounding and at twice it, the second notch left in,
where `TryCutOpenings` gave 56 800; it measures 56 800. Of the 5 000 bodies of the run above, the 6 measured wrong at
1E-12 above the rounding and the 9 at 1E-6, each an opening left in, measure right now; every other measure at or above
the rounding is the same to the bit, 1E-3 and 1E-2 among them, and `TryCutOpenings` is unchanged at every tolerance.
The plate with the notches takes 8.8 milliseconds at the rounding where it took 6.2, wrong, on .NET 10, and 20.1 where
13.7 on .NET Framework 4.8, the openings cut twice. A plain difference of two bodies at the rounding is fixed on its own;
see above.

**FIXED.** `TriangulateSurface`, `DxfWriter.Add` of a body, and `ProjectToSolid`, with `GetClosestPointOnBoundary`,
`GetShortestLineTo` of a point and `SignedDistanceTo` that read it, of a body with openings, at a point tolerance below
the rounding of the coordinates, cut the openings within the rounding as `TryCutOpenings` does. At nought the turned
plate with the hole through it was meshed into triangles holding 29 999.99 where it holds 58 800, its bottom lost; of
54 such plates with one or two openings, 0 to 1E8 out, 53 were meshed wrong and 2 are now, where `TryCutOpenings`
refuses them. A point in the middle of the hole was projected 1.5 from it, onto a face across the hole, and a thousand
and more out 10.11 from it, onto the rim of the hole's wall, the wall's face read at nought; it is projected onto the
wall, 10 off, the faces read within the rounding too. Of the 54 plates, from the middle of an opening, 36 were
projected wrong and none is now; of 1 000 of the bodies of the run above, six points drawn about each, 1 954 of the
4 989 points outside were projected wrong at nought and 1 213 of 3 494 at 1E-12 below the rounding, and none is now; at
and above the rounding every projection is the same to the bit. `Section` and `Mesh3.ToCells` below the rounding are
fixed on their own; see above.

**FIXED.** A difference of two closed bodies no longer trusts what it gives where a cell of one, planes of the other
running through it uncut, puts more on the wrong side of them than the tolerance times the area of what is left. A
cracked box 9.4 by 12 by 4.24 dipping 0.088 into an arm of a cracked U 30 by 10 by 10, less the U, was left whole,
478.10 cubic millimetres where 475.54 is left: its cells, cut by every plane of both, were judged apart across a plane,
and with no other result to check them by were taken as they glued. A cut judged alike on both sides of such planes was
trusted the same way: a box dipping 0.028 into the arm, the U cut by the box's planes one cell whose 0.84 beyond the box
was within the tolerance times the U's area, 1.39, said the box took nothing of the U, and left it whole, 0.84 over
where the tolerance times its area is 0.45. What such a cell puts on the wrong side is weighed now, by the parts every
plane crossing it makes of it judged otherwise than the cell: one, two or three planes as the cell is read for them, and
more where they fall into no more than three families of parallel planes, a slab between two of each read as what lies
beyond the nearer less what lies beyond the further. The box less the U weighs 2.554 so, where it was 2.554 over; of
1 767 differences weighed so, the measure came within a thousandth of what the result was off by on 1 649, and was never
on the other side of the bound from it. A difference cut by every plane of both is not worked out where its cells weigh
more than the tolerance times the area of what is left, unless the other body's cells within it, cut by the same planes,
weigh no more, and it is then the first body less those; a cut of one body by the other's planes judged alike is not
taken where it weighs more than that, at a tolerance above nought. A comb 50 by 10 by 10 with two notches, cracked under
the sides of two boxes taken as one body, each dipping 0.088 into the tooth beside a notch, one cell crossed by five of
the boxes' planes, held 4 391.85 less them where 4 386.75 is left, and holds 4 386.62; a comb of 100 notches less 100
such boxes held 255.33 over, and is 0.13 under. Of 45 000 booleans of cracked U's and cracked boxes in and about their
notches, in five runs, 1 044 differences of the box less the U and 575 of the U less the box trusted and wrong, 0.27 to
156.43 off, are not worked out, and 3 and 1 are right, so that none is trusted and wrong; no right one moves. A body
that does not close wound alike is not weighed, its cells holding no volume to weigh: a box 30 by 20 by 10 with its top
turned over, less a post through it, is cut as it was. Every other result is the same to the bit: 27 000 booleans of the
U's with boxes not cracked, 17 452 of cracked cubes and boxes about them, 24 000 volumes of such cubes with openings,
24 000 cuts of them by `TryCutOpenings` and 4 800 of two boxes set off from each other, 600 plates cut by twelve
openings (543 right, 57 wrong), 400 slabs in bands, 70 bent bars, columns in 200 to 1 000 strips (18.96 under), 32 400
booleans of a turned cube and slabs or chips half the tolerance to twice it into or beside it, and the columns and beams
lying about the tolerance into or apart, at three tolerances. On .NET Framework 4.8, the least of seven runs, the box
less the U is turned down in 3.5 milliseconds where it was made in 2.7, and in 4.0 and 5.4 where 2.6 and 4.1 with the
box through the floor and into both arms; the box dipping 0.028 in 3.3 where 1.5; the comb of two notches less the two
boxes takes 7.0 where 4.5, a comb of 100 notches less one box 45 and 47 where 44, and less 100 boxes 15.4 seconds where
14.8; the U less those boxes, and combs of one and ten notches less one box, up to an eighth more, the cell weighed each
time; every other boolean of these bodies takes what it took within a tenth.

**FIXED.** A common part of two closed bodies, neither cut cleanly by the other's planes and neither judged apart
across a plane, no longer comes out as nothing where the way it was cut put more on the wrong side of a plane than the
tolerance times the area of what the other way gives, and the other way does not. A cracked U and a cracked box whose
floor lies 0.014 under the floor of its notch, across it, turned or turned and 96 metres off, share a slab of 0.52
cubic millimetres; the U cut by the box's planes was one cell beyond the box and kept nothing, and the box cut by the
U's planes, which kept the slab, was not taken. The way that weighs less is taken now: the common part is the slab,
0.52, 0.66 and 0.53 of three such, in 2.7 milliseconds on .NET Framework 4.8 where nothing took 2.3. Of the 45 000
booleans, 6 common parts given as nothing are right; none moves otherwise. Not fixed: at a tolerance of a hundredth a
slab 0.0166 thin, 1.66 tolerances, turned, is cut cleanly into 0.66 of its 1.17, within the tolerance times its area of
either, and read as enclosing nothing.

**FIXED.** What a `GeoPolygonArc3` says in its plane, `Locate`, `Contains`, `SignedDistanceTo`, `GetClosestEdge` and the
shortest line to a shape in its plane, no longer loses a side shorter than the global tolerance. They lay the loop out in
its plane, and the layout cleaned it again within `Tolerance.Global`, whatever tolerance the loop was built within and
the caller passed, so they could disagree with `IsPointOn` and `DistanceTo`, which measure every side. At a tolerance of
a ten-thousandth, the loop (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0.0006, 0), (0, 10, 0), built within a billionth, has
(10.00005, 0.0003, 0) on it, 0.00005 out from its side 0.0006 long, where `Locate` read it outside, 0.00025 from the
triangle left without the side; (9.9998, 0.0003, 0) is inside, 0.0002 deep, where it was read on the outline and nought
from it; and the edge nearest the first point is that side, where it was the side from (10, 0, 0) to (0, 10, 0), which
the loop does not have. The layout for these keeps every side now, dropping one only where its ends land on the very
same point; `ToPolygonArc2`, `ProjectToPolygonArc2`, the area, the centroid, `IsSimple`, offsets, fillets, chamfers and
the booleans still read the loop as a `GeoPolygonArc2` is built. Of 300 000 chains and loops at tolerances of a
thousandth and a hundredth, the 494 points in a loop's plane where `Locate` and `IsPointOn` disagreed are none, and of
