300 000 more at a ten-thousandth, 798; signed distances off the exact ones go from 4 814 and 7 904 to none, nearest edges
the loop does not have from 28 200 and 56 110 to none, and shortest lines to a segment off the exact length from 733 and
1 102 to 29 and 21: 37 of those are the lines they were, and 13 are beside a side shorter than the tolerance, which
offers its start as it does on its own, and still off. Every answer for chains, and for loops the global tolerance drops
no side of, is the same to the bit, and `Locate` on a loop of 100 sides takes the 18 microseconds it took on .NET
Framework 4.8. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** The closest edge of a curved loop or chain in the plane, and its shortest line to a segment, an arc, a circle,
a polyline, a polygon or another loop or chain, measure a straight side no longer than the point tolerance as it is, as
the distance does. Such a side was read as the point at its start, so a shape beside its middle was measured to a corner
of it: at a tolerance of a hundredth, the loop (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 0.006), (0, 10) is 0.03 from the segment from
(10.03, 0.003) to (10.05, 0.003), and the shortest line to it now runs from (10, 0.003), 0.03 long, where it ran from a
corner, 0.0301496 long; the edge nearest the point (10.03, 0.003) is the side 0.006 long, where it was the side along
the bottom, as far from the corner and first round the loop. A `GeoPolygonArc3` asked about its plane follows, and so
does the shortest line from a straight polygon, rectangle or polyline to an arc. A segment you give no longer than the
tolerance is still read as its start where it crosses no side, and the closest edge now takes one crossing a side as
nought from it, as the distance does. The nearest point keeps its reading: `GetClosestPointOnBoundary`, and the shortest
line to a point, which leaves it, still carry a point beside such a side to the side's start, so that line can be longer
than the distance by up to the side's length, 0.0301496 from (10, 0) here where the distance is 0.03, as a point near
the centre of an arc is carried to the arc's start. Of 300 000 random chains and loops with straight edges and arcs, many
no longer than the tolerance, at tolerances of a thousandth and a hundredth, at the origin and out to a million, 89 666
closest edges were not the nearest and 158 are not now, every one beside the centre of an arc or a circle no wider than
the tolerance, or for a segment shorter than it read as its start; of 300 000 more at a ten-thousandth, 73 719 and 107.
The 1 459 and 1 095 shortest lines that were off the exact length beside a short side are none; of the shortest lines
of a `GeoPolygonArc3` to a segment in its plane, 50 off the exact length are 15: 7 a touch read within the tolerance
past the ends of two sides, 5 a segment shorter than the tolerance read as its start and 3 a rounding of five parts in
1E10. Every answer for a shape with no straight side as short as the tolerance, against a
shape with none either, is the same to the bit, and every answer of `GetClosestPointOnBoundary` and `DistanceTo`.
The shortest line from a loop of 100 sides to a segment takes the 31 microseconds it took on .NET Framework 4.8, and its
closest edge to a point 8.8 where it took 8.4. 9 new tests.

**FIXED.** The closest edge of a `GeoPolygon2`, a `GeoPolyline2` or a `GeoRectangle2`, and its shortest line to a
segment, a circle, a polyline, a polygon or a rectangle, measure a side no longer than the point tolerance as it is, as
the distance does and as the curved loops and chains now do. Such a side was read as the point at its start, so a shape
beside its middle was measured to a corner: at a tolerance of a hundredth, the polygon (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 0.006),
(0, 10) is 0.03 from the segment from (10.03, 0.003) to (10.05, 0.003), and the shortest line to it now runs from
(10, 0.003), 0.03 long, where it ran from a corner, 0.0301496 long; so do the polyline and the rectangle 10 by 0.006 on
the same corners, and the lines asked the other way round. The closest edge takes no tolerance and measured at the
global one, so a side shorter than a thousandth was read so: the rectangle 10 by 0.0006 on the origin names its
right-hand side for the point (10.03, 0.0003), 0.03 off, where it named the bottom, as far from the corner and first. A
segment you give no longer than the global tolerance is still read as its start where it crosses no side, and the
closest edge now takes one crossing a side as nought from it, as the distance does. The nearest point keeps its reading:
`GetClosestPointOnBoundary` of a polygon or a polyline, and the shortest line to a point, still carry a point beside
such a side to the side's start, 0.0301496 from (10, 0) here where the distance is 0.03; a rectangle's was exact and
stays so. A triangle and a face follow their polygons. Of 300 000 random polygons, polylines and rectangles with sides
down to a twentieth of the tolerance, at a thousandth and a hundredth, at the origin and out to a million, 59 072
closest edges were not the nearest and 12 are not now, each for a segment shorter than the tolerance read as its start;
of 300 000 more at a ten-thousandth, 116 915 and 63. The 4 097 and 1 681 shortest lines off the exact length beside a
short side are 1 and 2, each a side passing within the tolerance of the centre of an arc, which the line keeps carrying
to the arc's start. Every answer for a shape with no side as short as the tolerance, against a shape with none either,
is the same to the bit, and every answer of `GetClosestPointOnBoundary` and `DistanceTo`; no collision, intersection,
offset or fillet of 600 000 random pairs moved. The closest edge of a polygon of 100 sides to a point takes 2.9
microseconds on .NET Framework 4.8 where it took 3.2; its shortest line to a circle takes 7.6 where it took 7.1, and to
a triangle 45.3 where it took 43.6. 6 new tests.

**FIXED.** The distance from a segment to an arc smaller than the tolerance weighs the point of the arc facing the
segment however near the arc's centre the segment passes. A segment within the tolerance of the centre was measured to
the arc's ends only: at a tolerance of a hundredth, the half circle of radius 0.004 below the origin is 0.004 from the
segment along y = -0.008, where it read 0.008. The chains, the loops and the edges that hold such an arc follow, and so
do their closest edges and their collisions: of 600 000 random pairs of segments, arcs, chains, loops and edges, 7 that
read clear though within the tolerance now collide, every one beside an arc smaller than the tolerance: one read 0.0015
off where it is 0.000002 off, and one read clear at a hundredth and collided at a thousandth. Of the curved loops and
chains measured as above, the 109 and 71 closest edges left not the nearest beside an arc's centre are none. The
shortest line keeps carrying a point within the tolerance of an arc's centre to the arc's start. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** The shortest line between two shapes in the plane reads them as touching only where they come within the
tolerance. Two sides whose lines cross within the tolerance past the ends of both, and two arcs whose circles do, were
read so though they stand up to twice the tolerance apart, where `DistanceTo` measures the gap and `CollidesWith` says
they are clear: at a thousandth, two squares 100 by 100 whose corners stand 0.00085 apart in x and in y are joined by
the line between the corners, 0.0012 long, where it had no length, and the segment from the origin to (10, 0) and the
one leaving (10.00135, 0.00078) at 60 degrees by the line between those ends, 0.00156 long. A touch within the tolerance
stays one of no length. Of the random shapes above, the 1 011 and 953 straight shortest lines of no length where the two
stand more than the tolerance apart are 118 and 100, every one now against a circle, which a segment's end within the
tolerance of its rim still touches, up to 1.35 times the tolerance off; the 972 that started more than the tolerance off
the shape are none, and of the curved loops and chains the 505 and 385 are none. Only shortest lines moved, and no
collision, distance, intersection, offset or fillet of 600 000 random pairs. 3 new tests.

**FIXED.** A segment meets a circle or an arc exactly where it comes within the point tolerance of it, as the gap to the
rim says and as `CollidesWith` says of an arc. `TryIntersectWith` and `GetIntersections` of a `GeoCircle2` or a
`GeoArc2` and a segment, and so of a ray, a polyline, a polygon, a rectangle, a triangle, a face, a chain, a loop and an
edge against them, missed an end within the tolerance of the rim wherever the segment's line crossed the circle further
than the tolerance past it, and took a foot of the line up to the tolerance past an end for a touch though that end
stood up to 1.35 times the tolerance off. At a thousandth, the segment from (0.05, 50.0005) to (10, 50.0005) touches the
circle of radius 50 about the origin at its start, 0.000525 off, where it met it nowhere, and the one from (0.0009,
0.0019) to (1, 0.0019) no longer touches the circle of radius 0.001 about the origin, its start 0.0011 off; the shortest
line from the square on that segment to the circle is 0.0011024 long, where it had no length. A segment that runs into
the rim and stops within the tolerance of it meets it once, where it crosses: the one from (-1, 0) to (0.0004, 0) meets
the circle of radius 0.0012 about the origin at (-0.0012, 0) only, where its end was a second meeting. An arc whose end
lies within the tolerance of a segment touches it below that end, where they collide: the arc of radius 50 about (0,
50.0002) starting 0.0045 radians past its bottom touches the x axis at (0.2249992, 0), where it met it nowhere. Of
200 000 random segments ending about the rim of a circle and of an arc, at a thousandth and a hundredth and out to a
million, 7 035 touches of the circle and 6 551 of the arc were missed, 8 read past the tolerance, and 344 and 206
counted twice; none is now. A segment no longer than the tolerance is still read as its start. The shortest line
follows: of 600 000 random polygons, polylines and rectangles, the 218 lines of no length to a circle more than the
tolerance away are none, and the 25 841 lines that moved to a circle or an arc, with the 32 064 of the curved chains and
loops, each lie within the tolerance, of no length where the two touch. Offsets cut their pieces where they cross as
before: no collision, distance, closest edge, offset or fillet of 600 000 random pairs moved. On .NET Framework 4.8 a
circle meets a segment in 0.065 microseconds where it took 0.059, and an arc in 0.209 where it took 0.131. 7 new tests.

**FIXED.** `TryCutOpenings` and the measures of a body with openings no longer keep a skin the tolerance thin over an
opening that cut in alone would lose it. Cut in together, a plane of one opening cuts every cell that reaches the
opening's box, and a plate's first cells reach all of its openings: twelve boxes hidden 0.01 inside the faces of a plate
300 by 200 by 12, cut within a hundredth, the first 1.7E-7 deeper than the tolerance, had a skin cut off the whole plate
by the plane of that box's floor, and the fourth, 5.7E-6 nearer the faces than the tolerance, kept it over and under
it: the plate came back valid and 9.68 cubic millimetres over the most its skins can leave, and `GetVolume` read the
same. A cell thicker than the tolerance and thinner than twice it, on the body's skin, that across its thickness lies
in an opening all but the tolerance from that skin, read within the rounding of the coordinates, goes with the opening
now, as it would cut in alone; a wall thicker than the tolerance between two parts of an opening stays. Of 600 plates
with twelve openings through, flush with the faces, blind, near an edge, or boxes hidden inside, cut at 1E-3 and 1E-2,
6 that came back valid and as much as 25.08 off hold what their skins can leave, and 2 that were 63.80 and 44.43 over
are 0.003 over, their boxes' floors on the plane of another box's floor a few millionths off; 19 that were right are
cut otherwise and stay right, and no other moves. Measured by `GetVolume`, the same 8 move the same way. Every union,
difference and common part of the corpora is the same to the bit, and so are `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume` and
`GetSurfaceArea` of 24 000 cracked cubes with openings, and `TryCutOpenings` of 24 000 of them and of 4 800 less two
boxes set off from each other. The 600 plates take 62 seconds where they took 61; one of them, its cut at once now left
open, has its holes taken out one at a time, in 0.52 seconds where 0.25. 5 new tests.

**FIXED.** `TryUnion` no longer refuses the union of two bodies lying exactly the tolerance into each other where it came
out wound against itself every way it was worked out, nor hands it back wound so where it held the two. A column 300 by
300 by 1 000 and a beam 386.7 wide and 364.8 high running exactly 0.001 into its side, turned and moved, joined within a
thousandth, kept the slab of the beam's end beside the column whole, held the two and 63.5, and was not made; worked out
again with the cells no thicker than the tolerance left out, it came out the same. It is worked out once more now with a
corner read as on a plane within what rounding adds to the tolerance, a trillionth of the size of the coordinates, as the
cut of openings reads it, and taken where that closes wound alike and holds no less than the two with the faces of one
lying face to face on the other's moved onto them whole: it holds the two less 125.26, the slab where they overlap being
109.45 and the beam's whole end 141.07. Another, made holding the two though `Validate` read it as not valid, is valid
now and holds the two less 40.83. One that holds less than that any way is still not worked out: a beam 377.4 wide and
107.5 high running exactly 0.01 into the column held 573.26 less than the two worked out once more, where its whole end
is 405.6. The rule for two bodies exactly the tolerance into or apart is written down in the guide: they are read as
touching, their common part is nothing, each difference leaves its body whole, and their union holds the two less the
overlap or the two and the gap within the tolerance times the area where they lie face to face. Of 1 600 such columns
and beams running 0.8 to 2 tolerances into or clear of each other, turned at random and as far as 700 metres from the
origin, 6 unions refused at 1E-3 and 4 at 0.05 are made, and 2 made not valid at 1E-3 are valid, each within that band;
of 5 400 booleans of turned cubes and blocks exactly the tolerance into, onto or beside each other, 8 unions refused are
made, from the two less the block's foot to the two. No other result moves, by a bit: the rest of those, the same
bodies half the tolerance to twice it apart, 600 plates cut by twelve openings, 400 slabs in bands, 70 bent bars,
columns in 200 to 1 000 strips, 41 452 fuzzed booleans, 54 000 of cracked shapes, and 28 800 cuts of openings. 1 new
test, 5 cases.

**FIXED.** A layer copied with an entity into a drawing of R2000 or later no longer makes a file AutoCAD 2021 will not
open. Its plot style (390) was left out, AutoCAD's DxfIn refusing the file ("Did not receive PlotStyleName"): the library
looked for the plot style Normal the layer named in the dictionaries of the drawing, and ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME is a
dictionary with a default (ACDBDICTIONARYWDFLT), which it passed over. Any entity copied or appended from another drawing
of R2000 or later onto a layer the drawing had not brought that layer so: the layer GH_TRUECOLOR copied with a LINE into
the R2000 `DxfWriter` writes, and Defpoints with a dimension. The plot style is found there now, and a layer whose plot
style the drawing has none of takes layer 0's. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** A face of a polyface mesh made in code (`new DxfFaceRecord`) no longer makes a file AutoCAD 2021 will not open:
it was written with the marker AcDbVertex before its AcDbFaceRecord, and AutoCAD's DxfIn refuses the file ("Class separator
for class AcDbFaceRecord expected"). It carries AcDbFaceRecord alone now, as AutoCAD and ezdxf write a face. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** `Cetransparency` writes the number an entity's 440 holds, the method in its top byte and the alpha in its low
one, as AutoCAD 2021 reads the DICTIONARYVAR: the 61 written for the alpha 100, a per cent, AutoCAD read as BYLAYER. The
alpha 100 is written 33554532 now and reads back as 100, not 99; a number with no method in its top byte, a per cent
written before among them, reads BYLAYER, as AutoCAD reads it. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** `SummaryInfo` writes what AutoCAD 2021 reads back. The custom properties go in the groups 300 to 309, ten at
most, and their count after the base of the hyperlinks, as AutoCAD writes them, in every version: a drawing of R2018 had
them in a list after a group 90, of which AutoCAD read none. The base of the hyperlinks goes to the header's
`$HYPERLINKBASE` too, which AutoCAD reads it from, where it read none of `https://example.com/plates/`; it is read from
there where that is not empty. A drawing AutoCAD saved as R2004 or later, which keeps the texts in its header and has no
DWGPROPS, gives its `$TITLE`, `$AUTHOR` and the others, where it gave none, and has them set with the properties. 2 new
tests, 2 changed.

**CHANGED.** A named group left empty is kept when the drawing is saved, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps G_ERASE when its one line is
erased, G_REMOVE when its line is taken out, and G_NEW_EMPTY made with none; they were dropped. An anonymous group left
empty is still dropped. ezdxf's audit removes an empty group, which AutoCAD keeps. 1 new test, 3 changed.

**CHANGED.** A table mirrored by `TransformBy` stays readable, as AutoCAD 2021's `TransformBy` leaves it: its normal the
mirror's image of the normal, no longer turned round, its direction the image reversed, and its point the image of the far
end of its top edge, so that it fills the box the mirror makes of it, its first column still first. The table at (300,
-100), 70 wide, mirrored in the plane x = 280 stands at (190, -100) facing up, where it stood at (260, -100) facing down.
1 new test, 3 changed.

**CHANGED.** Erasing the last active viewport of a layout leaves the LAYOUT naming its viewport 1 (331), as AutoCAD 2021
does, where it named none. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** A GEODATA made in code is of version 3 (90), as AutoCAD 2021 writes one, where it was of version 2; its class
is listed with a count of 1 (91), as AutoCAD lists it. Versions 2 and 3 hold the same groups and are read alike. 1 new
test, 4 changed.

**CHANGED.** `Explode()` breaks a dimension, a LEADER, a MULTILEADER, a HATCH and a MESH as AutoCAD 2021's `Explode()` breaks
them, compared part by part with the files it saved:
- A dimension leaves out the POINTs of its block on Defpoints, which mark where it measures: the dimension in a tilted
  plane gives seven parts of its block's ten. 1 new test, 1 changed.
- A LEADER gives its arrowhead first, a SOLID of the corner on the right of the leader, the tip and the corner on its left,
  or the INSERT of its arrow block; then one LWPOLYLINE through its vertices (a LINE between each two, as before, where
  they stand off the plane of its normal), or for a splined one one SPLINE, its knots the lengths of the chords (0 to
  21.64 through (1.77, 1.77), (10, 10) and (20, 10)), the line starting at the arrow's back, 2.5 along the first segment
  for an arrow 2.5 long. It gave a LINE between each two vertices from the tip, then the arrow. Each part has the
  leader's own colour, true colour, linetype and lineweight, as AutoCAD gives them: DIMCLRD, DIMLWD, the overrides and the
  colour of the group 77 drew them before. The vertex AutoCAD adds where the words of an annotation end, which its fonts
  decide, is not among them. 3 new tests, 11 changed.
- A MULTILEADER gives its words or block, then for each leader its dogleg as a LINE, then for each line an LWPOLYLINE to
  the last point of the leader, or a SPLINE whose knots are the chords, and its arrowhead, the corners in the LEADER's order;
  the lines ran on through the dogleg, the arrow first. A colour BYBLOCK is the multileader's own, and the arrowheads have
  its own lineweight, as AutoCAD gives them: the words on the right of two lines, one splined, give an MTEXT, the dogleg, a
  polyline and a SOLID, and a SPLINE and a SOLID, all BYLAYER. 1 new test, 7 changed.
- A HATCH gives nothing along a straight edge a line of its pattern runs along: DOTS 1.5875 apart in a square 30 by 20
  from its corner give 228 dots, as AutoCAD's, where they gave 247, 19 on its bottom edge. In the outer style the loops
  flagged external or outermost (1 or 16) are those it is cut by, as AutoCAD and ezdxf take them, ignoring islands those
  flagged external; by how deep each lies where none is flagged. ANSI31 round circles of radius 7 and 3, both flagged
  outermost, gives AutoCAD's 17 lines, one inside the smaller circle, where it gave 16. 2 new tests.
- A MESH face of more than four corners breaks into triangles fanned from its first corner, as AutoCAD breaks one, the
  last first and each the other way round: the corners 0 to 4 give (4, 3, 0), (2, 0, 3) and (0, 2, 1). A face given a
  colour of its own keeps it on its 3DFACEs. Both were refused. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** An MTEXT given a background by `BackgroundFill` or `UseBackgroundColor` no longer makes a file AutoCAD 2021
will not open. The flag of group 90 was written alone, and AutoCAD refuses the whole file ("Error Decrypting Data", and
`eMissingDxfField` from its DxfIn) over an MTEXT whose background is on with no colour (63) and scale (45); now the two
are written where the MTEXT has none, as BYLAYER and 1.5, the values AutoCAD reads where they are missing, and from R2007
the transparency (441) by layer. A colour taken off while the background is on leaves 63 at BYLAYER. 3 new tests.

**FIXED.** A HATCH given a pattern of AutoCAD's file by `SetHatchPattern`, ANSI31 among them, no longer makes a file
AutoCAD 2021 will not open: the pattern's count of lines (78) was left out with its lines, and AutoCAD's DxfIn refuses
the file ("expected group code 78"). It is written as 0 now, ezdxf writing none for a pattern of no lines either.
1 new test.

**FIXED.** The vertices of a POLYLINE carry its look, as AutoCAD 2021's AUDIT wants them: a polyline of colour 1 had
vertices of no colour, and AUDIT reported each, 22 to 106 errors a file (`AcDb2dVertex color != owner's`, and the same
of `AcDb3dPolylineVertex` and `AcDbPolygonMeshVertex`). A vertex is now given its polyline's layer, linetype, colour,
lineweight, linetype scale, visibility, true colour and transparency when it is made (by `AppendVertex`, `SplineFit`,
`CurveFit`, `SurfaceFit` or a new shape) and when the polyline's are set, as AutoCAD's setters set them on its vertices;
a face of a polyface mesh keeps a colour of its own. 3 new tests.

**CHANGED.** `DxfPolygonMesh.SurfaceFit` makes the grid AutoCAD 2021's PEDIT makes: SURFU and SURFV are spans, so that an
open mesh 4 by 4 smoothed at 6 and 6 has 7 rows of 7 points, 49, where it had 36; round a closed direction as many points
as spans, as before. `Explode()` breaks a mesh smoothed either way into the cells of its surface. 1 new test, 3 changed.

**FIXED.** A handle of extended data (1005) copied into another drawing keeps its place, as AutoCAD 2021's `CopyObjects`
keeps it: it was left out, so that the groups after it moved up one. It is written as 0 where what it names stays behind,
and `WblockCloneObjects` names the copy where that is copied with it: the LINE whose data names a CIRCLE, copied with the
CIRCLE, names the CIRCLE's copy. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** `WblockCloneObjects` copies no GROUP, as AutoCAD 2021's `WblockCloneObjects` and its COPYCLIP and PASTECLIP
copy none; it copied a group all of whose entities came along, as PLATE_1 where the drawing had a PLATE. `db.Insert` of a
whole drawing still copies its groups. A LEADER copied alone into another drawing now brings the annotation it points at
by a hard pointer (340), as AutoCAD brings the MTEXT, where its copy pointed to nothing; copied alone within its own
drawing it still points to nothing. 2 tests changed.

**CHANGED.** The value (group 1) of an ATTRIB of several lines is the words of every line joined by spaces, as AutoCAD 2021
writes it, `LINE ONE LINE TWO LINE THREE` for three lines, by `MTextAttribute` and by `SetAttributeFromBlock` of a
definition of several lines; it was the first line, as ezdxf writes it, which an ATTDEF still is. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**CHANGED.** A LINE offsets to the left of its way seen from the tip of its normal, as AutoCAD 2021's `Offset(5)` of the
line from (0, 0, 0) to (30, 40, 0) starts at (-4, 3, 0); it went to the right, to (4, -3, 0), with the polylines and
splines, which AutoCAD offsets to the right and still go there. A RAY and an XLINE given a plane go the way a line does.
1 new test, 3 changed.

**FIXED.** The twist of a view of R12, R13 or R14 (`DxfViewport.TwistAngle`, in the extended data MVIEW) is written and
read in radians, as AutoCAD 2021 reads it: the 30 written for 30 degrees turned the view by 30 radians, 1 718.87 degrees.
From R2000 group 51 is in degrees, as before. 1 new test, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** A dimension, a leader or a tolerance copied into a drawing of R12 brings its dimension style, written in the form
of R12: its name, flags and the variables R12 has, its arrow blocks by name where the drawing has a block of the name; the
copy named a DIMSTYLE the drawing did not have. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** An anonymous group renamed by `GroupDictionary.SetName` is anonymous no longer, as one renamed by its `Name` is.
1 new test.

**CHANGED.** `DxfCurve.Spline` of a polyline of the plane fitted with a spline is the B-spline it is fitted with, on its
frame, as AutoCAD 2021's `Polyline2d.Spline` gives it: the frame of 5 vertices fitted by a cubic gives the cubic of those 5
control points, where it gave the spline of degree 1 through the 17 vertices drawn. Joining such a polyline into a SPLINE
and projecting it still take it as drawn. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** A splined LEADER is walked over the lengths of its chords, as AutoCAD 2021 walks one, and boxed by its
vertices: through (0, 0, 0), (10, 10, 0) and (20, 10, 0) its `EndParam` is 24.14, its point at 12.07 the one it had at
0.5, and its `GeometricExtents` runs from (0, 0, 0) to (20, 10, 0), where the spline's rose to 10.43. Its `Spline` runs
over the same length, and so does the spline `Explode()` gives, from the arrow's back (see `Explode()` above). 1 new
test, 3 changed.

**CHANGED.** A `new DxfGeoData()` is AutoCAD 2021's new one: of no known type of coordinates, in metres both ways, its
scale judged at the reference point, where it was ezdxf's, geographic in inches of no scale estimated. Its
`BlockTableRecord` and `PostToDb` refuse any block but model space, as AutoCAD refuses paper space. 2 new tests, 2 changed.

**NEW.** `DxfGeoData.NorthDirection`, the angle of `NorthDirectionVector` from the Y axis towards X, as AutoCAD 2021 gives
it: (1, 0) a quarter turn, (-1, 0) minus one. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** `db.LayerFilters` reads the filters of AutoCAD 2005 and later: nested in All, as AutoCAD 2021 lists them, the
property filters and groups of ACLYDICTIONARY, by their names, then those of ACAD_LAYERFILTERS not among them, then the
three AutoCAD makes, All Used Layers, Unreconciled New Layers and Viewport Overrides. 1 new test, 3 changed.

**NEW.** `DxfLayerStateManager.GetLayerStateNames(includeHidden, includeXref)`, as AutoCAD's: a state is hidden where its
mask has the flag 0x8000, as AutoCAD 2021 saves one, and of an xref where it names its layers by name. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.RemoveDataLink` leaves the DATALINK it lets go of in the drawing, anonymous or named, as AutoCAD
2021's `RemoveDataLink` leaves it; it erased an anonymous one. 1 test changed.

**FIXED.** `DxfDatabase.Insert` of another drawing no longer leaves the drawing changed when it refuses a block that would
come to insert itself through an INSERT of this drawing of a block it has not. It refused that block as the merge came
to it, the blocks merged before it left written, and the block refused too, empty: this drawing's P holding an INSERT of
M, and the other's A a line and M an INSERT of P, the merge left A and an empty M. The blocks to be merged are walked with
those the copies bring before anything is written now, and neither comes. So too `Insert(blockName, ...)`, which left
its new block written, empty: this drawing's P holding an INSERT of NEWB and the other's model space one of P, NEWB is
not made. Of 60 000 drawings of R12 inserted three ways, 23 097 refusals had left the drawing changed, and none does; of
20 000 pairs copied six ways, 532 refusals had, and none does. The 110 325 inserts that went through are written byte for
byte as before. An Insert of 10 000 blocks nested one inside the next takes 954 to 1 043 milliseconds where it took 897 to
913 on .NET 10, and 1 044 to 1 048 where 984 to 1 009 on .NET Framework 4.8, for the walk; 3 000 nested blocks 1 to 11 %
longer. 2 new tests, 1 changed.

**FIXED.** `DxfDatabase.WblockCloneObjects` of several entities, and `Insert`, no longer name a block AutoCAD names
itself, brought by one entity, as an INSERT in a block another brings names a block neither drawing has. This drawing
having *U1 and *U2, and P an INSERT of Q, which it has not, and the other's *U1 an INSERT of P and its Q one of *U3,
which it has not, an INSERT of *U1 copied with one of Q brought *U1 as *U3, which Q's INSERT then placed: P, Q, *U3 and P
without end, found only once *U3 was written, so that the set was refused half written. *U1 comes as *U4 now, and the
set is copied, Q's INSERT of *U3 placing nothing, as where it came from. Where no round closes, the INSERT came to place
a block it did not place: of 20 000 pairs copied six ways, 3 such copies come out with another name. 2 new tests.

**FIXED.** A block AutoCAD names itself, copied into a drawing with a dimension or a table that names a block it has not,
no longer takes that name, which the dimension then drew by: the drawing of R12 of nine dimensions without its block *D1,
as a file may come, took the copy of another drawing's *D1 as *D1, and its first dimension drew the other's. The copy
comes as *D10 now, and that dimension draws by nothing still. 1 new test.

**CHANGED.** An INSERT in a block that a copy brings from another drawing, by `WblockCloneObjects`, by `AppendEntity` of
a copy or by `Insert`, that names a block that drawing has not is copied as before, naming it, and is now said: one Debug

**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.RemoveDataLink` takes the table, and what it owns through its extension dictionary, out of the
objects the DATALINK it lets go of lists itself tied to (its 94 and the 330s after it), as AutoCAD 2021's `RemoveDataLink`

ACAD_TABLE the library reads, so a link AutoCAD made is still not read, and the library still writes none. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** `TryCutOpenings` no longer hands back a plate whose openings end the tolerance inside a face, to a few
bits, valid and hundreds of cubic millimetres short. Where cutting the openings in together leaves the material open
and a weld does not close it, they are taken out one at a time by differences, and a difference read a corner as on a
plane within the planar tolerance alone, not within the rounding of the coordinates besides, a trillionth of their
size, as the cut of openings does, so that the faces of a hole whose floor lay the tolerance under the top sloped
across the plate. A plate 300 by 200 by 12, turned and far from the origin, with twelve holes ending 0.01 under its
top to within a millionth, cut within a hundredth, came back valid and 130.70 cubic millimetres short of the plate less
every hole through; the differences now read a corner so all through, and it holds 666 668.11, within what its skins
can leave. With the holes 0.001 under, cut within a thousandth, the plate refused for coming back wound two ways holds
666 657.36. A difference that will not come out so is worked out within the tolerance alone, as before: a plate with
twelve boxes hidden 0.001 inside its faces, near the origin, refused either way, holds what its skins can leave. Of 600
such plates, their holes through, flush with the faces, blind, near an edge, or boxes hidden inside, cut at 1E-3 and
1E-2, 17 came back valid and as much as 157 cubic millimetres off and 16 were refused, and each now holds what its
skins can leave; 69 that were right are cut otherwise and stay right, and no other moves. Every union, difference and
common part of the corpora is the same to the bit, and so are `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume` and `GetSurfaceArea`, and
`TryCutOpenings` of 24 000 cracked cubes with openings and of 4 800 less two boxes set off from each other. The 600
plates take 61 seconds where they took 74. 5 tests, 4 of them new.

**FIXED.** `TryCutOpenings` no longer hands back material that `Validate` reads as not valid where its openings were
taken out one at a time. Where cutting them in together leaves the material open and a weld does not close it, each

turned and far from the origin, less a hole 22 across whose floor lay 0.001 under its top to 2E-15, within a

material holds 666 657.36, and the cut returned true; what the differences leave is checked now, and where it is not

such plates, their holes through, flush with the faces, blind, near an edge, or boxes hidden inside, cut at 1E-3 and
1E-2, that plate alone changes. Of 24 000 cubes 10 across, cracked, with one or two openings, `TryCutOpenings` refuses
one it cut not valid within a hundredth, though of the right volume, and cuts the rest to the bit as it did; their
`GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume` and `GetSurfaceArea`, and every boolean of the corpora, are the same to the bit. The 600
plates take 82 seconds where they took 80. 1 new test.

**FIXED.** `Offset2.Offset` of a `GeoPolygonArc2` that crosses itself, grown or shrunk with miters or chamfers, reads a
crossing the tolerance does not tell from what lies beside it within a finer step; so does `GeoPolygonArc3.Offset`,
which miters. A corner of the loop within the tolerance of a crossing turns the tip of the region there by its own
turn, and such a crossing was joined round the space between, as when rounded, its miter or chamfer left out, though
the corner bent the loop by a degree; and two crossings within the tolerance of each other are one place, which turns
the blunt end of the sliver between them into a point, whose miter ran on, or was squared off at its limit, past where
the loop's own corners take it. Where the tolerance is so coarse at a crossing, the loop is now cut again within a
hundredth of the tolerance, and then a ten-thousandth: a step it cannot be cut at is passed over, one is taken where it
is coarse at fewer places than the step before, until none is left, and the loop is offset within the last step taken.
A step coarse at as many places as the one before, as where three edges cross at one point, ends it, and where no step
is taken the loop is offset as before. A loop of the answer that is a point within the tolerance asked for, its corners
all within it of each other, is left out, so the answer is still within that tolerance. The bow tie from (-10, 2) to
(1, -0.2), (1, 0.2) and (-10, -2), its back an arc of bulge -0.25, with a corner on its first edge 0.005 past the
crossing where it turns by 1 degree, grown by 1 with miters at a tolerance of 0.01, keeps the miter of its long lobe
and encloses 54.419, where it was 52.501; the bow tie of 30 degrees with such a corner turning it by 2 degrees, grown
by 3 with chamfers, is 137.974 where it was 137.199. A loop of ten corners, two of whose edges cross 1.7 degrees apart
and are crossed by a third 0.0078 from there at points 0.00027 apart, shrunk by 0.3 with miters at 1E-3, is four loops
of 24.284 where 0.063 more was cut out beside the point, and shrunk by 1 one of 2.857 where it was 3.358; a loop of
four corners whose spike 2.4 degrees wide is crossed by an edge where it is 0.0057 wide, grown by 3 with miters at
0.01, is 386.351, as within 1E-4, where it was 387.385. A loop of ten corners in a box 0.95 by 0.86, shrunk by 0.1 with
miters at 0.01, is the one loop of 0.022622 it was: the triangle 0.0013 by 0.0014 its finer step leaves beside a
crossing is left out. Round joins, and the DXF polylines' `GetOffsetCurves`, read every crossing within the tolerance,
as before.

Read against the exact-wedge oracle of the entry for the tips of 13.0.0, over the same 21 504 offsets: grown with
miters at 1E-2, 7 were wrong and 3 are, grown with chamfers at 1E-2, 3 and 2, and shrunk with miters 2 at 1E-3 and 1 at
1E-2, and none is; 8 came nearer and none went further. The 5 left at 1E-2 are one loop, a corner of which pokes 0.0075
across an edge, which so crosses both its sides within the tolerance of it; and the loop that does not cross itself,
wrong grown by 3 with chamfers, is as it was. 82 offsets changed, all of loops that cross themselves, offset with
miters or chamfers; of the 74 that were right, 3 moved away from the oracle's area by 0.0002 at most and the rest
towards it, a loop of ten straight corners grown by 3 at 1E-2 by 0.255, to the oracle's 525.435. Every round offset,
every chain, every loop that does not cross itself and every offset of the straight path is the same to the bit, and so
is the `GetOffsetCurves` of 2 720 DXF polylines. Of 1 728 bow ties with a corner within the tolerance of their
crossing, before or past it, turning the loop by half a degree to 135 degrees, at 1E-2 and 1E-3, grown by 0.3, 1 and 3
with miters or chamfers, 1 162 were wrong and 235 are, 927 nearer and none further; those left turn the loop by 45
degrees or more, where the corner and two crossings make a lobe of their own finer than the tolerance, and were wrong
as they are. Of 28 800 offsets of 900 random loops at a twentieth of their size, with miters or chamfers at 1E-2 and
1E-3, 20 have more or fewer loops than they had: 18 as many as within 1E-6 where they had not, and 2 one fewer, a loop
of 0.00001 that is a point within 1E-2, which they kept and the reading within 1E-6 has. A loop cut again within a
finer step takes up to twice as long, and is cut at most twice more: the loop of four corners grown by 3 at 0.01 takes
0.65 milliseconds where it took 0.35 on .NET 10, and 0.28 where 0.16 on .NET Framework 4.8; the bow tie 0.055 where
0.027, and 0.082 where 0.049; and the loop of ten corners shrunk by 0.3 takes 1.22 where it took 1.11, and 2.04 where
1.90. A place where three edges cross at one point is coarse at every step, and ends the steps: 30 diameters of a
circle, crossing at its centre, grown by 0.3 with miters at 1E-3 take 163 milliseconds where they took 150 on .NET 10,
and 329 where 317 on .NET Framework 4.8, and shrunk by 0.05 at 1E-2 57 where 51, and 110 where 101. The 1 200 offsets
of 300 random loops, and the 600 of 150 loops of straight edges, at each join, tolerance and way, take as long as they

**FIXED.** A union of two closed bodies that share nothing at the tolerance, one standing exactly the tolerance into the
other or clear of it, was reported as not worked out where what it gave holds a volume such a union can. A union that
came out open on the way and was closed has its volume checked against the two less their common part, and with nothing
in common at the tolerance it was held to the two, within a hair for the rounding: a column 300 by 300 by 1 000 and a
beam 239.2 wide and 344.9 high running exactly 0.001 into its side, turned, came out open and, closed, held the two less
13.75, where the slab they overlap by is 82.5, and was not made; so were a turned cube of 100 and a block 40 by 40 by 50
whose foot runs exactly 0.001 into the cube's top at its corner, holding the two less 0.67 where the slab is 0.4, and two
turned cubes of 100 a thousandth apart, holding the two and half the gap. Such a union is taken now where it holds
anything from the two less twice the tolerance times the area where they lie face to face, the overlap and the faces
where they meet the tolerance further in, to the two and the gap, and no more; a union worked out again round a slab the
tolerance thick is read alike, but no lower than the two less the slab once. Of 6 400 unions and differences of a column and a beam whose end stands 0.8 to 2 tolerances into or clear of it
within a thousandth, at the origin, turned and up to 700 000 out, 4 unions not worked out are made, each between the two
less the slab and the two, and of 5 400 booleans of a turned cube of 100 and a box exactly a thousandth or a hundredth
into, onto, beside or clear of it, 6 unions, 5 between the two less the slab and the two and the gap and the corner
block 0.27 under the two less the slab. Every other result is the same to the bit: the column and the beam within a
hundredth, 6 400, and 8 000 within each of a thousandth, a hundredth and five hundredths with the common part; the
cube and the box at 0.5, 0.8, 1.25, 1.5 and 2 tolerances, 27 000; 41 452 volumes and booleans of cracked cubes with
openings within nought, a thousandth, a hundredth and five hundredths, and 41 452 more within nought and 1E-12; 54 000
booleans of U bodies, and 54 000 more within nought and 1E-12; 600 plates with blind holes cut, 400 bands, 70 bent bars
and columns of 2 402 to 12 002 faces joined to a beam. The union that came out open and is taken now takes what it took
to be refused, within the noise: the column and the beam 4.97 milliseconds where 4.91 on .NET 10, and 1.73 where 1.64 on
.NET Framework 4.8; the rest of the booleans timed take what they took.

**FIXED.** `Merge3.CoplanarFaces`, which every boolean runs on the faces it glues, takes an edge within the tolerance of
two others for the edge it shares with the nearer, the pair that leaves the least area between them; it took the first

square millimetres short, and the difference came out closed and valid and 32.9 cubic millimetres short of the beam
less the common part, 119 941 187.15 where 119 941 220.02. Of 70 such bars turned at random, 14 came out 32.9, 35.1 or
54.8 short, and are 0.11 or 0.02 short now, as the other 56 were short by up to 0.2, the bar's end standing the
tolerance over the floor. A side 2 000 by 300 cut by a line from one bottom corner to 0.0011 over the other, and
across by four more, merges into the one face of 600 000 square millimetres it was, where it was 0.53 short. Where
each edge has one edge to cancel, or none, the same pairs cancel as before.

Of 600 plates 300 by 200 by 12 with twelve openings the tolerance inside their faces, their openings cut in at once, 13
that came out closed and valid holding a volume no such plate can, up to 523 cubic millimetres short, hold one it can
now, 2 not cut are cut, and one cut wrong is not cut; one not cut, of boxes 22 by 22 standing 0.01 inside its top, its
floor and its end at a tolerance of 0.01, is cut, closed and valid, 177 short of the least it can hold, where its
`GetVolume` was 28 908 over and is that 177 short. 104 more are a hair different: of the plates with holes through, 79
are nearer the exact volume and 9 further, by 0.017 at most. Of 41 452 volumes and booleans of cracked cubes with
openings and 54 000 booleans of U bodies, 285 and 849 results moved, none from right, refused or wrong to another; of
32 400 booleans of a cube and a box the tolerance into, onto, beside or clear of it, 6 unions moved, of a block over a
corner 1 080 001.33 to 1 080 001.07 where 1 080 001.2 is the block snapped to the top. 400 bands, 160 envelopes and
columns of 2 402 to 12 002 faces joined to a beam are the same to the bit, and the booleans timed take what they took.

**FIXED.** A boolean whose result is welded closed no longer loses volume with the number of corners along the edges of
its faces. Corners within the tolerance of each other are made one at the corner of them that moves the volume least,
each weighed by the triangle it makes with its neighbours on each face; a face cut into strips keeps a corner on its
edges where each strip ended, and a corner beside them made a triangle a strip wide with them, however far the face
reached, so the weld took the face's own corner off its plane, where the face's fan from its first corner made it cost
the most. A column 300 by 300, web 11, flanges 19, 4 000 long, every edge of its profile cut into 200, 400 or 1 000
pieces, 2 402 to 12 002 faces, joined within 0.01 to a beam 500 by 180 whose end runs 0.002 into the column's flange and
whose flanges run 60 past its edge, the two turned, came out closed and valid holding the two less 25.72, 99.39 and
374.81 cubic millimetres, where their overlap is 17.04; it holds the two less 18.96 now, as the column in one piece
does, the beam's end tilted where it meets the column's edge. A corner is weighed by the corner each face turns at
either side of it now, past any corner its edges run straight on through within the tolerance; and where the corners
left open are welded within twice the tolerance and more, a corner welded to already is weighed by every face of each
copy welded to it, not by its own faces only: a column 300 by 300 by 1 000 joined to a beam whose end runs exactly 0.001
into it, at a tolerance of 0.001, had its corner taken off its face to the beam's, weighed by a sliver beside it, when
the first change was tried, and the union came out 7.6 short of the least it can hold.

Of 1 600 columns joined to beams their end the tolerance into or clear of them, at 1E-3 and at 1E-2, 70 bent bars cut
from a beam, and the 16 200 booleans of a cube and a box within 1.25 to 2 times the tolerance of it, none moved. Of the
16 200 within half to once the tolerance, 118 moved, 10 nearer the exact volume and 12 further, and one union of a block
exactly 0.001 into the top of a cube came out 1 059 998.61 where it held 1 059 999.61 and the exact is 1 060 000, 0.19
under the two less twice the slab: both corners it chose between lie on a straight edge of the top, and weigh nothing
either way, before as now. Of 600 plates with twelve openings cut in at once, 61 moved: one closed and valid within the
least it can hold is 1.35 under it, and one refused is cut, 9.9 under it, each the last of twelve cuts whose first came
out as before within 5E-10 and whose later ones parted from there; one wrong is refused and one right is refused, 40 right moved
within what they can hold, and of 16 wrong that moved 8 are nearer and 4 further. Of 400 bands 2 unions are nearer and the rest the same to the bit; of 41 452
volumes and booleans of cracked cubes with openings and 54 000 booleans of U bodies, 689 and 828 moved, none from right,
refused or wrong to another. The union of the column in 400 pieces and the beam takes 800 milliseconds where it took
729 on .NET 10, and 836 where 789 on .NET Framework 4.8, and in 1 000 pieces 2 284 where 2 062, and 2 298 where 2 178:
its weld tilts the beam's end now, and tries keeping the faces on their planes first, as it did for the column in 100
pieces or fewer, which takes what it took.

## 13.1.0

**FIXED.** The booleans of two curved bodies faceted at different stations, and `VolumeTakeoff` of them, no longer
run for minutes. A body was cut into cells by each plane of the other wherever the plane ran, and every plane of a
curved body crosses another curved along the same turn at many places: a spiral ramp 7 600 wide and 300 thick in 32
facets over half a turn and a spiral girder 600 by 500 in 38, lying 100 into the ramp's outer edge, had the girder cut
into 36 509 cells for their common part. Once a body is in more than 4 096 cells, and where both bodies close, a plane
now cuts a cell only where the cell's box comes within the tolerance of the box of the faces lying on that plane, which
is as far as a face of the other body can reach, and the girder is cut into 5 015. Faceted 56 and 66 times, as a Tekla
model facets such a pair, the girder was cut into 263 911 cells and their common part took 42 seconds on .NET 10 and 91
on .NET Framework 4.8; it is cut into 18 345 and takes 2.5 and 3.3, and the take-off of the two, which took 41 and 90
seconds, takes 1.2 and 3.0. Both give the 65 400 402.028 cubic millimetres slicing gives, as they did. The take-off's
test of near-coincident pairs does not send such a pair to slicing: their faces cross at small angles rather than
standing beside each other.

Up to 4 096 cells every plane cuts every cell it crosses, as before, and the booleans of bodies cut into no more give
what they gave, to the bit: 17 452 booleans of cracked cubes and openings, 72 000 of U bodies and boxes, 24 000 volumes
of cracked cubes with openings, 32 400 booleans of a cube and boxes half a tolerance to two tolerances into, onto or
beside it, 600 plates with twelve blind holes cut in at once and 400 bands; and 12 800 joins and cuts of a column and a
beam fail or fall out of their bounds in the same cases by the same amounts. Booleans of plain bodies take the time
they took: whether both bodies close, and their openings, is asked only once a body passes 4 096 cells.

A difference or a union whose one body, cut only where the planes reach, came out open, and sealed did not add up
against the two and their common part, is not taken in the end all the same, welded closed, where the cells of both
bodies cut by every plane of both have a cell judged apart; what is taken instead is checked the same way, and the
boolean is not worked out where it does not add up. A spiral ramp 7 600 wide in 56 facets less a spiral girder in 66
lying 100 into its outer edge, the girder's top 0.002 over the ramp's floor, worked out within a hundredth so, came out
35 554.6 cubic millimetres short, an eighth of the 263 740.0 the two share; it is not worked out, and the take-off
slices it. Made within the fallback, a result is held to the fallback times the area of the common part: the same two
with the girder's top 0.0005 over the floor leave 7 170.1 less than slicing, within the 36 000 a hundredth allows.

**CHANGED.** `IsClosed` reads a body as `Validate` reads it, the edges matched along a line within the point tolerance,
so that the two agree on every body but a speck. `IsClosed` matched the ends of the edges first, each to the first
corner seen within the tolerance of it, and made one of two corners 0.0015 apart where a corner lay between them: a
cube of 100 whose top stood 0.0015 over the tops of its sides, with a speck of a face at each corner of its top half
way up, was closed to it within a thousandth and open to `Validate` along every edge of the top, and open to both with
the specks given last. Of 432 readings of cubes whose tops stand over their sides, with those specks given first or
last or without them, slide along them, bulge out past one or run out at a corner, by half, one, one and a half and
nearly two tolerances, at the origin, turned and far off, within a thousandth, a hundredth and 2^-10, the two disagreed
on 46 and agree on all; a gap of 0.0005 is closed to both wherever it lies and one of 0.0015 open. A gap of exactly
the tolerance is so to a few bits either way, 100.001 less 100 being 0.001 000 000 000 004 8, and reads as the rounding
has it.

Both read two more things as closed than `Validate` did. Two copies of an edge whose ends lie within the tolerance
of each other are matched however little of them lies along the other: a slab 100 by 100 and 0.0012 thick whose side
at one end is slid up 0.0002, each upright edge of the side sharing 0.001 of its line with its twin, read open along
four edges, as did slabs 0.0014 and 0.0016 thick slid by 0.0005 and 0.0009, and is closed and valid. Every edge no
longer than the tolerance is left out, as before, but for one that is a copy of an edge longer than it and belongs
to a loop that has an edge longer than the tolerance itself, which is kept with its copy: a slab 0.0015 thick whose
side at one end runs from 0.0003 to 0.0012 up, its upright edges 0.0009 long beside copies 0.0015 long, is closed, and
`Mesh3.ToCells` cuts it into its cells, as it did. A speck, a loop with no edge longer than the tolerance, keeps none:
a cube of 100 whose top has a square hole 0.0019 across, a sliver triangle in each side of it whose edge of 0.00095
stands 0.000475 in from the side's ends, reads open. And below the rounding of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the
largest coordinate of the whole body, not of each part, the edges are matched within that rounding: at a tolerance of
nought `Validate` read a cube turned in space, a cylinder of 24 sides at the origin and the union of two turned boxes
made within a thousandth open along nearly every edge, and reads them closed. At every tolerance at or above that
rounding the rounding changes nothing, bit for bit.

The reading has its limits. Edges matched along one line are matched one after another, so a gap wider than the
tolerance reads closed where other edges lie in it within the tolerance of either side: that cube whose top stands
0.0015 over its sides, with a box of 1 standing against each side half way up the gap, reads closed and valid, as it
did. A short copy kept with a side of a hole cuts the open side into stretches no longer than the tolerance in the
same way: a sliver face with an edge longer than the tolerance, lying in a side of a hole wider than the tolerance, can
still read the hole closed. A speck, a body with no edge longer than the tolerance, is not closed to `IsClosed` and is
closed to `Validate`, which calls it not valid, enclosing nothing, as before.

The bodies that read otherwise now are these: a body whose copies of an edge are taken for one only through a
corner between them, which reads open; one closed by twin edges no longer than about the tolerance, which `IsClosed`
read closed and `Validate` open, and both read closed; and one closed only to the rounding of its coordinates, at
a tolerance below that rounding, which both read closed. `Mesh3.ToCells` and the IFC readers, which ask `IsClosed`,
follow it: `ToCells` refuses the cube with the specks given first, which it cut into 8 cells, and refuses as before
a body closed only to the rounding, the union at nought, which read closed it would have cut into no cell at all;
`MeshConvert`, `ProductConvert`, `SolidConvert` and `FlatGaps` read a solid as `IsClosed` reads it. The booleans, the
weld, the cutting of openings, the closing, the takeoff and `TryGetVolume` read the bodies they work on as they did,
the ends of the edges matched first and within the tolerance given and no wider, and every result of them is the same
to the bit, at every tolerance: 41 452 volumes and booleans of cracked cubes with openings within nought, a thousandth,
a hundredth and five hundredths, and 41 452 more within nought and 1E-12; 54 000 booleans of U bodies, and 54 000 more
within nought and 1E-12, of whose results `Validate` reads 1 523 valid it read not valid; 32 400 booleans of a cube
and boxes half a tolerance to two tolerances into, onto or beside it; 12 800 joins and cuts of a column and a beam;
600 plates with blind holes cut and 400 bands; and a cube less a box through it, far off and turned, within nought,
not worked out, with a warning, as before. `TryGetVolume` can so trust a body `IsClosed` reads open, the cube with
the specks given first, 1 000 005, and refuse one it reads closed, the union at nought; its own answer says whether
its volume can be trusted. `TryClose`, and the closing of the cuts `TrySubtractAll` would skip, read a body as the
booleans do, so that one `Validate` now calls valid can still be closed or refused: the slab 0.0012 thick slid by
0.0002 is refused, the gap too wide, and the one 0.0014 thick slid by 0.0005 welded, its 14 cubic millimetres moved
to 11.67. Some results of the booleans that `Validate` called not valid at a tolerance of nought, closed only to the
rounding of their coordinates, now read valid, those 1 523 of the U bodies among them, so a `TrySubtract` checked by
`Validate().IsValid` after it takes them; `TrySubtractAll` checks each cut as the booleans read it, and takes them as
it did. `IsClosed` reads a plate of 3 206 faces with 200 holes in 1.9 milliseconds where it took 9.7 on .NET 10, and
in 4.3 where it took 13 on .NET Framework 4.8, and a cube in 7 microseconds where it took 5 on .NET 10 and in 3 where
it took 5 on .NET Framework; `Validate` takes 2 to 10 % longer on .NET 10 for matching twin edges by their ends, and 4
microseconds more on a body of ten faces with edges no longer than the tolerance; `TryGetVolume`, `GetVolume` and the
booleans run as they ran.

**CHANGED.** Offsetting a curved loop cut at its crossings into many loops no longer slows with the square of them. Each
piece of the offset, and each point the offset is read at, was read against every box along the one axis the edges and
pieces are put in order on, and against every loop the crossings cut the loop into for which side of the region the point
lies on. The long edges along the arms of a plus reach every box along either axis, and the plus of 8 000 teeth 0.5 apart
across each arm, cut at a tolerance of 0.001 into 16 002 loops and grown by 0.3, read 992 million boxes to find where its
pieces cross, for the 189 152 pairs whose crossings are read. Where more than 64 boxes reach a box or a point along the axis,
those that overlap or hold it are found in a tree of the boxes, once the boxes read along the axis pass what making the tree
costs, and are read in the order the axis gives them; the tree is given up where it finds more than a fourth of the boxes,
or, for points, more than a sixteenth of the boxes along the axis, as along the chords of a star, and boxes that run out to infinity or are of no
number are read along the axis only. A region of more than 64 loops is read at a point against the loops whose boxes hold
it. Grown by 0.3 with round joins, the plus of 8 000 teeth to each arm takes 1.3 seconds where it took 20 to 28 on .NET 10, 1.5
where 39 on .NET 8 and 1.1 where 50 to 113 on .NET Framework 4.8; one of 4 000 teeth 0.85 where 5.0, 0.93 where 6.5 and 0.60 where
13; and one of 80 000 teeth to each arm, 160 002 loops, 7.1 seconds on .NET 10, 8.2 on .NET 8 and 13 on .NET Framework 4.8,
where by the square it would take most of an hour. With miters, the plus of 8 000 teeth takes 1.9 seconds where it took 26
on .NET 10 and 1.6 where 58 on .NET Framework 4.8. Loops of every day are offset in the time they took or less: grown by
0.3 at 0.001, a star of 49 points in 44 ms where 70 on .NET 10 and 79 where 119 on .NET Framework 4.8, 100 random corners in
33 ms where 67 and 53 where 140, a zigzag of 500 teeth in 5.3 to 6.4 ms where 7.4 to 7.8 and 13 to 23 where 64, a gear of
1 000 arcs in 51 to 55 ms where 63 to 67, a gear of 200 arcs in the 1.9 ms it took on .NET 10 and the 4.0 to 4.3 on .NET
Framework 4.8; the stars of 21 to 61 points grown and shrunk by 0.3 and 1 at a tenth in the time they took or up to 8 % less on .NET 10,
and in the time they took on .NET Framework 4.8, within the noise. Of 18 000 offsets of 1 000 random loops and chains,
dense loops, stars, diameters and combs, both ways, with mitred, round and chamfered joins at tolerances of 0.001, 0.01 and
0.1, and 1 440 of 720 pluses turned at any angle, with arcs and without, zigzags, gears of up to 2 400 arcs, random walks
and lattices, none gives another loop, edge or bulge, to the bit, nor do 9 000 of the first and all 1 440 of the second with
the trees read for every box and point; nor does any of 120 000 cuts of 20 000 loops at six tolerances, which make 20.8
million loops, nor are the 599 million crossings of those loops found otherwise.

**FIXED.** At a tolerance of nought a segment or a line without ends finds its crossing of a triangle or a face turned
about in space, and of every face of a body it passes through. The crossing a segment finds on a plane stands off it
by the rounding of numbers the size of the coordinates, and the triangle or face read that against the planar
tolerance of nought and refused it, as it refused a ray's before 13.0.0: of 1 000 segments from 30 under
the middle of a triangle turned about in space to 30 over it, 920 crossed nothing, and 928 of the same faces; of the
lines without ends along them 889 and 905; of 1 000 lines through a cylinder of radius 20 and height 50, its axis
leaning in space, 996 were given one crossing or none, 950 by its prepared form, and so were 981 of the 986 segments
that reach through it. A triangle or face now holds the crossing of a segment as it holds a ray's, to 1E-15 of the
largest coordinate of its own and the segment's, on its plane and past its rim, and a segment reaching from further
off than the triangle, the face or the body is large is read from a diagonal short of it, along its line; whether the
crossing lies between the segment's ends is read by the tolerance given. A line without ends is cut past what it is
asked of, as before, and read as that segment; the prepared body holds the crossings of its mesh to the rounding of the
whole mesh, as for a ray. Below the rounding, and only there, two crossings of a seam within eight times it of each
other are one, the segment along the seam of two sides of a cylinder of radius 20, through its axis, from 60, a million
or a hundred million out to as far beyond, being given its two crossings where it was given none; and a segment with an
end within the rounding of a triangle or face, its other end off the plane, meets it at that end where it touches it
as `CollidesWith` reads it, and nowhere else, so the crossing of the plane, worked out to the rounding, no longer falls
either side of the end: of 1 000 segments from 10 off the side of a box turned about in space to a point on it, the
crossing of the triangle under the point and the touch `CollidesWith` reads differed 512 times and differ none, and
the body, which `CollidesWith` and `DistanceTo` read as touched every time, gave 831 of them nothing and gives each
its point. In a body the end is read as the body reads it: met where the segment touches the face, or where the body
holds the end as `CollidesWith` holds it. On a single triangle or face an end so near is crossed only where
`CollidesWith` of the two finds them touching, and at a tolerance of nought it refuses about half of them: of 1 000
segments ending on points of the sides of turned boxes, 617 cross the triangle under their end, and of another 1 000,
some of them far out, 480 the triangle and 535 the face. `CollidesWith` of a segment and a body asks the boxes first as
far apart as the body holds a point, a billionth, or 1E-15 of the largest coordinate of the body and the end further
out than a million, and that reaches every point tolerance below it, not only those below the rounding: the segment
standing up from 5E-10 over the top of a box 100 by 80 by 50, which is nought from it, touched nothing and touches it
at a tolerance of nought, of 1E-12, of 1E-10 and of 3E-10, as does the one from 1E-7 over that box a thousand million
out at nought; of 25 000 prisms' answers its collision disagreed with its distance 69 times and does 4. A segment with a
coordinate that is not a number touches no body, as before. Where it reaches, at a tolerance below the rounding only,
but for that box: `TryIntersectWith` of a segment and a triangle or face and the lists of where they meet, the same of a
line without ends, `GetIntersections` of a segment or a line without ends and a body,
`GeoPreparedSolid3.GetIntersections` and `CollidesWith` of a line without ends, `GeoBvh3.GetIntersections` of one,
`CollidesWith` of a line without ends and a body, and what reads an edge's crossing of a triangle or face: whether two
triangles touch, the crossings of two regions, and the cutting of segments, chains and arc chains by faces and bodies.
At every tolerance at or above the rounding every answer is the same to the bit, but for the collisions that box lets
through: of 518 400 answers drawn at 1E-6, 1E-3 and 1E-2 for boxes, prisms, cylinders, cones and rings turned about in
space, at the origin and out to 1E9 (segments and lines without ends through them, into them, wholly inside, ending or
starting on a face, missing a face by half, three and a hundred times the tolerance, or a hair off it), none changed,
nor did any of 120 000 answers of rays and segments about boxes, U's, cylinders, cones and rings out to 1E9, nor any
boolean of the G2b corpora, at nought included; of the 138 840 answers at or above the rounding drawn at 1E-12 and
1E-10, 1 626 changed, each a segment missing a face by up to 1E-8 that was nought from the body and touched nothing,
and touches it now. At a tolerance of nought, of 172 800 such answers 53 260 were wrong and 131 are: 79 segments ending
or starting on a side of a cylinder or a cone made by `Revolve`, 76 of them a million and more out, where the side
stands off its own plane by billionths and the body does not hold the end either (parked); 48 lines without ends a hair,
1E-11, beside the long thin faces of a cone at the origin to a thousand out, held by a triangle of the prepared body
whose plane stands off its corners by more than the rounding, where 14 were before (parked); and 4 such ends on a single
face of a cone 100 out. Lines a hair off a cone are held so more often in a sample drawn for them: of 2 400 lines a hair
off any face of a cone turned about in space, at the origin to a thousand out, the prepared body read 282 as touching
where it read 96, and of 2 400 a hair under the disk of its base 594 where it read 206, a quarter of them. At 1E-12 and
1E-10, of 345 600 answers 77 347 were wrong and 32 412 are, nearly all of them segments and lines missing a face by
less than the body holds a point within, a billionth, or than the rounding of the coordinates far out; one count rose:
at 1E-12, segments missing a single face by up to a hundred times the tolerance read as crossing it 151 times where 4
did, each a miss smaller than the rounding of its coordinates, as at 1E-12 any coordinate past 1 000 is. A single
segment's crossing of a triangle or a face now asks first whether the coordinates reach the rounding: at a tolerance of a
thousandth, of 64 triangles turned about in space some 2 000 out, it takes 68 nanoseconds on .NET 10 where it took 65,
and 68 where it took 65 for a face, and on .NET Framework 4.8 394 where it took 382 and 407 where it took 391. A
segment through a cylinder of 300 faces turned about in space takes 23.9 microseconds where it took 23.1 on .NET 10 and
70 where it took 75 on .NET Framework 4.8, a line without ends through the prepared cylinder 6.0 where it took 6.2 and
27.8 where it took 27.4, and through a box 0.84 where it took 0.80 and 3.86 where it took 3.66. At a tolerance of
nought they take longer than they did, for now doing the work they skipped, and about as long as at a thousandth: the
line through the prepared cylinder 7.0 microseconds on .NET 10 where it took 4.7, and the segment through the body 23
where it took 3.3. 16 new tests.

**FIXED.** The distance from a curved chain or a curved loop in space to a point is measured to each straight edge as it
is, however short, as it is in the plane. A straight edge no longer than the point tolerance was read as its start
point, so a point beside its far end stood as far from the chain as from that start: at a tolerance of a thousandth,
the chain built of the straight edges from (0, 0, 0) to (10, 0, 0) and on to (10, 0.0006, 0) was 0.00108 from
(10.0009, 0.0006, 0), and the point off it, where it is 0.0009 and on it. `IsPointOn` and `Locate` of a chain and
`IsPointOn` of a loop follow, and so does everything that asks them or the distance: the point's `DistanceTo` of them,
a loop's `SignedDistanceTo` of a point off its plane, a ball's `DistanceTo`, `CollidesWith` and `GetShortestLineTo` to
them and theirs to it, whose line lands on the short edge where it landed on its start. Of 300 000 random chains and
loops of straight edges and arcs from a twentieth of the tolerance to 100 long, many of them no longer than the
tolerance, at tolerances of 0.001 and 0.01, at the origin and out to a million, 63 760 distances were more than a
ten-thousand-millionth of the size of their coordinates off the exact one, 376 points read off the shape that were on
it, and 8 028 balls read the wrong distance and 126 the wrong touch; none does now. Of the 300 000 points about edges,
chains and loops drawn for the bends of 13.0.0, the 2 313 distances off the exact one on chains and loops, each nearest
such an edge, and the 68 wrong answers of `IsPointOn` are gone. A cut of a chain or a loop at a point is made where it
was: a point now on the shape only beside a straight edge no longer than the tolerance, further than the tolerance from
both its ends, cuts nothing and is refused, the chain handed back whole and the loop opened at its start, as before; the
loop (0, 0, 0), (10, 0, 0), (10, 0.0006, 0), (0, 10, 0), built within a ten-thousandth, holds (10.00098, 0.0003, 0) at
a thousandth and is not cut there; of the 300 000 random shapes, every cut at the point is the same to the bit. Every
answer about a chain or a loop with no straight edge as short as the tolerance is the same to the bit, and so is `GetClosestPointOnBoundary` of every one, which, as in the plane, still
carries a point to the start of a straight edge no longer than the tolerance, so that the shortest line from the chain
to (10.0009, 0.0006, 0) is 0.00108 long, from (10, 0, 0), where the distance is 0.0009. A straight edge on its own that
short is read as its start, as a straight `GeoEdge2` or a segment you give is. In the loop's plane, `Locate` and
`SignedDistanceTo` still read a side shorter than `Tolerance.Global` as gone, so they can disagree with `IsPointOn`
there. The distance from a chain of 100 edges takes 8.5 microseconds on .NET 10 where it took 9.6, and 28.5 to 29.1 on
.NET Framework 4.8 where it took 29.1 to 29.2. 7 new tests.

**FIXED.** `TryCutOpenings` at a point tolerance below the rounding of the coordinates, a quadrillionth of the largest of
them, nought among them, no longer returns true with a body left open or wrong. The queries have cut the openings within
that rounding since they were held to it; the cut itself did not, and at nought a plate 200 by 100 by 3 turned about in
space, with a hole 20 by 20 through it, came back as a shell of 7 faces, its bottom lost, and the cut said it had worked.
The openings are cut within the rounding now, and where cutting them in together leaves the material open they are cut
in one at a time, each kept only where it closes, not taken out by a difference, which within the rounding came back
closed and wrong: the plate a million out with two holes 1 and 1.5 deep from under it, the first taken out by a
difference, lost nothing to it and held 57 600 where it holds 56 100. The corners the cut leaves a rounding apart are
then made one, by the weld within the rounding, where that closes the material within the tolerance given, so that
`TryGetVolume` of what comes back trusts it at that tolerance; of the 8 385 cuts below it in the run below, it refused
3 322 without the weld and refuses 155, whose corners stand further apart than the rounding. The plate with the hole comes
back closed, holding 58 800. A planar tolerance below the rounding with a point tolerance that is not cuts as it did:
raised, the point tolerance a thousandth and the planar nought, a plate with a hole flush with each face came back in 35
faces where it comes in 124, and one with two holes overlapping was refused. Of 5 000 plates, boxes and prisms shaped as
an L or a star, with one to three openings through them or blind from either face, turned about in space or not and 0 to
1E9 out, cut at nought, 3 451 came back open, 83 closed and wrong and 422 refused; none comes back open or wrong now, and
29 are refused. Of the 3 417 of them cut at 1E-12 where that is below the rounding, 901 came back wrong, 898 of them with
no opening cut, and 1 507 were refused; none comes back wrong now, and 3 are refused, one of them cut right before. Every
one that comes back is valid at the default tolerance. Openings that touch or overlap each other or lie flush with a
face are refused more often than the rest: of 120 plates turned about in space, 0 to 1E8 out, with a hole flush with
each face, 34 are refused at nought where 20 were and 95 came back wrong or open; of 120 with a hole from over and one
from under overlapping, 37 where 26 were and 89 came back wrong or open. What comes back can be valid at the default
tolerance and not at the rounding, for slivers a rounding thin: 2 of those 120 with the overlapping holes. The 16 583
cuts at 1E-12 where that is at or above the rounding, and at 1E-6, 1E-3 and 1E-2, are the same to the bit, as are the
1 440 at a point tolerance of a thousandth and a planar of nought and 1 440 at the default of the 12 shapes the plates
were drawn from, and the 145 000 answers of the queries tried on prisms with openings and on bodies turned about in space
far out. `GetVolume`, `TryGetVolume`, `GetSurfaceArea` and `GetCentroid` of a body with openings do not cut them so: at
nought that plate measures 60 000, its hole not taken out, and `TryGetVolume` says it can be trusted. At a thousandth the
cut takes the time it took, within the noise: a plate 400 by 200 by 10, turned about in space, with one hole through it
1.7 milliseconds at the origin and 0.31 a million out on .NET 10 and 0.66 on .NET Framework 4.8, with twenty 4.6 to 4.9
and 9.3 to 9.5. At nought, where it gave a body open or wrong, it takes 2.5 where 1.8 and 1.25 where 0.66 at the origin,
0.37 where 0.81 and 0.83 where 1.9 a million out; with twenty holes 7.5 where 4.6 and 16.7 where 9.2 at the origin, and 7.8
where 11.3 and 18.2 where 28.2 a million out, the weld most of what it adds.

**FIXED.** A difference of two closed bodies could leave whole a cell of one that is not convex, where planes of the
other ran through it and would not cut it, and trust what it gave. A U 30 by 10 by 10 whose bottom and outer sides are
cracked under the sides and the floor of a box dipping 0.088 into one of its arms is one cell to the box's planes, and was
read by the middles of its parts either side of each plane and of the four two planes make: those holding the 2.55
cubic millimetres the box takes held more of the U beyond the box, or had their middles in the notch, outside the
material, and were not read. The U less the box held 2 667.83, trusted, where 2 665.28 is left, and with the box dipping
through the floor of the notch, or into both arms and the floor at once, it was left whole the same way. Where one
such plane crosses a cell, or two, or three that meet at a point within the other body's box, or three of which two are
parallel and the third runs across them, the parts all of them make are read too, each by its middle wherever it lies,
since no face of the other body runs between a part and its middle; the U less the box holds 2 665.15. A common part
judged so whichever body is cut, and a union judged so whichever body's cells are kept, are reported as not worked out
rather than taken one way: the box dipping into the U's arm, joined to it, held 3 145.93 where the two hold 3 143.38,
what they share counted twice. A union judged so one way only is taken where the union cut the other way round, the
second whole and the cells of the first beyond it, holds as much within the tolerance times its area. Of 45 000
booleans of cracked U's and cracked boxes in and about their notches, in five runs, 325 differences of the U less the
box trusted and wrong are right, and 5 the difference gave as nothing, where 2 436 to 2 627 are left, are right; 6 more
given as nothing are trusted now and 1.9 to 5.8 off what is left; 3 common parts given as nothing are right and 2
trusted and wrong are not worked out; 4 unions trusted and wrong are right and 2 002 are not worked out, so that none is
trusted and wrong; and 20 unions that counted what the two share twice, 1.13 to 14.38, within the tolerance times their
area, are not worked out. 1 324 wrong before are wrong by another amount, 473 of them nearer and the rest farther by no
more than 0.005, and 7 right move within the bound, 6 of them nearer; none right or refused before is wrong now. The
27 000 booleans of the same U's with boxes not cracked are the same to the bit, as are 24 000 volumes of cracked cubes
with openings and 17 443 of 17 452 booleans of them; the other 9, trusted and wrong at a tolerance of nought, are not
worked out.

Not fixed: a difference judged so with no other result to take is still taken as its cells glue: the cracked box
less the cracked U it dips into, the box's cells judged so by the U's planes, holds 478.10
where 475.54 is left, trusted, and of the 45 000, 1 047 such differences of the box less the U and 576 of the U less
the box are trusted and wrong, as they were or by another amount. Checking such a difference against the other body
cut by every plane of both would leave 13 of the 45 000 trusted and wrong, but refuses 30 differences that are right
within the bound and 166 of the 325 put right here, and is not done. A cell crossed uncut by more than three planes, by
three meeting outside the other body's box or along one line, or by three parallel, is read as before; and where the
part the box takes is within the tolerance times the area of the body it is taken from, as from a comb of 10 notches,
the cell is read as it was. A comb of 2 notches, cracked the same way under the sides of two such boxes taken as one
body, one dipping into the tooth beside each notch, holds 4 391.85 less them where 4 386.75 is left, as it did. The U less the
box takes 3.3 milliseconds on .NET Framework 4.8 where it took 1.8, the least of seven runs, cut now by every plane of
both; a comb of 100 notches less one box dipping into a tooth by its middle notch takes 47 where it took 45, a comb of 10
5.1 as it did, and the comb of 100 less 100 boxes 16.9 seconds where it took 16.5.

**FIXED.** `DxfDatabase.WblockCloneObjects`, and an INSERT of another drawing copied alone and added by `AppendEntity`,
wrote blocks that insert themselves where the drawing copied into holds an INSERT of a block it has not, as a drawing
read from a file may. This drawing's P holding an INSERT of M, and the other drawing's M an INSERT of P, an INSERT of M
copied brought an M that places P, which then placed that M: P, M, P without end, which a reader places 64 deep at most
and AutoCAD's AUDIT takes out. Such a copy is refused now with an `ArgumentException`, and nothing is written; so is one
whose blocks insert one another in the other drawing (M inserting N and N inserting M), and one whose blocks would come
back to the block the copies are added to (an INSERT of Q copied into W, the other drawing's Q inserting W). The blocks a
copy brings are walked once each, with this drawing's blocks of the names they give, before anything is written.
`DxfDatabase.Insert` of the other drawing refused some of these rounds and wrote the rest; it refuses them all now, but as
the merge comes to the block refused, as when it refused before: the blocks merged before it stay written, and so does
that block, empty, which this drawing's INSERT of its name then places. This drawing's P holding an INSERT of M, and the
other drawing's A a line and M an INSERT of P, the merge is refused at M and leaves A and an empty M. A block AutoCAD
